GitHub auto-populates this list from the child issues linked to this epic.

issues.title: Define PunchProgram, ProgramRound, PunchCue domain types
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M24. Establish the Puncheokie program shape in the domain layer per §13.4 so downstream engine and UI code have a single source of truth. Lives under src/domain/programs/ per §16 and must not import RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE (§15.1).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/domain/programs/PunchProgram.ts` exports `PunchProgram`, `ProgramRound`, and `PunchCue` matching the interfaces in §13.4 verbatim (fields, optionality, and unions).
- [ ] `stance` on cues is the union `'inherit' | 'regular' | 'switch'`; program `defaultStance` is `'regular' | 'switch'`.
- [ ] `sequence: number[]` values are validated to be in 1..6 by a `validateProgram(p)` helper that returns typed errors, not throws.
- [ ] `targetVelocityZone` is the numeric literal union `1 | 2 | 3 | 4`.
- [ ] Module has zero runtime imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, or `react-native-ble-plx`.

## Non-goals

- No persistence, no editor UI, no cue matching logic.

## Notes

See §13.4 example program fragment for Three-Round Fundamentals. Related files: src/domain/programs/ProgramEngine.ts (later), src/storage/repositories/ProgramRepository.ts (M24-03).

issues.title: Add SQLite migration for punch_programs, program_rounds, punch_cues, cue_results
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M24. Persistence for Puncheokie authoring and scoring per §17.1. Migration lives under src/storage/migrations/ per §16. Also stores the decoder/capability snapshot per cue result so future decoder improvements can recalculate scores (§13.6).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New migration file creates `punch_programs` (id, name, description, version, default_stance, created_at, updated_at).
- [ ] Creates `program_rounds` (id, program_id FK, order_index, work_duration_ms, rest_after_ms).
- [ ] Creates `punch_cues` (id, round_id FK, start_offset_ms, duration_ms, stance, sequence_json, repeat, target_velocity_zone nullable, grace_before_ms, grace_after_ms, instruction nullable).
- [ ] Creates `cue_results` with columns listed in §17.1 (session_id, cue_id, expected_count, observed_count, correct_hand_count, correct_type_count, extra_count, average_velocity, completion_score) plus `decoder_version TEXT NOT NULL` and `capability_tier TEXT NOT NULL` for recalculation per §13.6.
- [ ] All FKs `ON DELETE CASCADE` from program → rounds → cues; `cue_results` references `sessions.id` and `punch_cues.id`.
- [ ] Indexes on `program_rounds.program_id`, `punch_cues.round_id`, `cue_results.session_id`.
- [ ] Migration runs forward cleanly on a fresh install and on a DB already migrated through Phase 4.

## Non-goals

- No seed data (see M24-04). No repository code (see M24-03).

## Notes

Sequence is stored as JSON text of `number[]`. Keep column names snake_case per existing tables.

issues.title: Implement ProgramRepository CRUD
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M24. Bridges domain PunchProgram objects (§13.4) to the SQLite tables added in M24-02. Per §16 lives at src/storage/repositories/ProgramRepository.ts. Domain layer stays unaware of SQLite (§15.1); repository handles JSON encoding of `sequence` and stance strings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `listPrograms()`, `getProgram(id)`, `upsertProgram(p)`, `deleteProgram(id)` are exported and typed against domain types from M24-01.
- [ ] `getProgram` returns a fully hydrated program with rounds ordered by `order_index` and cues ordered by `start_offset_ms`.
- [ ] `upsertProgram` writes program + rounds + cues in a single transaction; deleting removed rounds/cues cascades.
- [ ] `version` and `updatedAt` are bumped by the repository on every upsert.
- [ ] Unit tests using an in-memory SQLite adapter cover round-trip encode/decode, add/remove of a cue, and cascade delete.

## Non-goals

- No editor UI. No cue-result reads/writes (owned by matcher in M26).

## Notes

Mirror the shape used by SessionRepository / DeviceRepository from earlier phases.

issues.title: Seed Three-Round Fundamentals program
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M24. Ship a canonical starter program so first-run users have something to try. Uses the example in §13.4 as the source of truth for the first cues; extended to three rounds per the program name. Owned by storage per the phase rule that schema/seed lives in the storage area.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A seed function inserts a program named exactly `Three-Round Fundamentals` on first launch if no program with that name exists.
- [ ] `defaultStance` is `regular`; contains three rounds, each with `workDurationMs: 180000` and `restAfterMs: 60000`.
- [ ] Round 1 begins with the two cues shown verbatim in §13.4 (1-2 x3 for 8000 ms starting at 0; switch 1-2-3 x2 for 10000 ms starting at 8000).
- [ ] Seed is idempotent — re-running does not duplicate the program or its rows.
- [ ] Seed is exercised by an integration test that loads via `ProgramRepository.getProgram` and asserts the round/cue counts and the first two cues match §13.4.

## Non-goals

- No UI to reset or re-seed from settings.

## Notes

Cue content for rounds 2 and 3 can be simple variations (e.g. 1-2-3-2, 1-2-5-2) at the implementer's discretion; document choices in a header comment.

issues.title: Build basic program editor
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M24. Minimal editor so a user can create/edit a Puncheokie program end-to-end per §13.4 and §22 Phase 5 task 2. Screen lives under src/app/ (Expo Router) and composes domain types from M24-01 through ProgramRepository (M24-03). On the phase DoD critical path (user must be able to author a sequence workout).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Program list screen shows all programs from `listPrograms()` with name and round count and links to the editor.
- [ ] Editor lets the user set program name, description, default stance (regular/switch), and add/remove/reorder rounds.
- [ ] Round editor lets the user set work and rest durations (ms) and add/remove/reorder cues.
- [ ] Cue editor lets the user set `sequence` (numbers 1-6 picker), `repeat`, `stance` (inherit/regular/switch), `startOffsetMs`, `durationMs`, and optional `targetVelocityZone`, `graceBeforeMs`, `graceAfterMs`, `instruction`.
- [ ] Save calls `upsertProgram`; validation errors from `validateProgram` are shown inline and prevent save.
- [ ] Duplicating and deleting a program work from the list screen.

## Non-goals

- No drag-to-reorder gestures required (up/down buttons acceptable). No sharing/import/export.

## Notes

Keep the editor stance-agnostic — numbering is lead/rear (§13.2); the runner will resolve to left/right at run time.

issues.title: Implement StanceMapper for lead/rear to left/right resolution
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M25 (doc §27 step 1; retained in the v0.2 supersession). `StanceMapper` is the single source of truth for turning lead/rear punch numbers into physical hands. Vocabulary is D2: `Stance = 'orthodox' | 'southpaw'` (the recipe's `defaultStance`); `BlockStance = 'inherit' | 'orthodox' | 'southpaw' | 'switch'` — `switch` is the opposite of the default, absolute values override it, and "regular" is retired. M32-03 calls it to fill every `CueInstance.expectedPunches`; with hand-only or hand+broad-type data (FightCamp v1, H11) this mapping is the ground truth behind the **hand-sequence match** label (§13.3). On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §2 (lead/rear numbering: 1/3/5 lead, 2/4/6 rear), §11 (stance, hand hints, switch at reset points only), §3 (capability table).
- Spec §13.2 (mapping matrix), §13.3 (hand-sequence match rule), §15.1 (pure domain).
- Related: M31-01, M32-03, #127, #130.

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/StanceMapper.ts` — mapper (new).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/StanceMapper.test.ts` — smoke tests (#127 owns the exhaustive matrix).

### Interfaces
```ts
import type { PunchNumber, Stance, BlockStance, WorkoutToken } from '../workout/WorkoutTokens' // M31-01
export interface ExpectedPunch {
  tokenIndex: number
  number: PunchNumber
  hand: 'left' | 'right'
  body: boolean   // D10: display/scoring metadata only — never changes the hand
}
export function resolveHand(number: PunchNumber, effectiveStance: Stance): 'left' | 'right'
export function resolveEffectiveStance(blockStance: BlockStance, defaultStance: Stance): Stance
export function resolveSequence(tokens: WorkoutToken[], effectiveStance: Stance): ExpectedPunch[]
```

### Algorithm
1. `resolveHand`: orthodox → 1/3/5 `left`, 2/4/6 `right`; southpaw is the exact inverse.
2. `resolveEffectiveStance`: `'inherit'` → `defaultStance`; absolute values → themselves; `'switch'` → the opposite of `defaultStance` (so switch of southpaw = orthodox).
3. `resolveSequence`: each punch token yields one `ExpectedPunch` via `resolveHand`; the `b` body modifier copies onto `body` and **never changes the hand** (D10); defense/footwork/coach tokens are display-only and yield no `ExpectedPunch` (D4).
4. **Invariants:** pure, deterministic, no wall time, no I/O.

### Data flow
M32-03 `expandTimeline` resolves each block's effective stance, then `resolveSequence` fills `CueInstance.expectedPunches`; #130 compares those hands against `TrackerPunchEvent.hand` (from the connection slot per H11).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `Stance` and `BlockStance` unions match D2 verbatim; the string `regular` appears nowhere in the module.
- [ ] Orthodox: 1/3/5 → `left`, 2/4/6 → `right`; southpaw inverts every row (§13.2).
- [ ] `resolveEffectiveStance('switch', 'southpaw')` returns `'orthodox'`; absolute block stances override the default; `'inherit'` passes it through.
- [ ] `resolveSequence` on `1-2b-3` in orthodox returns left-right-left with `body: true` only on the second punch — `b` never flips the hand (D10).
- [ ] Display-only tokens yield no `ExpectedPunch` (D4).
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, `src/ble/**` (§15.1); no velocity labels of any kind in this module (§4.3).

## Test plan
- Unit: `StanceMapper.test.ts` — one happy-path case per export; #127 (M25-02) owns the exhaustive matrix.

## Non-goals
- Timeline and window math (M32-03); matching (#130); scoring and labels (#131); UI hand hints (M32-06).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-01 (`PunchNumber`, `Stance`, `BlockStance`, `WorkoutToken`).
- Unblocks: #127 (M25-02), M32-03, #130 (M26-01).

## Notes
- Rewritten 2026-08-23 for Puncheokie v0.2 (docs/puncheokie-ux-workout-engine.md); original body superseded.
- Decisions (do not re-litigate): D2 stance vocabulary; D10 `b` semantics; numbered roles stay lead/rear.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: StanceMapper unit tests: orthodox and southpaw x switch
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M25 (retained in the v0.2 supersession). Exhaustive, table-driven coverage of the StanceMapper (#126) so a regression never silently inverts a hand assignment — with hand-only or hand+broad-type tracker data (FightCamp v1, H11) the mapping is the ground truth behind every **hand-sequence match** score (§13.3). Vocabulary is D2: `Stance = 'orthodox' | 'southpaw'`, `BlockStance = 'inherit' | 'orthodox' | 'southpaw' | 'switch'` (`switch` = opposite of the default); "regular" is retired.

## Design references

- Doc §2 (numbering table), §11 (hand hints reverse under switch; numbering unchanged), §3 (what hand-level data can validate).
- Spec §13.2 (mapping matrix), §13.3 (hand-sequence match label), §21.1 (pure domain functions get unit tests), §15.1.
- Related: #126 (implementation), M32-03 (consumer), #133 (M26-04 fixtures build on these expectations).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/StanceMapper.test.ts` — exhaustive matrix suite (extends the #126 smoke tests; no production files).

### Interfaces
```ts
// Consumed verbatim from #126 (M25-01) — this issue adds no exports:
resolveHand(number: PunchNumber, effectiveStance: Stance): 'left' | 'right'
resolveEffectiveStance(blockStance: BlockStance, defaultStance: Stance): Stance
resolveSequence(tokens: WorkoutToken[], effectiveStance: Stance): ExpectedPunch[]
```

### Algorithm
1. `resolveHand` matrix: `test.each` over all 12 rows (2 effective stances × numbers 1–6) asserting the §13.2 table — orthodox 1/3/5 `left`, 2/4/6 `right`; southpaw the exact inverse.
2. `resolveEffectiveStance` matrix: all 8 `BlockStance` × `defaultStance` combinations, including **switch of southpaw = orthodox** and switch of orthodox = southpaw; absolute values override; `'inherit'` passes through.
3. Inversion property: for every number, `resolveHand(n, 'southpaw') !== resolveHand(n, 'orthodox')`.
4. `resolveSequence` cases: `1-2-3` under both effective stances; `1-2b-3-2` asserting the `b` body modifier never changes the hand (D10); a token list with defense/footwork/coach tokens asserting they yield no `ExpectedPunch` (D4).

### Data flow
CI-only. Runs with the domain jest project, headless on Windows without hardware (§21.1), guarding every downstream consumer: M32-03 timelines, #130 matching, #131 labels.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Table-driven tests cover `resolveHand` for every number 1–6 under both `effectiveStance` values, matching §13.2 exactly.
- [ ] `resolveEffectiveStance` is asserted for all 8 `BlockStance` × `defaultStance` combinations, explicitly including switch-of-southpaw = orthodox.
- [ ] A property-style case asserts `switch` always yields the opposite hand set versus the same default stance.
- [ ] `resolveSequence([1,2,3])` hand arrays are asserted for both effective stances; the `1-2b-3-2` case shows `body: true` without a hand flip (D10).
- [ ] Display-only tokens produce no `ExpectedPunch` (D4); the string `regular` appears nowhere in the tests.
- [ ] Suite runs headless in CI with zero RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports (§15.1, §21.1); no velocity labels appear (§4.3).

## Test plan
- This issue is the test plan: `StanceMapper.test.ts`, named cases `resolveHand matrix`, `effective stance matrix`, `switch inversion`, `sequence resolution`, `body modifier`, `display-only tokens`.

## Non-goals
- Matching or window behavior (#130, #133); timeline expansion (M32-03); scoring labels (#131).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: #126 (M25-01 exports), M31-01 (token types).
- Unblocks: M32-03, #130 (M26-01), #133 (M26-04).

## Notes
- Rewritten 2026-08-23 for Puncheokie v0.2 (docs/puncheokie-ux-workout-engine.md); original body superseded.
- Decision (do not re-litigate): D2 stance vocabulary; these tests pin the mapping only — visible labels belong to #131/M33 surfaces.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement ProgramEngine cue timer and round state machine
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M25. Drives a program through countdown → work → rest → next round → complete, emitting cue-active windows for the matcher. Lives at src/domain/programs/ProgramEngine.ts (§16). Uses the monotonic time source per §18.3 and stays pure domain (§15.1); UI subscribes via a store in src/state/useProgramStore.ts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Engine states include `idle`, `countdown`, `work`, `rest`, `completed`; transitions are unit-tested with a fake clock.
- [ ] During `work`, the engine computes the current cue and next cue from `startOffsetMs` and `durationMs` and exposes them plus time remaining.
- [ ] Engine emits `cueWindowOpened` and `cueWindowClosed` events using `windowStart = cueStart - graceBefore` and `windowEnd = cueEnd + graceAfter` per §13.6.
- [ ] All cue/round timing derives from the monotonic clock source per §18.3 (no `Date.now()` for elapsed math); the clock is injected so tests can substitute a fake.
- [ ] Pause and resume preserve elapsed time correctly; abort transitions to `idle` without persisting partial results.
- [ ] Engine has no imports from RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: two cues back-to-back, cue with grace overlapping neighbor, pause during rest, abort mid-work.

## Non-goals

- No event-to-cue matching (M26-01). No UI. No persistence of cue results (M26-03).

## Notes

Related: SessionEngine (Phase 4) for the state-machine pattern to mirror.

issues.title: Build live Puncheokie cue screen with visual and haptic cues
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M25. Realizes §13.5 cue presentation on top of the ProgramEngine (M25-03) and StanceMapper (M25-01). Route lives under src/app/, composes components from src/components/ (RoundTimer, PunchSequenceCard). On the phase DoD critical path (user must be able to run the sequence workout).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Screen shows: current stance, current numbered sequence in large type, lead/rear or left/right hand hints, repeat count, time remaining in the cue, next cue preview, round timer, actual punch count for the cue, sequence-match status, and (when supported) velocity-zone status per §13.5.
- [ ] A haptic pulse fires at cue start; sequence chevrons advance visually per matched punch (data source stubbed until M26-01 lands).
- [ ] No app-generated audio is played; a comment references §13.5 policy-review gate for future audio work.
- [ ] Pause/resume/abort controls call into the ProgramEngine; UI reflects state transitions.
- [ ] Screen renders correctly at tablet size in landscape (per punchCraft conventions).

## Non-goals

- No Spotify integration (Phase 6). No scoring UI (M26-03).
- No app-generated audio cues, tones, count-ins, or TTS pending Spotify policy review (§13.5).

## Notes

Use expo-haptics; guard for devices without haptics.

issues.title: Implement CueMatcher event-to-cue matching with acceptance windows
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M26 (doc §27 step 8; retained in the v0.2 supersession). `CueMatcher` assigns `TrackerPunchEvent`s to the expected punches of one cue. v0.2 input change: it consumes `CueInstance.expectedPunches` (via #126/M32-03) and M32-03's **already-clamped** windows — `[start − graceBefore, end + graceAfter]` clamped to `[0, workDurationMs]` (§18.2) — never recomputing grace; the §13.6 invariants are unchanged. On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §6 (matching requirements), §21 (extras never dropped), §3 (capability table).
- Spec §13.6 (invariants), §13.3 (hand-sequence match), §15.1, §4.3.
- H11: hand from the connection slot, not the frame; the only type signal is the vendor `'power'` vs non-power flag; no sequence number — order by tracker timestamp when reliable, else receive time.
- Related: M32-03, M32-02, #126, #131, #133.

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/CueMatcher.ts` — matcher (new).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/CueMatcher.test.ts` — unit suite (#133 adds the fixture matrix).

### Interfaces
```ts
// CueInstance: M32-03; CapabilityTier: M32-02; TrackerPunchEvent: src/domain/punch
export type MatchOutcome = 'matched' | 'hand-mismatch' | 'type-mismatch'
export interface CueMatchResult {
  cueId: string
  assignments: { expectedIndex: number; eventId: string; outcome: MatchOutcome; offsetMs: number }[]
  missedExpectedIndexes: number[]
  extras: { eventId: string; eventTimeMs: number }[]   // never dropped (§13.6)
  capabilityTier: CapabilityTier
  decoderVersions: string[]
}
export class CueMatcher {
  constructor(tier: CapabilityTier)
  match(cue: CueInstance, events: TrackerPunchEvent[]): CueMatchResult
}
```

### Algorithm
1. Sort `events` by event time; **one event is assigned to at most one expected slot**, greedily to the earliest unfilled `ExpectedPunch` inside the clamped window.
2. `matched` vs `hand-mismatch` by hand; **hand mismatch ≠ type mismatch** — `type-mismatch` only when the decoder actually reported a type (tier ≥ `hand-broad-type`).
3. Events outside the window, or arriving once every slot is filled, become `extras` — visible, never merged away.
4. `recovered: true` events are assignable after reconnection when their tracker timestamp orders reliably (§13.6, H11).
5. **Invariant:** pure and deterministic; identical inputs give deep-equal results (recalculable, §13.6).

### Data flow
CueEngine (M32-04) emits `cue-window-opened/closed`; M33-02 calls `match` on window close → `scoreCue` (#131) → store/UI, then `cue_results` via M33-08.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `match` uses the M32-03 windows verbatim — no grace or clamp math in the matcher (§18.2).
- [ ] One event → at most one slot, in event-time order; an event valid for two overlapping cues goes to the earlier cue only (§13.6; #133 fixture 6).
- [ ] `hand-mismatch` ≠ `type-mismatch`; no `type-mismatch` at `hand-only`/`hand-timestamp` tiers.
- [ ] Extras always surface with event ids; recovered events with reliable timestamps are applied (H11).
- [ ] Velocity fields pass through unrelabeled — tracker-reported velocity only (§4.3).
- [ ] Zero RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports; no `Date.now()` (§15.1, §18.3).

## Test plan
- Unit: perfect run; hand mismatch; extras mid-cue; recovered late event; deterministic re-run equality. #133 owns the fixture matrix.

## Non-goals
- Score aggregation and labels (#131); live wiring and extras policy (M33-02); persistence (M33-08, M31-09).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M32-03 (`CueInstance` + windows), M32-02 (tier), #126 (`ExpectedPunch`), M31-01; M32-04 supplies the window lifecycle via M33-02.
- Unblocks: #131 (M26-02), #133 (M26-04), M33-02, M33-08.

## Notes
- Rewritten 2026-08-23 for Puncheokie v0.2 (docs/puncheokie-ux-workout-engine.md); original body superseded.
- Do not re-litigate: §13.6 invariants; FightCamp v1 tier is `hand-broad-type` (D4).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement capability-aware scoring with hand-sequence match label
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M26 (retained in the v0.2 supersession). Aggregates `CueMatchResult`s (#130) into per-cue scores using the tier and label from M32-02. The v0.2 label rule (D4): at `hand-broad-type` — the FightCamp v1 tier per H11 — the headline **stays `hand-sequence match`**; `technique match` only at `hand-distinct-type`. Broad-type agreement is a secondary metric with caveat text — the decoder's `'straight'`/`'uppercut'` families are working guesses; only the vendor `'power'` flag is confirmed (H11).

## Design references

- Doc §3 (capability table), §6 (scoring dimensions incl. timing-window % and target-zone %), §21 (capability honesty).
- Spec §13.3 (label rule), §13.6 (recalculable results), §4.3 (tracker-reported velocity only), §15.1.
- Related: M32-02, #130, M33-02, M33-08.

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/cueScoring.ts` — `scoreCue` (new).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/cueScoring.test.ts` (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
// CapabilityTier + sequenceScoreLabel: M32-02 capabilityTier.ts; CueMatchResult: #130 CueMatcher.ts
export interface CueScore {
  cueId: string
  label: ReturnType<typeof sequenceScoreLabel>  // 'technique match' only at 'hand-distinct-type'
  completionPct: number
  correctHandPct: number
  timingWindowPct: number
  broadTypeAgreementPct?: number   // secondary, caveated (D4)
  targetZonePct?: number           // only when velocity is available
  averageVelocity?: number         // tracker-reported velocity
  extraCount: number
  capabilityTier: CapabilityTier
  decoderVersions: string[]
  calculationVersion: string
}
export function scoreCue(result: CueMatchResult, tier: CapabilityTier): CueScore
```

### Algorithm
1. `label = sequenceScoreLabel(tier)` (M32-02); `technique match` only at `hand-distinct-type`, else `hand-sequence match`.
2. Percentages count scored expected punches only; display-only defense/footwork/coach tokens never enter a denominator (D4).
3. `broadTypeAgreementPct` only at tier ≥ `hand-broad-type`, always secondary, caveated: vendor type families are unverified.
4. Velocity dimensions only when the source reports velocity; otherwise omitted with a `capabilityGap` note.
5. **Invariant:** deterministic; stamped with tier + `decoderVersions` + `calculationVersion` for recalculation (§13.6).

### Data flow
M33-02 calls `scoreCue` per closed cue → store (the live badge shows the label) → M33-08 aggregates the summary and writes `cue_results` (`capability_tier`, `decoder_version`, `calculation_version`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At `hand-broad-type` the headline label is exactly `hand-sequence match` on every consuming surface; `technique match` only at `hand-distinct-type` (D4, §13.3).
- [ ] Every scored cue gets completion %, correct-hand %, timing-window %, and extra count; broad-type agreement only with typed data, secondary + caveat text.
- [ ] Target-zone % only when velocity is available; else field omitted + `capabilityGap` note, never a zero.
- [ ] `capabilityTier` comes from M32-02, recorded on every result (§13.6).
- [ ] Terminology guard passes: only "tracker-reported velocity"; `'power'` only as the quoted vendor `punchType` classification (§4.3).
- [ ] Pure domain: zero RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports (§15.1).

## Test plan
- Unit: one case per tier asserting the exact label; caveated broad-type branch; velocity supported/unsupported; display-only exclusion; determinism (deep-equal re-run).

## Non-goals
- Matching (#130); badge rendering (M33-02); summary aggregation and persistence (M33-08).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: #130 (M26-01 `CueMatchResult`), M32-02 (tier + `sequenceScoreLabel`).
- Unblocks: M33-02, M33-08, #133 (M26-04).

## Notes
- Rewritten 2026-08-23 for Puncheokie v0.2 (docs/puncheokie-ux-workout-engine.md); original body superseded.
- Do not re-litigate: D4 label scope (doc §6 dimensions are first-class).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Persist cue_results and render program summary screen
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M26. Closes the Puncheokie loop by writing the scoring output to `cue_results` (§17.1) and presenting a completion summary that satisfies the phase Definition of done (capability-appropriate completion results). Repository under src/storage/repositories/, summary screen under src/app/. On the phase DoD critical path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On program completion the app writes one row to `cue_results` per cue with the exact columns listed in §17.1: `session_id`, `cue_id`, `expected_count`, `observed_count`, `correct_hand_count`, `correct_type_count`, `extra_count`, `average_velocity`, `completion_score`.
- [ ] Each `cue_results` row also records `decoder_version` and `capability_tier` (from the protocol adapter and M26-02 capability tier) so results can be recalculated later when decoders improve (§13.6).
- [ ] Writes occur inside a single transaction alongside the parent `sessions` row (mode = `puncheokie`).
- [ ] Summary screen shows total completion percentage, per-round breakdown, hand-match percentage, and — only when supported — technique-family/technique percentage and velocity-zone percentage per §13.6.
- [ ] Summary displays the capability-tier label from M26-02 verbatim (e.g. `hand-sequence match`); does not claim technique accuracy when only hand data is available (§13.3).
- [ ] Extra punches are visible in a dedicated section with count and timestamps (§13.6).
- [ ] Summary uses the §4.3 terminology (tracker-reported velocity only).

## Non-goals

- No Spotify metadata on the summary (Phase 6). No sharing/export.

## Notes

Store `session_id` on the summary route so history (Phase 4) can link forward.

issues.title: CueMatcher fixture tests for hand-only, hand+type, and recovered-event cases
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M26 (retained in the v0.2 supersession). Locks CueMatcher (#130) and scoring (#131) against representative event streams so decoder improvements never silently change results (§13.6). v0.2 changes: inputs are `CueInstance`s from M32-03 (expected punches + pre-clamped windows); fixture 5 uses the D2 vocabulary (`Stance`/`BlockStance`; "regular" retired); a new fixture covers a window clamped at round end (§18.2).

## Design references

- Doc §6 (matching requirements), §3/§21 (capability tiers; extras never dropped), §20 (windows inside work).
- Spec §13.3 (labels), §13.6 (invariants), §18.2 (clamping), §21.1 (fixtures run headless on Windows).
- H11: hand from the connection slot; vendor `'power'` vs non-power flag; epoch + 1/256 s timestamps; no sequence number.
- Related: #126/#127, M32-03, M32-02, #130, #131.

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/fixtures/cueMatching/*.ts` — typed fixtures: `CueInstance` + `TrackerPunchEvent[]` + expected results (new).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/CueMatcher.fixtures.test.ts` — runs every fixture through `match` + `scoreCue` (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
// Consumed verbatim (this issue adds no exports):
CueMatcher.match(cue: CueInstance, events: TrackerPunchEvent[]): CueMatchResult  // #130
scoreCue(result: CueMatchResult, tier: CapabilityTier): CueScore  // #131
sequenceScoreLabel(tier: CapabilityTier)  // M32-02
resolveEffectiveStance(blockStance: BlockStance, defaultStance: Stance): Stance  // #126
```

### Algorithm
Fixture matrix (each pins cue, events, tier, expected output):
1. Hand-only: 1-2-3, orthodox default → left-right-left matched; label exactly `hand-sequence match`; no broad-type metric.
2. Hand + broad type (FightCamp v1): same sequence with vendor `'power'`/non-power flags; headline **stays** `hand-sequence match`; broad-type agreement secondary + caveat (D4).
3. Extras remain visible: an extra mid-cue event appears in `extras`, never dropped; completion % unaffected (§13.6).
4. Recovered: a `recovered: true` event with a reliable tracker timestamp arrives late but inside grace → applied (H11).
5. Stance vocabulary (D2): `defaultStance: 'southpaw'`, block stance `'switch'` → effective `'orthodox'` → expected hands for 1-2 are left-right.
6. One-slot invariant: a single event inside two overlapping windows is assigned to the earlier cue only.
7. Clamped window at round end (new): the cue's `graceAfter` would cross `workDurationMs`, so M32-03 delivers it clamped; an event past the boundary is never assigned, one just inside is (§18.2).

### Data flow
CI-only; fixtures double as golden inputs for M33-08's recalculation test; build events from `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/fixtures/` where available.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fixtures 1–7 pass with exact-label assertions: `hand-sequence match` at every tier below `hand-distinct-type` (D4, §13.3).
- [ ] Fixture 5 uses `Stance`/`BlockStance` values only; the string `regular` appears nowhere.
- [ ] The clamped-window fixture proves no acceptance beyond `workDurationMs` (§18.2).
- [ ] Every §13.6 invariant is asserted at least once (≤1 slot, event-time order, recovered, hand ≠ type, extras visible); a re-run yields deep-equal results.
- [ ] Runs headless in CI (§21.1); fixture comments label velocity as tracker-reported velocity (§4.3).
- [ ] Expected outputs are literal objects, not snapshots.

## Test plan
- This issue is the test plan; named cases mirror the fixture list, plus a determinism re-run case.

## Non-goals
- BLE integration (M33-01); live extras policy (M33-02); summary persistence (M33-08).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: #130, #131, #126, M32-03 (`CueInstance`), M32-02 (tier + label).
- Unblocks: M33-02, M33-08 (golden recalculation inputs).

## Notes
- Rewritten 2026-08-23 for Puncheokie v0.2 (docs/puncheokie-ux-workout-engine.md); original body superseded.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Define WorkoutToken, WorkoutBlock, ProgramRound, and GeneratedWorkout contracts
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M31 (doc §27 step 1). Lands the pure-TS contracts every other Phase 5 issue imports: the `WorkoutToken` union, `WorkoutBlock`, `ProgramRound`, `PunchProgram`, and `GeneratedWorkout` shapes plus the `b`-notation helpers. Root of the M31–M36 dependency graph; on the Phase 5 DoD critical path. Replaces the retired spec §13.4 `PunchProgram`/`ProgramRound`/`PunchCue` trio (supersession row C2).

## Design references

- Doc §2 — lead/rear numbering (1/3/5 lead, 2/4/6 rear); numbers are technique roles, never physical hands.
- Doc §4 — program/round/block structure and the Three-Round Fundamentals fragment.
- Doc §14 — the seven block kinds; doc §26 — `PunchNumber`, `Stance`, `WorkoutToken`, `GeneratedWorkout` contracts.
- Spec §13.2 — numbering model; spec §15.1 — domain purity.
- Related: M31-02, M31-03, M31-04, M31-05, M31-09, M32-03, M32-06, M33-03, M34-02, M35-01; #126 M25-01 (StanceMapper consumes `Stance`/`BlockStance`).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/WorkoutTokens.ts` — token, block, round types + `parseCombo`/`formatCombo` (new).
- `src/domain/workout/GeneratedWorkout.ts` — `PunchProgram`, `GeneratedWorkout`, `validateGeneratedWorkout` (new).
- `src/domain/workout/WorkoutRecipe.ts` — doc §26 `WorkoutRecipe` interface, type-only here; M31-04 finalizes (new).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/WorkoutTokens.test.ts`, `GeneratedWorkout.test.ts` (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export type PunchNumber = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6
export type Stance = 'orthodox' | 'southpaw'            // D2 — 'regular' is retired
export type BlockStance = 'inherit' | 'orthodox' | 'southpaw' | 'switch'
export type DefenseCommand = 'duck' | 'bob-weave' | 'slip' | 'roll' | 'pull'
export type FootworkCommand = 'pivot' | 'step-off' | 'circle' | 'cut-off-ring' | 'reset'
export type CoachCommand = 'double-up' | 'put-it-on-em' | 'touch-and-go' | 'breathe' | 'hands-up'
export type WorkoutToken =
  | { kind: 'punch'; number: PunchNumber; body: boolean; beatOffset: number; velocityZone?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 }
  | { kind: 'defense'; command: DefenseCommand; beatOffset: number }
  | { kind: 'footwork'; command: FootworkCommand; beatOffset: number }
  | { kind: 'coach'; command: CoachCommand; beatOffset: number }
export type BlockKind = 'exact-combo' | 'repeated-combo' | 'volume-burst' | 'defense-counter'
  | 'footwork-exit' | 'active-recovery' | 'open-pressure'
export interface WorkoutBlock {
  id: string; kind: BlockKind; startOffsetMs: number; durationMs: number; stance: BlockStance
  tokens: WorkoutToken[]; gapBeats: number              // D5 — post-window gap; never 'recovery'
  repeat?: number; targetPunches?: number; targetVelocityZone?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4
  graceBeforeMs?: number; graceAfterMs?: number; spokenPhrase?: string; instruction?: string
}
export interface ProgramRound {
  id: string; order: number; kind: 'warm-up' | 'round' | 'cooldown'; countsTowardGoal: boolean
  theme: string; workDurationMs: number; restAfterMs: number; targetPunches: number; blocks: WorkoutBlock[]
}
export interface PunchProgram {
  id: string; name: string; description?: string; version: number; defaultStance: Stance
  rounds: ProgramRound[]; generatorVersion?: string; seed?: string; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string
}
export interface GeneratedWorkout {
  id: string; recipe: WorkoutRecipe; schedule: ProgramRound[]; roundPunchTargets: number[]
  expectedTechniqueDistribution: Record<string, number>; estimatedActivePunchesPerMinute: number
  warnings: string[]
}
export interface WorkoutValidationError { code: string; path: string; message: string }
export function validateGeneratedWorkout(w: GeneratedWorkout): WorkoutValidationError[]
export function parseCombo(notation: string): WorkoutToken[]  // '1-2b-3-2' — b ⇒ body: true (D10)
export function formatCombo(tokens: WorkoutToken[]): string   // inverse; always lowercase 'b'
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. `parseCombo` splits on `-`: `<n>` → punch token (`b`/`B` suffix ⇒ `body: true`); defense/footwork command words (`slip`, `roll`, `pivot`, …) map to their tokens; anything else is a typed error. Emitted `beatOffset`s are the placeholder sequence 0, 1, 2, … — musical offsets are authored by templates (doc §17) or via M31-02.
2. `formatCombo` renders `<n>` with lowercase `b` suffix and command words, joined by `-`. **Round-trip law: `formatCombo(parseCombo(s))` equals lowercase-normalized `s`.**
3. `validateGeneratedWorkout` returns every violation, never throws: rounds ordered by `order`; `countsTowardGoal === false` iff `kind !== 'round'`; block `startOffsetMs + durationMs ≤ workDurationMs`; `beatOffset`s non-decreasing within a block; `roundPunchTargets.length ===` scored-round count; `repeat` only on `repeated-combo`.
4. **Invariants:** nothing here maps a number to a physical hand (StanceMapper, #126, owns that); the post-window gap field is `gapBeats` (D5 — spec §19.3 reserves BLE `recovering`).

### Data flow
Type-only imports from every M31–M36 issue; `parseCombo`/`formatCombo` used by samples (M31-05) and the combo library (M35-01); `validateGeneratedWorkout` gates samples (M31-05) and generator output (M35-03).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `Stance = 'orthodox' | 'southpaw'`, `BlockStance = 'inherit' | 'orthodox' | 'southpaw' | 'switch'`; the string `'regular'` appears nowhere (D2, spec §13.2).
- [ ] `WorkoutToken` matches doc §26 exactly, with `body: boolean` on punch tokens (D10); `BlockKind` covers the seven doc §14 kinds.
- [ ] `ProgramRound.kind: 'warm-up' | 'round' | 'cooldown'` with `countsTowardGoal` false exactly for warm-up/cooldown (doc §9).
- [ ] `WorkoutBlock.gapBeats` names the post-window gap; no identifier in `src/domain/workout/**` contains `recovery` except the `'active-recovery'` block kind (D5).
- [ ] `parseCombo('1-2b-3-2')` yields four punch tokens with `body` true only on the second; `B` accepted case-insensitively; `formatCombo` always emits lowercase `b` and round-trips (D10).
- [ ] `validateGeneratedWorkout` returns typed `WorkoutValidationError[]`, never throws, covering every Method step-3 rule.
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, `src/ble/**` under `src/domain/workout/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] Velocity is only ever "tracker-reported velocity" in "tracker units"; nothing labels it force/power/energy (spec §4.3).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `WorkoutTokens.test.ts` — table-driven parse/format: every command word, `b`/`B` handling, round-trip property, malformed inputs (`'1-2x'`, `''`, `'7'`) → typed errors.
- `GeneratedWorkout.test.ts` — a workout built from the doc §4 fragment passes; one fixture per violation class (block overrun, unordered rounds, wrong `countsTowardGoal`, bad `roundPunchTargets` length).

## Non-goals
- Beat→ms conversion (M31-02); schedules/goals (M31-03); recipe defaults/validation/summary (M31-04); samples (M31-05); stance→hand mapping (#126); timeline expansion (M32-03).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: none — this is the Phase 5 root.
- Unblocks: M31-02, M31-03, M31-04, M31-05, M31-09, M32-03, M32-06, M33-03, M34-02, M35-01.

## Notes
- D2, D5, D10 are settled — do not re-litigate stance values, `gapBeats`, or lowercase `b` serialization (the uppercase **B** badge is display-only, doc §13).
- `WorkoutRecipe.ts` lands type-only so `GeneratedWorkout.recipe` typechecks; M31-04 owns its behavior and must not rename fields.
- Existing `@domain/*` alias covers these paths — no tsconfig/jest changes.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement cadence profiles and beat-offset to millisecond conversion
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M31 (doc §27 step 1). Beats are the authoring unit for all cue timing; this issue lands the beat→millisecond conversion that timeline expansion (M32-03), sample authoring (M31-05), and the recipe summary (M31-04) build on. Per D3, BPM is a recipe parameter scheduled on the spec §18.3 monotonic clock — never derived from Spotify audio, Audio Features/Analysis, track metadata, microphone, or playback position. On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §17 — cadence profile table (Technical 80–90, Steady 95–110, Pressure 110–130, Sprint 130–150 BPM) and token beat offsets (`1-2-3-2` at 0 / 0.75 / 1.55 / 2.30 beats).
- Spec §14.6 — no audio analysis or beat sync; spec §18.3 — monotonic scheduling; spec §15.1 — domain purity.
- Related: M31-01 (`WorkoutToken.beatOffset`, `gapBeats`), M31-04, M31-05, M32-03, M33-05, M35-01.

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/cadence.ts` — profiles + conversion helpers (new).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/cadence.test.ts` (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export type CadenceProfileId = 'technical' | 'steady' | 'pressure' | 'sprint'
export interface CadenceProfile { id: CadenceProfileId; minBpm: number; maxBpm: number; nominalBpm: number }
export const CADENCE_PROFILES: Record<CadenceProfileId, CadenceProfile>
export function beatsToMs(beats: number, bpm: number): number
export function tokenOffsetsMs(tokens: WorkoutToken[], bpm: number): number[]
export function blockDurationMs(tokens: WorkoutToken[], gapBeats: number, bpm: number): number
export function clampToProfile(bpm: number, profile: CadenceProfile): number
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. `beatsToMs(beats, bpm) = beats * 60000 / bpm`. Returns fractional milliseconds; callers round only at the display/scheduling edge.
2. `tokenOffsetsMs` maps each token's `beatOffset` through `beatsToMs`, preserving order and length.
3. `blockDurationMs(tokens, gapBeats, bpm) = beatsToMs(maxBeatOffset(tokens) + gapBeats, bpm)` — the trailing `gapBeats` (D5 naming) belongs to the block, so back-to-back blocks never overlap.
4. `CADENCE_PROFILES` carries the doc §17 ranges verbatim; `nominalBpm` defaults (suggest 85 / 100 / 120 / 140) are implementation-chosen constants recorded in the completion comment. `clampToProfile` bounds adaptive adjustments (consumed by M33-05).
5. **Invariants:** every function is pure and total for `bpm > 0`; `blockDurationMs` is increasing in `gapBeats` and decreasing in `bpm`; no function reads a clock, audio API, or global state.

### Data flow
The recipe (M31-04) selects a `CadenceProfileId`; samples (M31-05) and the generator (M35-03) compute block durations here; timeline expansion (M32-03) converts every `beatOffset` to round-relative ms; PacingEngine (M33-05) uses `clampToProfile` for its ±10–15% per-round cadence bound.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `CADENCE_PROFILES` ranges match doc §17 exactly: technical 80–90, steady 95–110, pressure 110–130, sprint 130–150 BPM.
- [ ] `beatsToMs(1, 60) === 1000` and `beatsToMs(0.75, 120) === 375`; fractional results are not rounded inside the module.
- [ ] `tokenOffsetsMs` reproduces the doc §17 `1-2-3-2` example offsets (0 / 0.75 / 1.55 / 2.30 beats) at any BPM.
- [ ] `blockDurationMs(tokens, gapBeats, bpm)` includes the trailing `gapBeats` gap (D5) and satisfies both monotonicity invariants.
- [ ] No API accepts or reads audio data, track metadata, or playback position — BPM is a plain recipe-authored number (D3, spec §14.6, CLAUDE.md rule 8).
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, `src/ble/**` under `src/domain/workout/**`; no `Date.now()` (spec §15.1, §18.3).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

## Non-goals

issues.title: Implement roundSchedule and punchGoals: schedules, goal tiers, focus scaling
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M31 (doc §27 step 1). Lands the fixed 3:00/1:00 round schedules and the punch-goal tier matrix consumed by recipe defaults (M31-04), samples (M31-05), goal allocation (M33-06), and pacing (M33-05). The first release keeps the standard structure so generation and target math stay predictable (doc §9). On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §9 — schedule table, guided warm-up, cooldown, active work time; doc §10 — goal presets, tier matrix, implied rates, focus scaling, Extreme warning; doc §22 — pace formulas consume active seconds.
- Spec §8.1 — session types; spec §15.1 — domain purity.
- Related: M31-01 (`ProgramRound.kind`, `countsTowardGoal`), M31-04, M31-05, M33-05, M33-06, M35-02; #107 M20-01 (SessionEngine runs these intervals).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/roundSchedule.ts` — `buildRoundSchedule` + types (new).
- `src/domain/workout/punchGoals.ts` — `GOAL_TIERS`, `suggestGoal`, `impliedTargets`, `intensityLabel` (new).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/roundSchedule.test.ts`, `punchGoals.test.ts` (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export type WorkoutDurationMinutes = 20 | 30 | 40 | 60
export interface RoundScheduleEntry {
  kind: 'warm-up' | 'round' | 'cooldown'; workDurationMs: number; restAfterMs: number; countsTowardGoal: boolean
}
export interface RoundSchedule {
  durationMinutes: WorkoutDurationMinutes; entries: RoundScheduleEntry[]
  scoredRoundCount: number; activeSeconds: number
}
export function buildRoundSchedule(minutes: WorkoutDurationMinutes): RoundSchedule
export type IntensityTier = 'technique' | 'steady' | 'hard' | 'high-volume' | 'extreme'
export type WorkoutFocus = 'hands' | 'movement' | 'balanced'
export const GOAL_TIERS: Record<IntensityTier, Record<WorkoutDurationMinutes, number>>
export function suggestGoal(minutes: WorkoutDurationMinutes, tier: IntensityTier, focus: WorkoutFocus): number
export interface ImpliedTargets { perScoredRound: number; activePunchesPerMinute: number }
export function impliedTargets(goal: number, schedule: RoundSchedule): ImpliedTargets
export function intensityLabel(goal: number, minutes: WorkoutDurationMinutes):
  { tier: IntensityTier; label: string; warning?: string }
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. `buildRoundSchedule` reproduces the doc §9 table exactly:

| Selected duration | Default schedule | Active work time |
|---|---|---|
| 20 minutes | 5 × 3:00 rounds, 4 × 1:00 rests, 1:00 cooldown | 15 minutes |
| 30 minutes | 2:00 guided warm-up, 7 × 3:00 rounds, 6 × 1:00 rests, 1:00 cooldown | 21 minutes |
| 40 minutes | 10 × 3:00 rounds, 9 × 1:00 rests, 1:00 cooldown | 30 minutes |
| 60 minutes | 15 × 3:00 rounds, 14 × 1:00 rests, 1:00 cooldown | 45 minutes |

Warm-up and cooldown entries get `countsTowardGoal: false`; they map to `ProgramRound.kind` `'warm-up'`/`'cooldown'` (M31-01) and run as SessionEngine work intervals (#107). **`activeSeconds` counts scored rounds only:** 900 / 1260 / 1800 / 2700.

2. `GOAL_TIERS` is the doc §10 matrix verbatim:

| Intensity label | 20 min | 30 min | 40 min | 60 min |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Technique | 800 | 1,200 | 1,600 | 2,400 |
| Steady | 1,000 | 1,500 | 2,000 | 3,000 |
| Hard | 1,200 | 1,800 | 2,400 | 3,600 |
| High Volume | 1,500 | 2,250 | 3,000 | 4,500 |
| Extreme | 2,000 | 3,000 | 4,000 | 6,000 |

3. `suggestGoal`: hands = tier value; balanced ≈ 85–95% of it; movement ≈ 65–80% (doc §10). Pick fixed constants in those bands, round to a multiple of 50, record them in the completion comment.
4. `impliedTargets`: `perScoredRound = goal / scoredRoundCount`; `activePunchesPerMinute = goal / (activeSeconds / 60)`.
5. `intensityLabel` maps a goal to the nearest tier at that duration; the Extreme tier always carries a `warning` — a specialized high-volume target (doc §10, §25).

### Data flow
`GOAL_TIERS`/`suggestGoal` feed the Recipe screen goal control (M31-06); `impliedTargets` feeds `summarizeRecipe` (M31-04); `buildRoundSchedule` shapes samples (M31-05), round planning (M35-02), and `allocateRoundTargets` (M33-06); PacingEngine (M33-05) reads `activeSeconds`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `buildRoundSchedule` matches the doc §9 table for all four durations, including the 2:00 guided warm-up (30 min only) and the 1:00 cooldown, both `countsTowardGoal: false`.
- [ ] `activeSeconds` = 900 / 1260 / 1800 / 2700 for 20/30/40/60 minutes — the doc §9 "Active work time" column.
- [ ] `GOAL_TIERS` equals the doc §10 matrix cell-for-cell (e.g. `GOAL_TIERS['high-volume'][30] === 2250`).
- [ ] `suggestGoal` uses the tier value for hands and applies the doc §10 balanced (85–95%) and movement (65–80%) scaling with documented constants.
- [ ] `impliedTargets` reproduces the doc §10 20-minute rows: 800 → 160/round ≈ 53/min through 2000 → 400/round ≈ 133/min.
- [ ] `intensityLabel` returns a `warning` for the Extreme tier (doc §10; doc §25 "Label high-volume targets clearly").
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, `src/ble/**` (spec §15.1); goals are punch counts, never labeled force/power/energy (spec §4.3).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `roundSchedule.test.ts` — all four durations against the doc §9 table; entry ordering; `scoredRoundCount`; `activeSeconds`.
- `punchGoals.test.ts` — full-matrix table test; implied-rate vectors; property: `suggestGoal(m, t, 'movement') ≤ suggestGoal(m, t, 'balanced') ≤ GOAL_TIERS[t][m]`.

## Non-goals
- Per-round target allocation `allocateRoundTargets` (M33-06); pacing math (M33-05); goal UI (M31-06); user schedule overrides (excluded from the first release, doc §9).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-01 (`ProgramRound.kind`, `countsTowardGoal`).
- Unblocks: M31-04, M31-05, M33-05, M33-06, M35-02.

## Notes
- The 3:00/1:00 structure is fixed for this release (doc §9) — do not add override parameters.
- Warm-up/cooldown as `countsTowardGoal: false` work intervals is settled; #107 carries the SessionEngine comment.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Define WorkoutRecipe: defaults, conflict validation, and recipe summary text
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M31 (doc §27 step 1). The `WorkoutRecipe` is the single input to workout generation (M35-03) and the Recipe screen (M31-06): this issue finalizes the doc §26 contract, provides defaults, an explicit-conflict validator (doc §12 — never silently ignore a preference), and the summary text generator behind `RecipeSummaryCard`. On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §8 — primary/advanced controls and the Recipe Summary example ending in expected active pace.
- Doc §11 — stance modes and bias as generator weights (lead 58–68% band), not hard requirements.
- Doc §12 — enablement menu and the jab-disabled conflict example; doc §26 — `WorkoutRecipe` contract.
- Spec §15.1 — domain purity.
- Related: M31-01 (type-only `WorkoutRecipe.ts` landed there), M31-02 (`CadenceProfileId`), M31-03 (`suggestGoal`, `impliedTargets`), M31-06, M31-09, M35-02.

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/WorkoutRecipe.ts` — finalize the M31-01 type-only declaration; add `defaultRecipe` (modify).
- `src/domain/workout/recipeValidation.ts` — `validateRecipe` + conflict catalog (new).
- `src/domain/workout/recipeSummary.ts` — `summarizeRecipe` (new).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/recipeValidation.test.ts`, `recipeSummary.test.ts` (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export interface WorkoutRecipe {                      // doc §26 verbatim — field names binding
  durationMinutes: WorkoutDurationMinutes
  totalPunchGoal: number
  focus: WorkoutFocus
  defaultStance: Stance
  stanceMode: 'fixed' | 'switch-by-round' | 'switch-on-command'
  bias: 'balanced' | 'lead' | 'rear' | 'left' | 'right'
  enabledPunches: PunchNumber[]
  bodyShotPercent: number
  enabledDefense: DefenseCommand[]
  enabledFootwork: FootworkCommand[]
  enabledCoachCalls: CoachCommand[]
  maximumComboPunches: number
  defenseFrequency: 'off' | 'light' | 'moderate' | 'heavy'
  footworkFrequency: 'off' | 'light' | 'moderate' | 'heavy'
  cadenceProfile: CadenceProfileId
  voiceMode: 'off' | 'minimal' | 'standard' | 'full'
  adaptationMode: 'fixed' | 'adaptive' | 'goal-seeking'
  generatorVersion: string
  seed: string
}
export function defaultRecipe(): WorkoutRecipe
export interface RecipeConflict {
  code: string; fields: Array<keyof WorkoutRecipe>; severity: 'error' | 'warning'
  message: string; resolution: string
}
export function validateRecipe(recipe: WorkoutRecipe): RecipeConflict[]
export interface RecipeSummary { lines: string[]; expectedActivePace: number }
export function summarizeRecipe(recipe: WorkoutRecipe, schedule: RoundSchedule): RecipeSummary
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. `defaultRecipe()`: a clean, useful workout in under a minute (doc §8) — 20 min, Steady-tier goal via `suggestGoal`, balanced focus/bias, orthodox fixed stance, all six punches, steady cadence. Chosen defaults must validate with zero conflicts; record them in the completion comment.
2. `validateRecipe` conflict catalog (each with `code`, offending `fields`, `message`, `resolution`): (a) `enabledPunches` empty; (b) jab (1) disabled while bias/focus implies jab-led generation — the doc §12 example; (c) `defenseFrequency`/`footworkFrequency` ≠ `'off'` with the matching command list empty; (d) goal above the Extreme tier for the duration (warning); (e) goal unreachable given `maximumComboPunches` + focus versus the implied active pace (warning). **A conflict is always surfaced, never silently resolved** (doc §12).
3. `summarizeRecipe` emits the doc §8 line classes: duration · rounds · goal; focus/stance; estimated technique distribution (rough weights from enabled punches + bias until M35-03 refines); body/defense/footwork frequencies; adaptation + voice mode; final line `Expected active pace: N punches/minute` via `impliedTargets` (M31-03).

### Data flow
`useWorkoutStore` (M31-06) holds a `WorkoutRecipe` and re-runs `validateRecipe` + `summarizeRecipe` on every edit; M31-09 persists recipes to `workout_recipes`; M35-02/M35-03 consume the recipe as generator input.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `WorkoutRecipe` matches doc §26 field-for-field; names are binding for M31-06, M31-09, and M35-02.
- [ ] `defaultRecipe()` validates with zero conflicts and summarizes without placeholder text.
- [ ] Disabling the jab in a jab-led configuration returns an explicit `RecipeConflict` with a resolution hint — never silently ignored (doc §12).
- [ ] `defenseFrequency`/`footworkFrequency` ≠ `'off'` with an empty command list is a conflict (doc §12).
- [ ] A goal above the Extreme tier for the selected duration yields a warning-severity conflict (doc §10).
- [ ] `summarizeRecipe` covers every line class of the doc §8 example and ends with `Expected active pace: N punches/minute` computed via `impliedTargets` (M31-03).
- [ ] Summary and conflict text use "heavy punches"/"rear-hand punches" phrasing; velocity, where mentioned, is "tracker-reported velocity" and never labeled force/power/energy (spec §4.3).
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, `src/ble/**` under `src/domain/workout/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `recipeValidation.test.ts` — table-driven catalog: one fixture per conflict code, plus a clean default; property: `validateRecipe(defaultRecipe()).length === 0`.
- `recipeSummary.test.ts` — golden test shaped on the doc §8 example (30 min · 7 rounds · goal · pace line); pace values cross-checked against `impliedTargets`.

## Non-goals
- Recipe UI (M31-06) and advanced panel/enablement menus (M31-07 — which also adds `extraPunchPolicy` to this type); persistence (M31-09); generation (M35-02/M35-03); Surprise Me seeds (M35-06).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-01 (types + type-only `WorkoutRecipe.ts`), M31-02 (`CadenceProfileId`), M31-03 (`suggestGoal`, `impliedTargets`, tiers).
- Unblocks: M31-06, M31-09, M35-02.

## Notes
- `recipe_schema_version` starts at 1 (persisted by M31-08/M31-09); bump it on any field change after first persist.
- `cadenceProfile` is a profile id — BPM is authored, never derived from audio (D3); `seed`/`generatorVersion` are pass-through until M35-03 populates them.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen (defaults, conflict codes), and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Hand-author sample GeneratedWorkouts including Three-Round Fundamentals
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M31 (doc §27 step 1 — "Build the Workout Recipe screen with hard-coded sample programs"). Hand-authored `GeneratedWorkout`s let the Recipe screen (M31-06) and the live screen (M32-08) ship before the procedural generator (M35) exists, and they become the standing fixtures for the cue timeline and CueEngine suites. Supersedes #124 (M24-04, which seeded the retired program tables). On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §4 — the Three-Round Fundamentals fragment (orthodox, seed `fundamentals-2026-08-22`, round 1 "Jab and cross rhythm" with a repeated-combo and a defense-counter block).
- Doc §9 — schedules the samples must follow; doc §14 — block kinds to exercise; doc §16 — round themes ("Establish the jab", switch-stance fundamentals).
- Spec §13.4 — program structure origin (superseded shapes; the samples use the M31-01 replacements).
- Related: M31-01, M31-02, M31-03, M31-06 (sample picker), M32-08 (live screen runs `three-round-fundamentals`), M32-09.

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/samples/threeRoundFundamentals.ts` — sample 1 (new).
- `src/domain/workout/samples/establishTheJab20.ts` — sample 2 (new).
- `src/domain/workout/samples/switchByRound.ts` — sample 3 (new).
- `src/domain/workout/samples/index.ts` — `listSampleWorkouts`, `getSampleWorkout` (new).
- `src/domain/workout/samples/__tests__/samples.test.ts` (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export type SampleWorkoutKey = 'three-round-fundamentals' | 'establish-the-jab-20' | 'switch-by-round'
export interface SampleWorkout {
  key: SampleWorkoutKey; name: string; description: string; workout: GeneratedWorkout
}
export function listSampleWorkouts(): SampleWorkout[]
export function getSampleWorkout(key: SampleWorkoutKey): SampleWorkout
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. **`three-round-fundamentals`** — the doc §4 fragment realized: orthodox default stance, `generatorVersion: '1.0.0'`, `seed: 'fundamentals-2026-08-22'`; round 1 "Jab and cross rhythm" (3:00 work / 1:00 rest, target 210) opens with the `repeated-combo` 1-2 × 3 (`spokenPhrase: 'One, two. Three times.'`, beat offsets 0 / 0.75) followed by the `defense-counter` slip → 2-3-2 (offsets 0 / 1 / 1.75 / 2.5); author rounds 2–3 in the same style (e.g. hooks after straights; body-head transitions) so each scored round plausibly reaches its target.
2. **`establish-the-jab-20`** — 20-minute jab-establishment workout on `buildRoundSchedule(20)` (5 × 3:00, 4 × 1:00 rests, 1:00 cooldown): jab-led motifs (1 · 1-1 · 1-2 · 1-1-2), Steady-tier goal from `suggestGoal(20, 'steady', 'balanced')`.
3. **`switch-by-round`** — stance alternates per round (`stanceMode: 'switch-by-round'`) to exercise `BlockStance` and stance-change presentation (M32-06) and StanceMapper (#126/#127). **Stance never changes inside a combination — only at round boundaries** (doc §11).
4. All combos authored via `parseCombo` (D10 lowercase `b` notation where body shots appear) and all block/round durations computed with `beatsToMs`/`blockDurationMs` (M31-02) — no hand-typed millisecond literals.
5. Every sample must return zero errors from `validateGeneratedWorkout`, with `roundPunchTargets` consistent with each round's `targetPunches`.

### Data flow
`listSampleWorkouts()` feeds the Recipe screen "Start with a sample" list (M31-06); `getSampleWorkout('three-round-fundamentals')` is the workout M32-08 runs on the simulated source; the samples also serve as fixtures in M32-03/M32-09 tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `three-round-fundamentals` reproduces the doc §4 fragment: stance, seed, round-1 theme, the 1-2 × 3 `repeated-combo`, and the slip → 2-3-2 `defense-counter` with the doc's beat offsets.
- [ ] `establish-the-jab-20` sits on `buildRoundSchedule(20)` and at least 60% of its structured combos are jab-led (doc §15/§16 spirit).
- [ ] `switch-by-round` changes stance only at round boundaries; a test asserts no stance change occurs inside a block (doc §11).
- [ ] All three samples pass `validateGeneratedWorkout` with zero errors in CI.
- [ ] Durations derive from `beatsToMs`/`blockDurationMs` (M31-02); no bare ms literals for block or round lengths.
- [ ] `listSampleWorkouts()` returns exactly the three keys above — stable identifiers binding for M31-06.
- [ ] `spokenPhrase` strings speak numbers and commands only; nothing labels tracker-reported velocity as force/power/energy (spec §4.3).
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, `src/ble/**` under `src/domain/workout/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `samples.test.ts` — per-sample: `validateGeneratedWorkout` clean, schedule matches `buildRoundSchedule`, target sums match `roundPunchTargets`; snapshot of each token stream (these snapshots are the downstream fixtures); jab-share assertion for sample 2; stance-boundary property for sample 3.

## Non-goals
- Procedural generation and combo library (M35-01…M35-03); recipe screen wiring (M31-06); persistence of samples (they are code, not `workout_recipes` rows — M31-09/M36-01 handle saved recipes).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-01 (contracts, `parseCombo`), M31-02 (cadence helpers), M31-03 (`buildRoundSchedule`, `suggestGoal`).
- Unblocks: M31-06, M32-08.

## Notes
- Supersedes #124 — close-with-pointer handled by the landing plan's legacy disposition, not by this issue.
- Keep samples boring and correct: they are the reference data every cue-engine test leans on; cleverness belongs in M35.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen (targets, offsets), and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Build Workout Recipe screen with primary controls, summary card, and landing
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M31 (doc §27 step 1). The Workout Recipe screen is the first user-visible Puncheokie surface: primary controls, live conflict feedback, the pinned summary card, and "Start with a sample". It replaces the retired free-form program editor (supersedes #125, M24-05; spec §22 Phase 5 task 2 old form / route `editor.tsx`). The landing screen also gets the approved copy — the current paragraph still promises beat-synced scoring, which D3 forbids. On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §1 — core user flow; doc §8 — the seven primary control groups + Recipe Summary; doc §10 — goal presets, intensity labels, Extreme warning; doc §11 — stance/bias semantics (lead/rear bias default; physical left/right for rehab and asymmetry work).
- Spec §6 — Puncheokie routes (amended: `recipe.tsx`, `presets.tsx`); spec §13.1 — flow origin; spec §19.4 — text + icon, never color alone.
- Related: M31-04 (`validateRecipe`, `summarizeRecipe`), M31-05 (`listSampleWorkouts`), M31-07 (advanced panel), M35-06 (generator wiring), M36-01 (presets).

## Method

### Files
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/recipe.tsx` — Recipe screen (new).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/index.tsx` — landing copy + "Set up a workout" entry (modify).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/_layout.tsx` — stack registration for the tab (new).
- `src/state/useWorkoutStore.ts` — recipe slice (new).
- `src/components/workout/RecipeSummaryCard.tsx` — pinned summary + conflicts (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
// src/state/useWorkoutStore.ts (recipe slice; live slice arrives in M32-08)
export interface WorkoutStoreState {
  recipe: WorkoutRecipe
  conflicts: RecipeConflict[]
  summary: RecipeSummary
  selectedSampleKey?: SampleWorkoutKey
  setRecipe: (patch: Partial<WorkoutRecipe>) => void   // re-runs validateRecipe + summarizeRecipe
  selectSample: (key: SampleWorkoutKey | undefined) => void
  resetRecipe: () => void
}
export const useWorkoutStore: UseBoundStore<StoreApi<WorkoutStoreState>>

// src/components/workout/RecipeSummaryCard.tsx
export function RecipeSummaryCard(props: { summary: RecipeSummary; conflicts: RecipeConflict[] }): React.JSX.Element
```

### Behavior
1. Primary controls per doc §8: duration (20/30/40/60 segmented); punch goal (suggested via `suggestGoal`, tier presets from `GOAL_TIERS`, minus/plus stepper, plain-language intensity label, Extreme warning); focus (hands/movement/balanced); stance (Orthodox · Southpaw · Switch by round · Switch on command); bias (lead/rear default per doc §11, physical left/right with a rehab caption); Voice Coach mode picker (values stored only — speech lands in M34); plan behavior (fixed/adaptive/goal-seeking).
2. Every change dispatches `setRecipe`; the store re-runs `validateRecipe` + `summarizeRecipe` and `RecipeSummaryCard` (pinned at the bottom) re-renders. Conflicts render inline near the offending control and in the card — text + icon, never color alone (spec §19.4).
3. "Start with a sample" lists `listSampleWorkouts()`; selecting one shows its summary and primes Start. The Start action is disabled with a "live screen arrives in M32" caption until M32-08 lands.
4. Landing `index.tsx` replaces the beat-sync paragraph with the approved copy and keeps `TrackerBadgesRow`.
5. Dark theme via `@/theme/colors` only; store mirrors zustand patterns from `useTrackerStore` (exported selectors, minimal subscriptions).

### Data flow
Controls → `useWorkoutStore.setRecipe` → domain validation/summary (M31-04) → `RecipeSummaryCard`; sample selection → `selectedSampleKey` → later consumed by `useWorkoutRunner` (M32-08); persistence of named recipes arrives with M31-09/M36-01.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All seven doc §8 primary control groups render and mutate the recipe slice; the Advanced affordance is present but stubbed (M31-07 owns it).
- [ ] Goal control shows tier presets from `GOAL_TIERS`, the intensity label, and the Extreme warning (doc §10).
- [ ] `RecipeSummaryCard` updates on every control change and always shows `Expected active pace: N punches/minute` (doc §8).
- [ ] Conflicts from `validateRecipe` appear inline with text + icon, never color alone (doc §12, spec §19.4).
- [ ] "Start with a sample" lists the three M31-05 samples by name and key.
- [ ] The landing paragraph in `index.tsx` reads exactly (no apostrophes — `react/no-unescaped-entities`): "Puncheokie is the punch-along workout mode. Numbered combinations run on an independent workout clock: every cue, rest, and round is scheduled by punchCraft on the tablet, never by a song. You can optionally connect Spotify to listen to your own playlist in the background while you train, and an optional Voice Coach can speak the cues; when music is playing it stays off until you switch it on. Scoring uses the same tracker frames Velocity Lab shows raw and is labeled as a hand-sequence match."
- [ ] `grep -n "beat" src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/index.tsx` returns nothing; every scoring mention on these screens says **hand-sequence match** (D4).
- [ ] Store state is plain and serializable; no raw event arrays in global state (spec §15.3).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- Component tests (jest-expo + react-test-renderer): control → `setRecipe` patch mapping; conflict rendering for the jab-disabled fixture; summary recompute on duration change; sample list rendering; landing snapshot containing the approved copy.
- Manual: tablet pass in portrait — controls reachable, summary legible at arm's length.

## Non-goals
- Advanced panel and enablement menus (M31-07); generator + Surprise Me (M35-06); saved presets UI (M36-01); live screen and navigation into it (M32-08); any audio.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-04 (`WorkoutRecipe`, `validateRecipe`, `summarizeRecipe`), M31-05 (`listSampleWorkouts`).
- Unblocks: M31-07.

## Notes
- Supersedes #125 — the recipe + generator replace editable programs (plan C5); no free-form editor returns.
- The approved landing copy contains no apostrophes by design; keep printWidth 100 wrapping.
- `useWorkoutStore` is a new store file — follow `useTrackerStore` conventions (module-level helpers for non-React callers land with M32-08).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Add Recipe advanced panel with enablement menu and explicit recipe conflicts
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M31 (doc §27 step 1). Second half of the Recipe screen's progressive disclosure (doc §8): the Advanced Recipe panel with the doc §12 enablement menus, inline conflict feedback from `validateRecipe`, and the extra-punch policy. Not on the DoD critical path (P1) — the primary controls (M31-06) make a runnable workout without it.

## Design references

- Doc §8 — advanced control list and progressive disclosure; extra punches encouraged/neutral/discouraged.
- Doc §12 — menu grouping (Punches / Defense / Footwork / Coaching and pace calls), frequency bands, and the jab-disabled conflict example.
- Spec §19.4 — large targets, text + icon, never color alone.
- Related: M31-04 (`validateRecipe` catalog), M31-06 (host screen), M33-02 (consumes `extraPunchPolicy`), M35-06 (generator warnings surface here later).

## Method

### Files
- `src/components/workout/EnablementMenu.tsx` — grouped switches + frequency selectors (new).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/recipe.tsx` — mount the Advanced panel (modify).
- `src/domain/workout/WorkoutRecipe.ts` — add `extraPunchPolicy` (modify).
- `src/domain/workout/recipeValidation.ts` — extend the catalog for advanced fields (modify).
- `src/components/workout/__tests__/EnablementMenu.test.tsx` (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export type ExtraPunchPolicy = 'encouraged' | 'neutral' | 'discouraged'
// WorkoutRecipe gains: extraPunchPolicy: ExtraPunchPolicy   (default 'neutral'; consumed by M33-02)

export interface EnablementMenuProps {
  recipe: WorkoutRecipe
  conflicts: RecipeConflict[]
  onChange: (patch: Partial<WorkoutRecipe>) => void
}
export function EnablementMenu(props: EnablementMenuProps): React.JSX.Element
```

### Behavior
1. The Advanced panel is collapsed by default (doc §8); expanding never mutates values. Its open state lives in `useWorkoutStore`, not component state, so it survives in-tab navigation.
2. Menu groups per doc §12, large switches with short examples: **Punches** — Jab / 1 · Cross / 2 · Lead hook / 3 · Rear hook / 4 · Lead uppercut / 5 · Rear uppercut / 6 · Body variations (drives `bodyShotPercent` enablement); **Defense** — `duck`, `bob-weave`, `slip`, `roll`, `pull` with frequency Off / Light (≈2–3) / Moderate (≈5–8) / Heavy (≈9–14 calls per round); **Footwork** — `pivot`, `step-off`, `circle`, `cut-off-ring`, `reset` with the same frequency bands; **Coaching and pace calls** — `double-up`, `put-it-on-em`, `touch-and-go`, `breathe`, `hands-up`.
3. Remaining advanced controls: `bodyShotPercent` slider, `maximumComboPunches`, `cadenceProfile` picker, and the extra-punch policy (encouraged / neutral / discouraged).
4. Toggling a prerequisite off surfaces the matching `validateRecipe` conflict inline at the switch — message + resolution, text + icon (doc §12, spec §19.4). **A conflict is shown where it is caused, never silently ignored.**
5. Every change flows through `onChange` → `setRecipe` (M31-06 store); no local recipe copies.

### Data flow
`recipe.tsx` renders `EnablementMenu` with the store's recipe + conflicts; patches go through `setRecipe` → `validateRecipe`/`summarizeRecipe` recompute → inline badges and `RecipeSummaryCard` update together. `extraPunchPolicy` is read later by CueMatcher integration (M33-02) for extras handling.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Menu groups and command names match doc §12 exactly: `duck`, `bob-weave`, `slip`, `roll`, `pull`; `pivot`, `step-off`, `circle`, `cut-off-ring`, `reset`; `double-up`, `put-it-on-em`, `touch-and-go`, `breathe`, `hands-up`.
- [ ] Defense/footwork frequency options show the doc §12 calls-per-round ranges in their captions.
- [ ] Disabling the jab with a jab-led configuration shows the conflict inline at the Jab switch with resolution text — text + icon, never color alone (doc §12, spec §19.4).
- [ ] `extraPunchPolicy: 'encouraged' | 'neutral' | 'discouraged'` lands on `WorkoutRecipe` with default `'neutral'` (doc §8; binding for M33-02).
- [ ] The panel is collapsed by default and its open state persists in `useWorkoutStore` across in-tab navigation.
- [ ] Body-variations toggle gates `bodyShotPercent`; serialized combo notation stays lowercase `b` (D10) — the UI badge alone is uppercase **B** (doc §13).
- [ ] Disabled commands are reflected in the recipe arrays immediately and the summary card updates in the same interaction.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `EnablementMenu.test.tsx` — group/switch rendering from a recipe fixture; switch toggle → expected `Partial<WorkoutRecipe>` patch; conflict badge rendering for the jab fixture; frequency selector captions.
- `recipeValidation.test.ts` — extended cases for `extraPunchPolicy` default and body-variations gating.

## Non-goals
- Voice-related advanced settings — metric announcement frequency, command vocabulary style, visual lead time (M34-05); generator-shaping controls — combo complexity, velocity-zone emphasis (arrive with M35-06/M36-03 tuning); double-up variations beyond the coach call (M35-01 template tags).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-06 (host screen + store slice).
- Unblocks: M35-06.

## Notes
- `extraPunchPolicy` is the one sanctioned addition to the doc §26 recipe (doc §8 lists it); do not add other fields here — M35 owns generator-shaping inputs.
- Keep switches glove-friendly-sized per doc §25 even though this screen is pre-workout.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Add workouts migration: recipes, generated workouts, adaptations, cue results
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M31 (doc §27 step 1, persistence leg). Adds the four Puncheokie tables from the spec §17.1 amendment as a TS `Migration` appended to `MIGRATIONS`. Supersedes #122 (M24-02, which targeted the retired `punch_programs`/`program_rounds`/`punch_cues` trio). Per D8, `realized_tokens_json` is NOT NULL so recalculation always replays what actually happened, never the recipe. On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §16 — seed/replay determinism; doc §22 — adaptation decisions recorded with inputs + monotonic time; doc §24 — the summary reads these tables.
- Spec §8.6 — stored sessions recalculable; spec §17.1 (amended) — the table definitions below; spec §19.1 — reliability/durability.
- Related: #115 M22-01 (sessions migration — must precede this and follow the same TS pattern), M31-09 (repository), M33-07 (adaptation writes), M33-08 (cue-result writes + recalculation golden test).

## Method

### Files
- `src/storage/migrations/00N_workouts.ts` — the migration; N = next id after #115's sessions migration (new).
- `src/storage/migrations/001_initial.ts` — append the export to `MIGRATIONS` (modify).
- `src/storage/migrations/__tests__/workoutsMigration.test.ts` (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
// Follows the repo's TS Migration pattern from src/storage/migrations/001_initial.ts — NOT .sql files:
//   interface Migration { id: number; name: string; up: (db: SQLiteDatabase) => void }
export const MIGRATION_WORKOUTS: Migration   // { id: N, name: '00N_workouts', up(db) { db.execSync(...) } }
```

### Algorithm / state machine
Tables per the spec §17.1 amendment, created in one `up()`:
1. `workout_recipes` — `id` PK, `name`, `preset_key` nullable, `default_stance`, `params_json`, `recipe_schema_version`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.
2. `generated_workouts` — `id` PK, `recipe_id` → `workout_recipes`, `session_id` nullable → `sessions`, `generator_version`, `seed`, `params_snapshot_json`, `blocks_json`, `realized_tokens_json` **NOT NULL** (D8), `created_at`.
3. `workout_adaptations` — `id` PK, `generated_workout_id` → `generated_workouts`, `decided_at_monotonic_ms`, `boundary` CHECK IN ('block','rest','round'), `inputs_json`, `decision_json`.
4. `cue_results` — `session_id`, `generated_workout_id`, `block_id`, `token_index`, `expected_hand`, `expected_type` nullable, `observed_event_id` nullable, `outcome` CHECK IN ('matched','hand-mismatch','type-mismatch','missed','late','during-pause'), `offset_ms` nullable, `velocity_raw`/`velocity_calibrated`/`velocity_unit` nullable, `capability_tier`, `decoder_version`, `calculation_version`; PK (`session_id`, `generated_workout_id`, `block_id`, `token_index`); indexes on `session_id` and `generated_workout_id`.
5. **The v1.0 `punch_programs`, `program_rounds`, `punch_cues` tables are superseded and never created** (spec §17.1 note).
6. The existing runner provides per-migration transactions and `schema_migrations` bookkeeping — no runner changes.

### Data flow
`runMigrations` (called from `openDatabase()` in `src/storage/database.ts`) applies this after #115's sessions migration; M31-09's `WorkoutRepository` is the only reader/writer of these tables; M33-07 appends adaptations; M33-08 writes `cue_results` alongside the `sessions` row.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The migration is a TS `Migration` object appended to `MIGRATIONS` in `src/storage/migrations/001_initial.ts` — no `.sql` files anywhere.
- [ ] All four tables and columns match the spec §17.1 amendment exactly, including `realized_tokens_json NOT NULL` (D8, spec §8.6, §19.1).
- [ ] `outcome` and `boundary` are enforced with CHECK constraints; foreign keys are declared (`PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is already set in `database.ts`).
- [ ] `punch_programs`, `program_rounds`, and `punch_cues` are not created (superseded, spec §17.1).
- [ ] Applying the migration to an already-migrated database is a no-op via `schema_migrations` (runner idempotence test).
- [ ] Velocity columns store raw/calibrated values with an explicit `velocity_unit` — the schema never bakes in a physical-unit or force/power/energy label (spec §4.3).
- [ ] A comment is posted on #115: the sessions migration must follow the TS `Migration` pattern (not `.sql`) and carry `generated_workout_id` nullable in `sessions` per the §17.1 amendment (replacing `program_id`).
- [ ] No imports from `src/ble/**`, React, or `src/app/**` under `src/storage/**`; `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `workoutsMigration.test.ts` on an in-memory SQLite database: all four tables exist with the expected columns (`PRAGMA table_info`); re-running is a no-op; a bad `outcome`/`boundary` insert is rejected; `realized_tokens_json` NULL insert is rejected; FK violation on `generated_workouts.recipe_id` is rejected.

## Non-goals
- Repository CRUD and JSON mapping (M31-09); the `sessions` table itself (#115); adaptation/cue-result write paths (M33-07/M33-08); any data backfill (there is none — the old tables never existed).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: #115 M22-01 (`sessions` table for the `session_id` FK and migration-id ordering).
- Unblocks: M31-09.

## Notes
- If #115 has not merged when this starts, develop on a branch with the test db stubbing `sessions`, and fix the final migration id before merge — ids are never renumbered after landing.
- D8 is settled: the realized stream column is NOT NULL; recalculation replays the realized stream, never the recipe.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen (final migration id/name), and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement WorkoutRepository CRUD for recipes, workouts, adaptations, cue results
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M31 (doc §27 step 1, persistence leg). Storage-layer CRUD mapping the M31-01/M31-04 domain types onto the M31-08 tables, following the `DeviceRepository` conventions.
