Supersedes #123 (M24-03 ProgramRepository). Feeds goal-seeking persistence (M33-07), the summary screen's `cue_results` write + recalculation golden test (M33-08), and preset replay (M36-01). On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §16 — same recipe + generator version + seed reproduces the plan; the stored realized stream is what recalculation replays (D8).
- Doc §24 — summary reads workouts, adaptations, and cue results.
- Spec §15.1 — dependency direction: storage never imports UI or BLE; spec §15.4 — local persistence conventions.
- Related: `src/storage/repositories/DeviceRepository.ts` (pattern to follow), M31-08 (schema), M31-01/M31-04 (types), M33-07, M33-08, M36-01.

## Method

### Files
- `src/storage/repositories/WorkoutRepository.ts` — repository (new).
- `src/storage/repositories/__tests__/WorkoutRepository.test.ts` — in-memory SQLite suite (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export type CueOutcome = 'matched' | 'hand-mismatch' | 'type-mismatch' | 'missed' | 'late' | 'during-pause'
export type RealizedTokenStream = Array<{ blockId: string; tokens: WorkoutToken[] }>
export interface WorkoutRecipeRow {
  id: string; name: string; presetKey: string | null; recipe: WorkoutRecipe
  recipeSchemaVersion: number; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string
}
export interface CueResultRow {
  sessionId: string; generatedWorkoutId: string; blockId: string; tokenIndex: number
  expectedHand: 'left' | 'right'; expectedType: string | null; observedEventId: string | null
  outcome: CueOutcome; offsetMs: number | null
  velocityRaw: number | null; velocityCalibrated: number | null; velocityUnit: string | null
  capabilityTier: string; decoderVersion: string; calculationVersion: string
}
export interface AdaptationRecord {
  generatedWorkoutId: string; decidedAtMonotonicMs: number
  boundary: 'block' | 'rest' | 'round'; inputs: unknown; decision: unknown
}
export class WorkoutRepository {
  constructor(db: SQLiteDatabase)
  saveRecipe(name: string, recipe: WorkoutRecipe, presetKey?: string): WorkoutRecipeRow
  listRecipes(): WorkoutRecipeRow[]
  saveGeneratedWorkout(w: GeneratedWorkout, realized: RealizedTokenStream, sessionId?: string): void
  getWorkoutBySession(sessionId: string): { workout: GeneratedWorkout; realized: RealizedTokenStream } | null
  updateRealizedTokens(generatedWorkoutId: string, realized: RealizedTokenStream): void
  appendAdaptation(a: AdaptationRecord): void
  writeCueResults(rows: CueResultRow[]): void   // single transaction — all or nothing
}
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. JSON columns: `params_json = JSON.stringify(recipe)`; decode checks `recipe_schema_version` and surfaces unknown versions as typed errors — **a parse failure never silently returns null or discards the stored payload**.
2. `saveGeneratedWorkout` writes `params_snapshot_json` (recipe at generation time), `blocks_json` (schedule), and `realized_tokens_json`; before any adaptation the realized stream equals the planned expansion — the caller passes it explicitly, and an empty/missing stream is a typed error (`realized_tokens_json` NOT NULL, D8).
3. `writeCueResults` executes inside a SAVEPOINT-based transaction: any failing row rolls back the whole batch. Using a savepoint (not BEGIN) lets M33-08 compose it with the `sessions` row write in one outer transaction.
4. Conventions from `DeviceRepository`: sync prepared statements finalized in `finally`, `mapRow` snake→camel normalization, `@diagnostics/logger` events, `newId()`-style ids (no crypto polyfills). Timestamps: `created_at`/`updated_at` are wall-time ISO for display/export; ordering fields (`decided_at_monotonic_ms`) are monotonic ms only (spec §3.2, §18.3).

### Data flow
Recipe screen (M31-06 via a thin service) → `saveRecipe`/`listRecipes`; generator/runner → `saveGeneratedWorkout`; PacingEngine mutations (M33-07) → `appendAdaptation` + `updateRealizedTokens`; summary (M33-08) → `writeCueResults` then reads everything back for the recalculation golden test; presets/replay (M36-01) → `listRecipes` + stored seed/generator version.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `WorkoutRepository` follows the `DeviceRepository` pattern: sync statements finalized in `finally`, `mapRow`, `@diagnostics/logger` events.
- [ ] `saveRecipe`/`listRecipes` round-trip a `WorkoutRecipe` deep-equal through `params_json`, carrying `recipe_schema_version`.
- [ ] `saveGeneratedWorkout` rejects an empty or missing realized stream with a typed error (D8, spec §8.6).
- [ ] `getWorkoutBySession` returns workout + realized stream for a linked session, `null` otherwise.
- [ ] `appendAdaptation` stores `decided_at_monotonic_ms` and `boundary` exactly as given — monotonic time, never a `Date.now()` substitution (spec §18.3, §3.2).
- [ ] `writeCueResults` is atomic: a failing row leaves zero rows (proved by test), and the savepoint implementation composes inside an outer transaction (M33-08).
- [ ] Velocity fields pass through `velocityRaw`/`velocityCalibrated`/`velocityUnit` untouched — the repository never converts values or relabels tracker-reported velocity with a physical unit (spec §4.3).
- [ ] No imports from `src/ble/**`, React, or `src/app/**` under `src/storage/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `WorkoutRepository.test.ts` against in-memory SQLite — a dev-only adapter over `better-sqlite3` exposing the `execSync`/`prepareSync`/`getAllSync` subset the repositories use, so the suite runs on Windows CI without a device: migration + CRUD round-trips for all four tables; atomic-rollback case (one bad row in a 50-row `writeCueResults` batch); schema-version mismatch surfaces a typed error; FK violation rejected; `getWorkoutBySession` miss returns `null`.

## Non-goals
- Summary computation (`workoutSummary.ts`, M33-08); adaptation decision logic (M33-05/M33-07); preset UX (M36-01); sessions-table writes (#115/#117 own `sessions`/`session_metrics`).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-08 (tables), M31-01 (`GeneratedWorkout`, `WorkoutToken`), M31-04 (`WorkoutRecipe`).
- Unblocks: M33-07, M33-08, M36-01.

## Notes
- The in-memory test adapter is a test utility, not a production dependency — expo-sqlite remains the only runtime driver.
- Method names here are binding for M33-07/M33-08/M36-01; deviations must be recorded.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Add PunchEventSource port and SimulatedPunchSource with scripted and tap input
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M32 (doc §27 step 2). This is the port that lets the whole Puncheokie live stack — CueEngine (M32-04), the landscape live screen (M32-08), and later CueMatcher — be built and CI-tested against simulated punches before the tracker stream is wired in (M33-01). `PunchEventSource` is the seam: `SimulatedPunchSource` (this issue) and `TrackerPunchEventSource` (M33-01) implement the same contract, so swapping sources changes no consumer code. On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §27 step 2 — build the live screen against a simulated punch-event stream before BLE protocol work completes.
- Spec §12.5 — the normalized `TrackerPunchEvent` contract the source must emit; `'power'` appears only as a `punchType` classification.
- Spec §28 — future sources (other trackers, replay) plug in behind the same normalized event shape; the port must not leak FightCamp specifics.
- Spec §21.1 — pure-TS harness must run on Windows CI without Bluetooth hardware.
- Related: M32-08 (SimControls UI), M33-01 (tracker implementation of the port), M32-02 (capability tier reads `capability`).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/punch/PunchEventSource.ts` — the port + capability descriptor (new, pure TS).
- `src/simulation/SimulatedPunchSource.ts` — scripted/tap implementation (new, pure TS).
- `src/simulation/scripts.ts` — the script catalogue (new).
- `src/simulation/__tests__/SimulatedPunchSource.test.ts` — see Test plan.

### Interfaces
```ts
export interface PunchEventSourceCapability {
  hand: boolean; timestamp: boolean; punchType: 'none' | 'broad' | 'distinct'; velocity: boolean
}
export interface PunchEventSource {
  readonly id: string
  readonly capability: PunchEventSourceCapability
  subscribe(listener: (event: TrackerPunchEvent) => void): () => void
  start(): void
  stop(): void
}
export type SimScriptId = 'alternating-1-2' | 'combo-1-2-3-2' | 'burst'
export interface ScriptStep { hand: 'left' | 'right'; offsetMs: number; punchType?: PunchType; velocityRaw?: number }
export const SIM_SCRIPTS: Record<SimScriptId, ScriptStep[]>
export interface SimOptions {
  clock: MonotonicClock
  script?: SimScriptId
  loop?: boolean
  latencyMs?: number   // fixed delivery delay, default 0
  jitterMs?: number    // uniform ±jitter added to latencyMs, default 0
  dropRate?: number    // 0..1 probability an event is dropped, default 0
  velocity?: boolean   // emit velocityRaw with velocityUnit: 'tracker-unit'
  seed?: string        // deterministic jitter/drop stream for tests
}
export class SimulatedPunchSource implements PunchEventSource {
  constructor(opts: SimOptions)
  emitTap(hand: 'left' | 'right'): void
  playScript(id: SimScriptId, bpm?: number): void
}
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. `start()` arms the source; `playScript` schedules each `ScriptStep` at `stepOffset + latencyMs ± jitterMs` on the injected `MonotonicClock`; `stop()` cancels all pending emissions.
2. Every emission builds a complete `TrackerPunchEvent`: `deviceId` `sim-left`/`sim-right`, `hand` from the step, `decoderId: 'simulated'`, `recovered: false`, `receivedMonotonicTimeMs` from the clock, fresh `id`/`sourceFrameId`. When `velocity` is on, `velocityRaw` is set and `velocityUnit` is `'tracker-unit'`; otherwise `velocityUnit: 'unknown'` and no velocity fields.
3. Scripts: `alternating-1-2` — steady left/right jab-cross alternation; `combo-1-2-3-2` — a four-punch L-R-L-R combination with doc §17-style uneven beat offsets; `burst` — a high-density flurry (~6 punches/s) for stress and §19.2 budget testing.
4. Jitter and drop draw from a PRNG seeded by `seed` — a given seed always yields the same delivered event sequence.
5. **Invariants:** emitted events are valid spec §12.5 `TrackerPunchEvent`s; delivery order is monotonic in `receivedMonotonicTimeMs`; no timers or `Date.now()` — all time flows from the injected clock.

### Data flow
`useWorkoutRunner` (M32-08) constructs the source, subscribes, and forwards events into counts; `SimControls` (M32-08) calls `emitTap`/`playScript`. M32-02 reads `capability` to resolve the tier. M33-01 replaces the sim with `TrackerPunchEventSource` behind the identical port.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `PunchEventSource` lives in `src/domain/punch/PunchEventSource.ts` and is implementable by both the sim and `TrackerPunchEventSource` (M33-01) without change (doc §27 step 2, spec §28).
- [ ] Every emitted event is a fully populated `TrackerPunchEvent` (spec §12.5); simulated velocity always carries `velocityUnit: 'tracker-unit'`, never a physical unit or force/power/energy label (spec §4.3).
- [ ] `SIM_SCRIPTS` contains exactly `alternating-1-2`, `combo-1-2-3-2`, `burst` with the hand sequences and densities described above.
- [ ] `latencyMs`, `jitterMs`, `dropRate` measurably shift/perturb/thin delivery; with a fixed `seed` the delivered sequence is deterministic.
- [ ] `emitTap(hand)` emits one event subject to the configured latency; unsubscribe stops delivery; `stop()` cancels pending emissions.
- [ ] `capability` truthfully describes the configured source (e.g. `velocity: false` sources never emit velocity fields).
- [ ] §15.1 purity: zero React/React Native/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports under `src/domain/punch/PunchEventSource.ts` and `src/simulation/**`; no `Date.now()`.
- [ ] Suite runs on Windows CI without Bluetooth hardware (spec §21.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `SimulatedPunchSource.test.ts` with a fake `MonotonicClock`: (a) `combo-1-2-3-2` delivers 4 events at the scripted offsets; (b) latency 80 ms shifts all deliveries by 80 ms; (c) jitter stays within ±bound and is identical across runs for one seed; (d) `dropRate: 0.5` with a seed drops a stable subset; (e) tap emits immediately (+latency); (f) unsubscribe/stop cases; (g) every event passes a `TrackerPunchEvent` shape assertion including `velocityUnit`.

## Non-goals
- The `SimControls` UI drawer (M32-08), the real tracker source (M33-01), capability-tier resolution (M32-02), any matching or scoring (#130/M33-02).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: none — `TrackerPunchEvent` already exists (`src/domain/punch/PunchEvent.ts`). If #111 M20-05 (`MonotonicClock`) has not merged yet, declare the clock parameter structurally and align the import when it lands.
- Unblocks: M32-08, M33-01.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): the sim is a first-class implementation of the port, not a test mock — it ships in dev builds and backs the live screen until M33-01.
- Pitfall: if a `@simulation/*` path alias is introduced, add it to both `tsconfig.json` and `jest.config.js`.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Resolve capability tier and sequence-score label from tracker capabilities
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M32 (groundwork for doc §27 steps 6 and 10). Puncheokie must never claim more than the connected tracker's data supports (doc §3). This issue delivers the single pure function that maps a punch-event source's capabilities to a `CapabilityTier`, plus the label rule every scoring surface must use (D4). CueMatcher (#130), the scoring readouts (#131), the MetricsRail (M32-07), and the tracker wiring (M33-01) all consume it, so it lands early and small.

## Design references

- Doc §3 — capability-aware scoring table: hand only / hand + timestamp / hand + broad type / hand + distinct type, with velocity as an orthogonal optional dimension.
- Doc §21 — tracker capability determines what can be scored; defense/footwork and body-vs-head are unscored.
- Spec §4.2 — unresolved hardware capabilities; claims must trail the evidence.
- Spec §13.3 — a hand-pattern score must be labeled hand-sequence match, never punch-technique accuracy, on every surface.
- Related: M32-01 (`PunchEventSourceCapability`), #130/#131 (consumers), M33-01 (resolves tier from observed events), `docs/protocol/hypotheses.md` H11.

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/capabilityTier.ts` — tier resolution + label (new, pure TS).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/capabilityTier.test.ts` — see Test plan.

### Interfaces
```ts
export type CapabilityTier = 'hand-only' | 'hand-timestamp' | 'hand-broad-type' | 'hand-distinct-type'
export interface ResolvedCapability { tier: CapabilityTier; velocityAvailable: boolean }
export function resolveCapabilityTier(
  input: { capability: PunchEventSourceCapability } | { observedEvents: TrackerPunchEvent[] }
): ResolvedCapability
export function sequenceScoreLabel(tier: CapabilityTier): 'hand-sequence match' | 'technique match'
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. From a declared `capability` (M32-01): `punchType: 'distinct'` → `hand-distinct-type`; `'broad'` → `hand-broad-type`; else `timestamp` → `hand-timestamp`; else `hand-only`. `velocityAvailable = capability.velocity`.
2. From `observedEvents` (M33-01 path): inspect the sample — `punchType` present on real punches promotes to broad; `trackerTimestampMs` present promotes to timestamp; `velocityRaw` with `velocityUnit: 'tracker-unit'` sets `velocityAvailable`. An empty sample resolves conservatively to `hand-only`.
3. **FightCamp v1 resolves to `hand-broad-type`**: per `docs/protocol/hypotheses.md` H11 the payload yields only a power/non-power flag (`Punch.b()` — type byte 1 or 2), a tracker epoch timestamp, and tracker-unit velocity; hand comes from the connection slot, and there is no sequence number. The decoder's `'straight'`/`'uppercut'` readings for other type bytes are working guesses and never promote the tier to `hand-distinct-type` (D4).
4. `sequenceScoreLabel` returns `hand-sequence match` for every tier except `hand-distinct-type`, which alone may say `technique match` (D4, spec §13.3). Any broad-type agreement figure is a secondary metric with caveat text, owned by #131.
5. **Invariant:** the tier limits what may be scored, never what is displayed — extra punches and unscored tokens stay visible regardless (doc §21).

### Data flow
M33-01 calls `resolveCapabilityTier` from the observed event stream and writes the result into the workout store; M32-07 hides velocity tiles on `velocityAvailable: false`; #130 selects its matching dimensions from `tier`; #131 and M33-08 stamp `capability_tier` into `cue_results` and pick their headline label via `sequenceScoreLabel`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `CapabilityTier` is exactly `'hand-only' | 'hand-timestamp' | 'hand-broad-type' | 'hand-distinct-type'` (doc §3).
- [ ] A FightCamp v1-shaped input (hand from slot, binary power/non-power `punchType` flag, tracker timestamp, tracker-unit velocity, no sequence number) resolves to `hand-broad-type` with `velocityAvailable: true` (`docs/protocol/hypotheses.md` H11, D4).
- [ ] `sequenceScoreLabel` returns `hand-sequence match` for `hand-only`, `hand-timestamp`, and `hand-broad-type`, and `technique match` only for `hand-distinct-type` (spec §13.3, D4).
- [ ] Empty or hand-only observed samples resolve conservatively to `hand-only`; capability is never inferred upward from absent fields (spec §4.2).
- [ ] Both input shapes (declared capability, observed events) are covered and agree for equivalent sources.
- [ ] §15.1 purity: zero React/React Native/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports in `src/domain/workout/capabilityTier.ts`.
- [ ] Velocity is referenced only as "tracker-reported velocity" / `velocityAvailable`; no force/power/energy labels (spec §4.3).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `capabilityTier.test.ts`: table-driven cases for all four tiers from declared capabilities; a FightCamp v1 fixture event sample (H11 shape) → `hand-broad-type` + `velocityAvailable: true`; hand-only sim source → `hand-only`, no velocity; empty sample → conservative default; `sequenceScoreLabel` over all four tiers.

## Non-goals
- Matching logic (#130), score aggregation and caveat text for broad-type agreement (#131), UI labels (M32-07 consumes the string), tracker stream wiring (M33-01).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: none (`TrackerPunchEvent` exists; `PunchEventSourceCapability` from M32-01 can be declared structurally if M32-01 has not merged).
- Unblocks: M32-07, M33-01, #130, #131.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): FightCamp v1 is `hand-broad-type`, and the sequence-score label at that tier — and at every tier except `hand-distinct-type` — is `hand-sequence match`, never technique accuracy (D4).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Expand GeneratedWorkout into a cue timeline with clamped acceptance windows
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M32 (doc §27 steps 3 and 5). `expandTimeline` turns a `GeneratedWorkout` (M31-01) plus the athlete's stance and cadence into the flat, fully timed `RoundTimeline[]`/`CueInstance[]` structure the CueEngine (M32-04) walks. All beat math, stance resolution, repeat expansion, and acceptance-window clamping happen here, once, at load — the engine and matcher then work in plain milliseconds. On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §6 — acceptance windows: `windowStart = cueStart − graceBefore`, `windowEnd = cueEnd + graceAfter`.
- Doc §14 — block kinds (exact-combo, repeated-combo, defense-counter, footwork-exit, active-recovery; volume-burst/open-pressure timeline support arrives in M33-06).
- Doc §17 — beat offsets per token; beats map to ms through the authored cadence only (D3).
- Doc §20 — the lifecycle consumes `previewAt`/`announceAt`/window fields computed here.
- Spec §13.6 — cue results must be recalculable; expansion is deterministic.
- Spec §18.2 — accepted events must fall inside the active work interval: windows are clamped, never spilling into rest/paused.
- Related: M31-01 (contracts), M31-02 (`beatsToMs`), #126 StanceMapper, M32-04 (consumer), M32-09 (test suite), #133 (fixtures).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/CueTimeline.ts` — `expandTimeline`, `CueInstance`, `RoundTimeline` (new, pure TS).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/CueTimeline.test.ts` — see Test plan.

### Interfaces
```ts
export interface ExpectedPunch { tokenIndex: number; hand: 'left' | 'right'; type?: PunchType }
export interface CueInstance {
  id: string
  blockId: string
  repeatIndex: number
  tokens: WorkoutToken[]
  tokenOffsetsMs: number[]
  expectedPunches: ExpectedPunch[]
  displayOnlyTokenIndexes: number[]
  previewAt: number
  announceAt: number
  scheduledStartMs: number
  scheduledEndMs: number
  windowStartMs: number
  windowEndMs: number
  spokenPhrase?: string
}
export interface RoundTimeline {
  roundIndex: number
  workDurationMs: number
  cues: CueInstance[]
  stanceChanges: { atMs: number; toStance: Stance }[]
}
export function expandTimeline(workout: GeneratedWorkout, defaultStance: Stance, bpm: number): RoundTimeline[]
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. For each `ProgramRound`, walk blocks in `startOffsetMs` order. Resolve the block's effective stance via `resolveEffectiveStance(block.stance, defaultStance)` (#126); emit a `stanceChanges` entry only when it differs from the previous block's — stance changes occur at reset points only, never inside a combination (doc §11).
2. Token beats → ms with M31-02 `beatsToMs(bpm)`; `scheduledEndMs = scheduledStartMs + last token offset + gapBeats·beatMs` (D5 naming: the post-combo gap timing field is `gapBeats`).
3. **Repeat expansion:** a block with `repeat: N` yields N `CueInstance`s sharing `blockId`, with `repeatIndex` 0…N−1, each re-based at `blockStartMs + repeatIndex × (comboDurationMs + gapBeats·beatMs)`.
4. **Clamping formula:** `windowStartMs = max(0, scheduledStartMs − graceBeforeMs)` and `windowEndMs = min(workDurationMs, scheduledEndMs + graceAfterMs)` — windows never precede the bell or outlive the round's work interval (doc §6, spec §18.2, D5).
5. `previewAt = scheduledStartMs − leadTimes.previewMs` and `announceAt = scheduledStartMs − leadTimes.announceMs`, floored at 0 (doc §18 lead times; defaults tuned in M36-03).
6. `expectedPunches`: punch tokens only — `hand` from `resolveHand(number, effectiveStance)` (#126); `type?` optionally carries the broad family implied by the number for tiers that can use it (#130 decides usage). Defense/footwork/coach tokens contribute no expected punch and are listed in `displayOnlyTokenIndexes` — display-only, unscored, excluded from completion (D4).
7. **Invariants:** cues within a round are sorted and non-overlapping in `[scheduledStartMs, scheduledEndMs]`; expansion is a pure deterministic function of `(workout, defaultStance, bpm)` (spec §13.6).

### Data flow
`useWorkoutRunner` (M32-08) calls `expandTimeline` once at workout start and hands the result to `new CueEngine(timeline, …)` (M32-04). CueMatcher (#130) reads `expectedPunches` and windows off the emitted `CueInstance`s. Nothing here touches the store or storage.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `expandTimeline` is deterministic: same `(workout, stance, bpm)` → deep-equal output (spec §13.6).
- [ ] Windows obey `windowStartMs = max(0, scheduledStartMs − graceBeforeMs)`, `windowEndMs = min(workDurationMs, scheduledEndMs + graceAfterMs)`; no window exceeds `[0, workDurationMs]` (doc §6, spec §18.2).
- [ ] `repeat: N` produces N instances with `repeatIndex` 0…N−1, re-based by combo duration plus `gapBeats` (doc §14, D5).
- [ ] `expectedPunches.hand` flips correctly between orthodox and southpaw via StanceMapper (#126); a `switch` block inverts the default stance (D2).
- [ ] Defense/footwork/coach tokens appear in `tokens` and `displayOnlyTokenIndexes` but never in `expectedPunches` (D4, doc §21).
- [ ] `stanceChanges` entries occur only at block boundaries, never mid-combination (doc §11).
- [ ] Token offsets use authored cadence via M31-02 only — no audio-derived timing anywhere (D3).
- [ ] §15.1 purity: zero React/React Native/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports and no `Date.now()` in `src/domain/programs/CueTimeline.ts`.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `CueTimeline.test.ts`: expand `Three-Round Fundamentals` (M31-05) and assert cue count, ordering, and windows; repeat re-basing; orthodox vs southpaw expected hands; window clamped at round end (`graceAfter` past the bell) and at round start; display-only token indexes; determinism (double-call deep equal). M32-09 adds the exhaustive/property suite; #133 curates shared fixtures.

## Non-goals
- Lifecycle execution (M32-04), volume-burst/open-pressure timeline support (M33-06), matching (#130/M33-02), pacing mutation of future rounds (M33-05/M33-07).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-01 (token/block/round contracts), M31-02 (`beatsToMs`), #126 M25-01 (`resolveHand`, `resolveEffectiveStance`).
- Unblocks: M32-04, M32-09, M33-05, M33-06, #130, #133.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): clamping happens here, not in the engine — M32-04 asserts the invariant on load and treats a violation as a programming error.
- `previewAt`/`announceAt` floor at 0 rather than widening the window: a cue right at the bell simply gets a shorter preview.
- The Interfaces block is imported verbatim by M32-04, #130, M33-05, and M33-06 — coordinate any rename before merging.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement CueEngine cue lifecycle composed with the SessionEngine state machine
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M32 (doc §27 step 3). The CueEngine walks a round's cue timeline (M32-03) and drives every cue through the doc §20 lifecycle, emitting the events consumed by the live screen (M32-08), CueMatcher (#130 via M33-02), CueAnnouncer (M34-03), and PacingEngine (M33-05). It does not own work/rest/pause — those belong to the §18.1 SessionEngine (#107); the CueEngine composes with it (D5). On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §20 (cue state machine + preserved timestamps), §18 timing example (T−1.50 s preview, T−0.75 voice, T−0.10 ready tone, tokens at +0.00/0.45/0.95/1.45, T+2.20 lock), §14 block kinds, §21 (no red flash; partial completion is not failure), §25 (immediate stop).
- Spec §18.1 (session states), §18.2 (accepted events fall inside work), §18.3 (monotonic time), §15.1 (no RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports), §19.3 (BLE "recovery" is reserved — the cue gap state is `gap`).
- Related: M32-03 CueTimeline, #130 CueMatcher, M34-03, M33-05, #107 M20-01, #109 M20-03, #111 M20-05.

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/CueEngine.ts` — engine (new).
- `src/domain/programs/CueState.ts` — `CueStatus`, `CueEvent`, `CueTimestamps`, `SessionPhaseEvent` (new).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/CueEngine.test.ts` — see Test plan (M32-09 extends).

### Interfaces
```ts
export type CueStatus = 'queued' | 'previewing' | 'announcing' | 'active' | 'accepting'
  | 'completed' | 'expired' | 'gap' | 'suspended' | 'cancelled'
export interface CueTimestamps {
  previewScheduledMs: number; previewActualMs?: number
  voiceScheduledMs: number; voiceActualMs?: number
  executionScheduledMs: number; executionActualMs?: number
  windowCloseMs: number; completedAtMs?: number
  trackerEventTimesMs: number[]; suspensions: { atMs: number; resumedAtMs?: number }[]
}
export type SessionPhaseEvent =
  | { type: 'work-entered'; roundIndex: number; nowMs: number }
  | { type: 'paused' | 'resumed' | 'rest-entered' | 'finishing' | 'cancelled'; nowMs: number }
export type CueEvent =
  | { type: 'cue-previewing' | 'cue-announcing' | 'cue-active' | 'cue-window-opened' | 'cue-window-closed'
      | 'cue-completed' | 'cue-expired' | 'cue-suspended' | 'cue-resumed' | 'cue-cancelled';
      cue: CueInstance; status: CueStatus; timestamps: CueTimestamps; workElapsedMs: number; nowMs: number }
  | { type: 'token-due'; cue: CueInstance; tokenIndex: number; workElapsedMs: number; nowMs: number }
export interface CueEngineOptions { leadTimes: { previewMs: number; announceMs: number; readyToneMs: number }; clock: MonotonicClock }
export class CueEngine {
  constructor(timeline: RoundTimeline[], opts: CueEngineOptions)
  onSessionPhase(e: SessionPhaseEvent): void
  tick(workElapsedMs: number): void               // from the session tick (20–60 Hz); idempotent per value
  notifyMatch(cueId: string, expectedIndex: number, eventTimeMs: number): void   // from CueMatcher
  skipCue(): void; repeatCue(): void; notifyTrackerFault(active: boolean): void
  subscribe(listener: (e: CueEvent) => void): () => void
  snapshot(): { current?: CueInstance; next?: CueInstance; status: CueStatus; remainingMs: number }
}
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. Time base: **all scheduling compares against `workElapsedMs`**, the SessionEngine's round work clock, frozen while `paused` (#107/#109). `clock.nowMs()` is written only into `*ActualMs` fields. A pause needs no offset shifting — the cue simply stops advancing.
2. `work-entered(roundIndex)` loads that round's `CueInstance[]` as `queued`.
3. Each `tick(t)`: head cue transitions when `t ≥ previewAt` → `previewing`, `t ≥ announceAt` → `announcing`, `t ≥ scheduledStartMs` → `active` (+ `cue-window-opened` once `t ≥ windowStartMs`); each token at `scheduledStartMs + offsetMs` emits `token-due`; after the last token → `accepting` until `windowCloseMs`; then `completed` if every scored expected punch was matched via `notifyMatch`, else `expired` with partial counts (not a failure, doc §21); then `gap` until the next cue's `previewAt`.
4. Lookahead: up to two cues may be `previewing` while one is `accepting`; **only one cue is `active|accepting` at a time**. Windows arrive clamped to `[0, workDurationMs]` from M32-03; the engine asserts this on load.
5. `paused` or `notifyTrackerFault(true)`: `announcing|active|accepting` → `suspended` (push a suspension record); `resumed`/fault cleared → prior status. `rest-entered|finishing|cancelled` → every remaining cue `cancelled`, emitted once each.
6. `skipCue` cancels the current cue and advances; `repeatCue` enqueues a copy with `repeatIndex + 1` re-based at the next gap.
7. **Invariants:** status moves forward except `suspended ↔ prior`; every event carries the full `CueTimestamps`; no wall time; no RN/Expo imports.

### Data flow
SessionEngine tick → `CueEngine.tick` → `CueEvent`s → `useWorkoutStore` (throttled ≤10 Hz for UI, spec §15.3), CueMatcher (`cue-window-opened/closed`), CueAnnouncer (`cue-previewing/announcing`, `token-due`). CueMatcher → `notifyMatch`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `CueStatus` union and transitions match doc §20 with `gap` replacing "recovery" (D5).
- [ ] Scheduling uses `workElapsedMs` only: holding it constant for 5 s while `clock.nowMs()` advances produces zero transitions.
- [ ] `paused` suspends `announcing|active|accepting` cues; `resumed` restores the same status with a suspension record appended.
- [ ] Engine asserts on load that no window extends beyond the round's work interval (spec §18.2).
- [ ] Every `CueEvent` carries scheduled timestamps set at load and actual timestamps set at emission.
- [ ] `token-due` fires exactly once per token in event-time order; `repeated-combo` instances carry `repeatIndex` 0..N−1.
- [ ] `rest-entered|finishing|cancelled` cancel all remaining cues exactly once (immediate stop, doc §25).
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, `src/ble/**`; no `Date.now()` under `src/domain/programs/**`.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `CueEngine.test.ts` with a fake `MonotonicClock` and scripted `tick()` values: (a) full status walk for one exact-combo and one repeated-combo cue; (b) pause mid-`accepting` → suspended → resumed; (c) window close with 2/3 matched → `expired` with partial counts; (d) `skipCue` then `repeatCue`; (e) `rest-entered` cancels remaining; (f) tracker fault suspends and clears; (g) property: emitted events are monotonic in `workElapsedMs`.
- M32-09 adds the exhaustive timeline/clamping suite.

## Non-goals
- Timeline expansion (M32-03), matching (#130/M33-02), voice (M34-03), pacing (M33-05), UI (M32-08).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M32-03 (`CueInstance`, `RoundTimeline`); #111 M20-05 (`MonotonicClock`); #107 M20-01 (transition events → `SessionPhaseEvent`; until merged, drive the engine in tests with hand-made events); #109 M20-03 (frozen work clock).
- Unblocks: M32-08, M32-09, M33-02, M34-03, M33-05.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): consume the session's frozen work clock instead of shifting offsets on resume.
- Default lead times `{ previewMs: 1500, announceMs: 750, readyToneMs: 100 }` from doc §18; tuned in M36-03.
- On completion, comment with: files added, any deviation from the Interfaces block (imported by M33-02/M34-03/M33-05), and the test count.

issues.title: Spike: landscape lock per route, keep-awake, and haptics on the Lenovo TB125FU
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M32 (enabler for doc §27 step 2). The Puncheokie live screen is landscape-first on the tablet — a deliberate, recorded inversion of spec §19.4's phone-first rule for this one route (D7). `app.config.ts` currently pins `orientation: 'portrait'`, and the mechanism (global `'default'` plus a per-route lock vs. anything else) has never been exercised in this app. Three native modules are implicated, and each requires a prebuild + dev-client rebuild on the locked Expo SDK 57. M32-08 builds directly on this spike's decision, so it runs early and in parallel with the domain work.

## Design references

- Doc §19 — the live screen "should preferably use landscape orientation on a tablet"; the four-zone layout assumes landscape width.
- Doc §25 — keep the screen awake during active rounds; glove-friendly controls; haptic pulses.
- Spec §11.2 — version lock: same Expo SDK 57, no upgrades; keep a known-good APK.
- Spec §19.4 — the phone-first rule this screen deviates from; the deviation is recorded as a spec §25 decision row (D7).
- Related: M32-08 (consumer of the decision), M34-01 (the parallel audio spike; batch the dev-client rebuild if both land the same day).

## Question

With `orientation: 'default'` in `app.config.ts`, can `expo-screen-orientation` lock `puncheokie/live` to landscape on focus and restore portrait on blur — without breaking expo-router navigation state or Zustand store state on rotation — and do `expo-keep-awake` and `expo-haptics` behave acceptably on the Lenovo TB125FU?

## Time box

1 day, on the tablet (hardware required — physical rotation, screen-timeout, and haptic behavior cannot be verified on the emulator).

## Method

1. Branch; change `app.config.ts` `orientation: 'portrait'` → `'default'`; add `expo-screen-orientation`, `expo-keep-awake`, `expo-haptics` at the SDK 57-pinned versions; `npm run prebuild` and `expo run:android --device` to rebuild the dev client (spec §11.2 — same locked SDK, no Expo upgrade).
2. Prototype a throwaway route that calls `ScreenOrientation.lockAsync(LANDSCAPE)` in a `useFocusEffect` and re-locks portrait (or unlocks) on blur. Compare against the alternative of a global orientation setting without per-route locking. Record which approach leaves every non-live route visually unchanged.
3. Rotate mid-session, background/foreground the app, and navigate away and back; confirm the expo-router stack and a test Zustand store survive without the Android activity recreation dropping state.
4. Verify `useKeepAwake()` holds past the tablet's screen timeout while the route is focused and releases on blur (doc §25).
5. Fire `expo-haptics` impact styles (Light/Medium/Heavy) at cue-tick cadence; record perceptibility on the TB125FU — tablets often have weak or absent vibration motors — and name the fallback (visual pulse only) if it is inert.

## Deliverable

- A decision comment on this issue: chosen orientation mechanism with a minimal code snippet, rotation/state findings, keep-awake and haptics findings, and the haptic fallback if needed.
- The `app.config.ts` + `package.json` config diff, committed on a branch M32-08 can stack on.
- A drafted spec §25 decision-log row recording the D7 landscape-first deviation and its mechanism.
- The rebuilt dev client installed on the tablet and kept as the known-good APK (spec §11.2).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decision comment answers the Question with evidence from the TB125FU, including the rotation/state-survival result.
- [ ] `orientation: 'default'` + per-route lock (or the explicitly justified alternative) verified: the prototype route locks landscape on focus, every other route keeps its current presentation, and blur restores it (D7).
- [ ] `expo-keep-awake` verified past the screen timeout and released on blur (doc §25).
- [ ] `expo-haptics` perceptibility on the TB125FU recorded per impact style, with a named fallback if the motor is weak (doc §21, §25).
- [ ] Dev client rebuilt on the locked Expo SDK 57 — no SDK, React Native, or BLE-library version changes (spec §11.2, CLAUDE.md rule 5).
- [ ] Spec §25 row for D7 drafted with the chosen mechanism, so the spec §19.4 deviation is recorded, not silent.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` pass on the config diff.

## Test plan
- Manual, on hardware only (this spike exists because the emulator cannot answer it): rotation matrix (portrait↔landscape × focused/blurred × backgrounded), screen-timeout wait, haptic cadence run. No unit tests — throwaway prototype code is deleted or clearly parked before close.

## Non-goals
- Building the actual live screen or its layout (M32-08), audio latency/focus/Spotify coexistence (M34-01), permanent `_layout.tsx` wiring (M32-08 lands it per this spike's decision).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: none.
- Unblocks: M32-08 (orientation/keep-awake/haptics mechanism and the rebuilt dev client).

## Notes
- Pitfall: every native module addition means prebuild + dev-client rebuild — coordinate with M34-01 so the tablet does not churn through two builds in one day.
- Do not re-litigate D7 (landscape-first for this screen); the spike chooses the mechanism, not the orientation.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Build token components: punch, body, defense, footwork, coach, stance card
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M32 (doc §27 steps 3 and 9). The token components are the visual vocabulary of the whole Puncheokie live experience: every cue the CueStage (M32-07) renders is composed from these primitives. They are pure presentational React components — all state arrives via props from the store; no domain logic, no subscriptions. Building them before the screen lets the visual grammar be reviewed in isolation.

## Design references

- Doc §13 — the visual command grammar this issue implements (restated under Behavior).
- Doc §21 — per-punch feedback: the active token briefly brightens; a missed token never flashes red mid-combination.
- Doc §25 — high-contrast and color-blind-safe labels, never color alone; large text and reduced-motion modes; glove-friendly sizing.
- Spec §19.4 — no color-only indication anywhere.
- Related: M31-01 (`WorkoutToken` unions), M32-07 (composes these into zones), M32-08 (screen), D10 (notation: data `body: boolean`, authored strings use lowercase `b`, the visual badge is uppercase **B**).

## Method

### Files
- `src/components/workout/PunchToken.tsx` — circular numbered token (new).
- `src/components/workout/DefenseToken.tsx` — word + motion-icon token (new).
- `src/components/workout/FootworkToken.tsx` — arrow/ring token (new).
- `src/components/workout/CoachBanner.tsx` — subordinate banner (new).
- `src/components/workout/StanceChangeCard.tsx` — full-width stance card (new).
- `src/components/workout/__tests__/tokens.test.tsx` — see Test plan.

### Interfaces
```ts
export type TokenVisualState = 'upcoming' | 'active' | 'completed'
export interface PunchTokenProps {
  number: PunchNumber; body: boolean; state: TokenVisualState
  handHint?: 'L' | 'R'; size?: 'stage' | 'preview'; reducedMotion?: boolean
}
export function PunchToken(props: PunchTokenProps): React.ReactElement
export interface DefenseTokenProps {
  command: 'duck' | 'bob-weave' | 'slip' | 'roll' | 'pull'
  state: TokenVisualState; size?: 'stage' | 'preview'; reducedMotion?: boolean
}
export function DefenseToken(props: DefenseTokenProps): React.ReactElement
export interface FootworkTokenProps {
  command: 'pivot' | 'step-off' | 'circle' | 'cut-off-ring' | 'reset'
  state: TokenVisualState; size?: 'stage' | 'preview'; reducedMotion?: boolean
}
export function FootworkToken(props: FootworkTokenProps): React.ReactElement
export function CoachBanner(props: {
  command: 'double-up' | 'put-it-on-em' | 'touch-and-go' | 'breathe' | 'hands-up'; visible: boolean
}): React.ReactElement
export function StanceChangeCard(props: { toStance: Stance; countdownMs?: number }): React.ReactElement
```

### Behavior
Doc §13 grammar, restated here as the binding spec:
- **Punch numbers** are large circular tokens. **Body shots** are the same numbered circle with a prominent uppercase **B** badge and a lower-on-screen placement cue (D10: the badge is visual; authored notation stays lowercase `b`).
- **Defense** commands are rounded-rectangular or hexagonal tokens carrying the word plus a simple motion icon.
- **Footwork** commands are arrow-shaped tokens or a ring/angle diagram (`circle`, `cut-off-ring`).
- **Coaching reminders** render as horizontal banner text, visually subordinate to active commands.
- **Stance change** is a full-width, high-contrast card with left/right foot orientation, optionally showing a countdown.
- States: `upcoming` is high-contrast but unfilled; `active` gets a bright animated ring; `completed` becomes subdued with a small check/hit flash. Every state is distinguishable by shape + text + icon, never color alone (spec §19.4).
- **No-red-flash rule:** a missed or unmatched token must not flash red during the combination — mismatch feedback belongs in the cue result and round summary (doc §13, §21). Mid-combo states never use `colors.danger`.
- **Reduced motion:** with `reducedMotion`, the animated ring is replaced by a static heavy outline plus the text/icon state markers (doc §25). The optional physical-hand hint (`L`/`R` below the number, doc §11) is caller-supplied.

### Data flow
Props only. M32-07's `CueStage` maps `CueInstance.tokens` plus engine statuses onto these components; nothing here reads stores, clocks, or the engine.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `PunchToken` renders numbers 1–6 in a circular token; `body: true` adds the uppercase **B** badge and lower placement cue (doc §13, D10).
- [ ] `DefenseToken` and `FootworkToken` render word + icon / arrow-or-ring forms for every command in their unions (doc §13).
- [ ] `CoachBanner` is visually subordinate (smaller type, no ring) and `StanceChangeCard` is full-width high-contrast with foot orientation (doc §13, §11).
- [ ] All three `TokenVisualState`s are distinguishable by shape + text + icon with color removed (spec §19.4, doc §25).
- [ ] No component ever styles a mid-combo state with `colors.danger` or any red flash (doc §13, §21).
- [ ] `reducedMotion` disables the animated ring on every token type (doc §25).
- [ ] All colors come from `@/theme/colors`; the `stage` size meets glove-friendly target dimensions (doc §25).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `tokens.test.tsx` (jest-expo + react-test-renderer): render matrix of every component × every state × `reducedMotion` on/off; body-badge presence; assert no style in the rendered tree resolves to `colors.danger` for any mid-combo state; banner subordination and stance-card snapshots.

## Non-goals
- Zone composition and layout (M32-07), animation timing against the cue clock (M32-08), the `CountBadge` result treatment with red/green/gold (M33-03 — the only place red appears, with text + icon).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-01 (`PunchNumber`, `Stance`, `WorkoutToken` command unions).
- Unblocks: M32-07, M32-08.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): no red flash mid-combo; red appears only in round/cue results (M33-03) with text + icon.
- Animations: prefer `react-native-reanimated` (already installed) — no new native module, no dev-client rebuild.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Build CueStage, RoundTopBar, and MetricsRail components for the live screen
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M32 (doc §27 steps 2–3). These are the three composed zones of the doc §19 live layout — top status bar, cue stage, and metrics rail — built as presentational components so M32-08 only assembles and feeds them. The rail is the customization surface: users choose at most four optional tiles (D9), and every velocity-derived surface must respect the source's capability (M32-02).

## Design references

- Doc §19 — the four-zone layout, zone contents, the eight optional tiles, and the ≤4 rule.
- Doc §5 — the live-screen content checklist these zones jointly satisfy.
- Spec §8.3 — the live metrics surface; §4.3 — velocity is "tracker-reported velocity" in tracker units, never force/power/energy.
- Spec §19.4 — no color-only indication; degraded mode uses text.
- Related: M32-06 (token primitives), M32-02 (`velocityAvailable`, `sequenceScoreLabel`), M32-08 (assembly), M33-05 (real required-pace values), D9.

## Method

### Files
- `src/components/workout/CueStage.tsx` — dominant combo zone (new).
- `src/components/workout/RoundTopBar.tsx` — status bar (new).
- `src/components/workout/MetricsRail.tsx` — metrics + optional tiles (new).
- `src/components/workout/__tests__/zones.test.tsx` — see Test plan.

### Interfaces
```ts
export interface CueView { cue: CueInstance; tokenStates: TokenVisualState[] }
export interface VelocityView { value: number; unit: 'tracker-unit'; label: 'tracker-reported velocity' }
export type TileId =
  | 'peak-velocity' | 'velocity-zone' | 'left-right-balance' | 'correct-hand-percent'
  | 'combo-completion' | 'punches-last-15s' | 'projected-final' | 'connection-completeness'
export function CueStage(props: { current?: CueView; next?: CueView; reducedMotion?: boolean }): React.ReactElement
export interface RoundTopBarProps {
  roundIndex: number; roundCount: number; roundRemainingMs: number; stance: Stance
  connection: { left: ConnectionState | 'simulated'; right: ConnectionState | 'simulated' }
  batteryPct?: { left?: number; right?: number }
  degraded?: string
}
export function RoundTopBar(props: RoundTopBarProps): React.ReactElement
export interface MetricsRailProps {
  counts: { total: number; left: number; right: number }
  roundGoal?: number; requiredPace?: number
  avgVelocity?: VelocityView; lastVelocity?: VelocityView
  velocityAvailable: boolean
  capabilityTier: CapabilityTier
  tiles: TileId[]   // user-chosen, at most 4 rendered (D9)
}
export function MetricsRail(props: MetricsRailProps): React.ReactElement
```

### Behavior
- **CueStage** (doc §19): the active combination occupies most of the zone, composed from M32-06 tokens with the active token's animated ring; the full combination stays visible for anticipation; the next combination appears above, smaller and dimmed; repeat count renders as ×N or a shrinking dot stack; body/defense/footwork tokens keep their distinct shapes and spatial cues.
- **RoundTopBar** (doc §19): round n/N, countdown timer, stance, L/R connection + battery status, and a subtle degraded-mode warning as text with an icon — never a bare color change (spec §19.4). A `'simulated'` connection renders an explicit SIM chip.
- **MetricsRail** (doc §19, D9): default metrics — actual punches / round target, current required pace, average velocity, most recent accepted velocity, left/right counts. Optional tiles, exactly the doc §19 set of eight: peak velocity, velocity zone, left/right balance, correct-hand percentage, combo completion, punches in the last 15 seconds, projected final count, connection completeness. At most four render; extras beyond four are ignored with a dev warning.
- **Capability gating:** when `velocityAvailable` is `false`, every velocity-derived surface (avg, last, `peak-velocity`, `velocity-zone`) is hidden entirely, not rendered empty (doc §3, M32-02). Visible velocity labels read "tracker-reported velocity" in tracker units (spec §4.3). The `correct-hand-percent` tile caption uses `sequenceScoreLabel(capabilityTier)` — at the FightCamp v1 `hand-broad-type` tier it reads **hand-sequence match**, never technique accuracy (D4, spec §13.3).

### Data flow
Pure props. M32-08 maps `LiveViewModel` from `useWorkoutStore` onto these three components; M33-05 later supplies real `requiredPace`; M33-02 supplies real correct-hand data (until then the tile shows an em dash).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `CueStage` renders the dominant current combo, dimmed next combo above, and ×N/dot-stack repeat treatment (doc §19).
- [ ] `RoundTopBar` renders round n/N, countdown, stance, L/R connection + battery, and a text+icon degraded warning (doc §19, spec §19.4).
- [ ] `MetricsRail` renders all five default metrics and supports exactly the eight doc §19 `TileId`s.
- [ ] At most 4 optional tiles render regardless of `tiles.length` (doc §19, D9).
- [ ] With `velocityAvailable: false`, no velocity tile or label appears anywhere in the rendered tree (doc §3).
- [ ] Every visible velocity label says "tracker-reported velocity" (tracker units); terminology guard passes (spec §4.3).
- [ ] The `correct-hand-percent` caption comes from `sequenceScoreLabel` and reads `hand-sequence match` for every tier except `hand-distinct-type` (D4, spec §13.3).
- [ ] Components are presentational only — no store, engine, or clock imports.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `zones.test.tsx` (jest-expo + react-test-renderer): CueStage with current + next and repeat variants; RoundTopBar degraded and simulated states; MetricsRail with 0/4/6 tiles (6 → 4 rendered); `velocityAvailable: false` hides all velocity surfaces; label assertions for the velocity and hand-sequence match strings.

## Non-goals
- Screen assembly, orientation, keep-awake, controls (M32-08); real pace values (M33-05); matching data (M33-02); round-result badge (M33-03); the tile-picker settings UI (lands with M32-08 or later).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M32-06 (token components), M32-02 (`CapabilityTier`, `sequenceScoreLabel`).
- Unblocks: M32-08.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): the rail is the customization surface and caps at four optional tiles (D9); velocity gating is structural (component absent), not cosmetic.
- `CueView`/`VelocityView` defined here are consumed verbatim by M32-08's `LiveViewModel`.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Build landscape live screen driven by CueEngine and SimulatedPunchSource
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M32 (doc §27 steps 2–3). The landscape live screen is the first visible Puncheokie deliverable. It is built against `SimulatedPunchSource` (M32-01) so it ships before the tracker stream is wired (M33-01), renders the four doc §19 zones, and subscribes to CueEngine (M32-04) through `useWorkoutStore`. On the Phase 5 DoD critical path. Landscape-first is a deliberate deviation from spec §19.4 (D7); M32-05 records the orientation mechanism.

## Design references

- Doc §19 (four zones, ≤4 optional tiles, settings locked during work), §5 (screen contents), §13 (visual grammar), §20 (statuses to render), §21 (per-punch feedback), §25 (keep-awake, glove targets, reduced motion, immediate stop).
- Spec §8.3/§8.4 (live UI + controls), §15.3 (throttled updates, no raw arrays in global state), §19.4 (no color-only indication, confirmation before discard), §4.3 (tracker-reported velocity), §13.5 (no app audio here — voice arrives in M34 behind its gate).
- Related: M32-05 (orientation/keep-awake/haptics), M32-06/M32-07 (components), M31-05 (samples), #107 M20-01, #112 M21-01.

## Method

### Files
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/live.tsx` — route (new); `_layout.tsx` — stack entry with header hidden for `live` (modify).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/useWorkoutRunner.ts` — hook instantiating SessionEngine + CueEngine + `PunchEventSource`, wiring ticks, throttling store writes to ≤10 Hz (new).
- `src/state/useWorkoutStore.ts` — live slice: phase, current/next `CueInstance`, token statuses, counts, last/avg velocity, tiles, source kind (extend).
- `src/components/workout/SimControls.tsx` — `__DEV__`-only drawer: tap L / tap R, play script, latency/jitter sliders (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export interface WorkoutRunner { start(): void; pause(): void; resume(): void; emergencyStop(): void; skipCue(): void; repeatCue(): void }
export function useWorkoutRunner(args: { workout: GeneratedWorkout; source: PunchEventSource; stance: Stance }): WorkoutRunner
export interface LiveViewModel {
  phase: SessionPhase; roundIndex: number; roundCount: number; roundRemainingMs: number; stance: Stance
  current?: CueView; next?: CueView
  counts: { total: number; left: number; right: number; inCue: number; inCueExpected: number }
  lastVelocity?: VelocityView; avgVelocity?: VelocityView   // undefined when the source has no velocity
  tiles: TileId[]; connection: { left: ConnectionState | 'simulated'; right: ConnectionState | 'simulated' }; degraded?: string
}
```

### Data flow
`PunchEventSource.subscribe` → runner → (M33-02 inserts CueMatcher here; for this issue each event increments counts and brightens the next unfilled expected token of the same hand) → store → zones. CueEngine events → store (`current/next`, token statuses). Haptic pulse on `token-due` (expo-haptics per M32-05). Keep-awake while phase ∈ {countdown, work, rest, paused}.

### Layout
`RoundTopBar`: round n/N, countdown, stance, L/R connection + battery placeholders, degraded text. `CueStage`: active combo dominant with animated ring, full combo visible, next combo dimmed above, ×N or dot stack. `MetricsRail`: actual / round goal, required pace (placeholder until M33-05), avg + last tracker-reported velocity, L/R counts, ≤4 optional tiles. Controls: pause/resume, emergency stop, skip/repeat behind long-press (glove mis-tap guard).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Route locks landscape on focus and restores the app default on blur per the M32-05 decision; keep-awake is active only while a workout runs.
- [ ] All doc §19 zone contents and the full doc §5 list render for `Three-Round Fundamentals` (M31-05) on the simulated source.
- [ ] Token states use shape + text + icon in addition to color (doc §13, spec §19.4); no red flash mid-combo.
- [ ] Tapping L/R in `SimControls` increments counts and brightens the matching token within one frame; store writes throttled to ≤10 Hz (spec §15.3).
- [ ] Pause suspends cues with visible "Paused" text; resume restores; emergency stop halts cues and haptics immediately, then offers Save / Discard behind a confirmation (doc §25, spec §19.4).
- [ ] Settings and recipe navigation are unreachable while phase = work (doc §19).
- [ ] Velocity tiles hidden when the source reports no velocity; visible labels say "tracker-reported velocity" (spec §4.3); terminology guard passes.
- [ ] No app-generated audio on this screen (voice lands in M34 behind its gate).
- [ ] Runs via `expo start --dev-client` on the tablet in landscape and survives rotation without losing session state.

## Test plan
- Component tests (jest-expo + react-test-renderer): store → `LiveViewModel` mapping; control enablement per phase; token rendering per `CueStatus`; velocity tiles hidden for a hand-only source.
- Manual on tablet: run the sample with script `alternating-1-2` at 0/80/200 ms latency; pause/resume/stop; rotate; wait past the screen timeout to confirm keep-awake.

## Non-goals
- Real tracker stream (M33-01), matching/scoring (M33-02), voice (M34), live pacing values (M33-05), round-result badge and rest phases (M33-03/M33-04).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M32-01, M32-04, M32-05, M32-06, M32-07, M31-05, #107 M20-01 (SessionEngine API).
- Unblocks: M33-01, M33-02, M34-05, M33-04, M36-02.

## Notes
- Use `@/theme/colors`; add `colors.gold` here if absent (M33-03 CountBadge needs it too).
- Keep `SimControls` out of release builds (`__DEV__`).
- On completion, comment with landscape screenshots, the throttle interval chosen, and any deviation from `LiveViewModel`.

issues.title: CueEngine tests: timeline expansion, pause suspension, clamping, timestamps
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M32 (doc §27 step 3 closure). M32-04 ships the CueEngine with a base suite; this issue adds the exhaustive, adversarial coverage that the downstream consumers (M33-02 matching, M33-05 pacing, M34-03 voice) will lean on: every doc §20 transition, timeline clamping under edge geometry, pause/suspension semantics, timestamp completeness, and a property test over generated timelines. Pure TS, fake clock, runs on Windows CI without hardware (spec §21.1).

## Design references

- Doc §20 — the cue state machine and its preserved timestamps; every transition needs a named case.
- Spec §18.2 — accepted events fall inside work; windows never exceed the work interval.
- Spec §21.1 — pure domain functions get unit tests; deterministic, hardware-free.
- Related: M32-03 (`expandTimeline` under test), M32-04 (`CueEngine` under test; its base suite is extended, not duplicated), #133 M26-04 (curated replay fixtures for CueMatcher — shared fixture shapes, different subject).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/CueTimeline.expansion.test.ts` — timeline-side suite (new).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/CueEngine.lifecycle.test.ts` — engine-side suite (new; M32-04's `CueEngine.test.ts` stays as the smoke walk).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/helpers/fakeClock.ts` — shared fake `MonotonicClock` + tick scripter (new).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/helpers/timelineGen.ts` — seeded random-timeline generator for the property test (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export function makeFakeClock(startMs?: number): MonotonicClock & { advance(ms: number): void }
export function generateTimeline(seed: number): RoundTimeline[]   // small seeded LCG; always valid, clamped timelines
```

### Algorithm / state machine
Named test cases (binding — implement each under this name):

`CueTimeline.expansion.test.ts`
1. `expands Three-Round Fundamentals into ordered non-overlapping CueInstances`
2. `repeat 3 yields repeatIndex 0..2 re-based by combo duration plus gapBeats`
3. `clamps windowStartMs to 0 when graceBefore precedes the bell`
4. `clamps windowEndMs to workDurationMs when graceAfter outlives the round`
5. `display-only defense, footwork, and coach tokens are unscored and listed in displayOnlyTokenIndexes`
6. `southpaw flips expectedPunches hands; switch block inverts the default stance`
7. `stance changes land only at block boundaries`

`CueEngine.lifecycle.test.ts`
8. `walks every §20 transition once for a fully matched exact-combo cue (queued to previewing, announcing, active, accepting, completed, gap)`
9. `accepting expires with partial counts at windowCloseMs when 2 of 3 punches matched`
10. `gap follows completed and expired until the next previewAt — status name is gap, never recovery`
11. `paused mid-active suspends and resumed restores prior status with a suspension record`
12. `pause while queued or in gap emits no cue-suspended`
13. `rest-entered cancels every remaining cue exactly once and a repeated rest-entered emits nothing`
14. `cancelled and finishing behave like rest-entered for remaining cues`
15. `timestamps are complete: scheduled at load, actuals at emission, trackerEventTimesMs appended per notifyMatch`
16. `frozen workElapsedMs with advancing clock.nowMs produces zero transitions`
17. `property: over 200 seeded random timelines and tick schedules, emitted events are monotonic in workElapsedMs and every window lies in [0, workDurationMs]`

**Invariants asserted throughout:** no wall time; every `CueEvent` carries full `CueTimestamps`; `token-due` count equals token count per instance.

### Data flow
Test-only. `timelineGen` feeds `expandTimeline` outputs and hand-built `RoundTimeline`s into `CueEngine`; session phases are driven with hand-made `SessionPhaseEvent`s, so no SessionEngine dependency exists in these tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every doc §20 transition, including the `suspended` and `cancelled` paths, is exercised by a named case above.
- [ ] Cases 3–4 pin the clamping formula and case 17 proves windows never exceed the work interval (spec §18.2, D5).
- [ ] Case 5 proves display-only tokens are excluded from `expectedPunches` and from completion (D4).
- [ ] Cases 13–14 prove cancel-exactly-once semantics (doc §25 immediate stop).
- [ ] Case 15 proves the doc §20 timestamp set is preserved end to end.
- [ ] Case 16 pins the `workElapsedMs`-only time base; case 10 pins the `gap` naming (D5).
- [ ] The property test (case 17) is seeded and reproducible — a failing seed is printed and re-runnable.
- [ ] §15.1 purity: suites import only `src/domain/**`; no timers, no `Date.now()`, no React/Expo/BLE.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- This issue is the test plan: the 17 named cases plus helpers, all green in one `npm test` run on Windows without Bluetooth (spec §21.1). Keep total runtime under roughly 10 s so the suite stays in the default CI path.

## Non-goals
- Matching-outcome tests (#130/#133 own CueMatcher and its fixtures), UI/component tests (M32-08), pacing tests (M33-05), bag-tuned constants (M36-03 may adjust graces — these tests assert structure, not tuned values).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M32-03 (`expandTimeline`, `CueInstance`, `RoundTimeline`), M32-04 (`CueEngine`, `CueState`).
- Unblocks: nothing directly — it is the regression net under M33-02, M33-05, and M34-03.

## Notes
- Hand-roll the seeded generator (small LCG in `timelineGen.ts`) rather than adding `fast-check` — no new dependency without a version-lock discussion (spec §11.2).
- Assert structure and invariants, not tuned constants: M36-03 will change grace/lead values and must not break this suite.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Wire TrackerPunchEventSource into the live screen: count and velocity overlays
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M33 (doc §27 step 6). Replaces `SimulatedPunchSource` with the real FightCamp v1 stream on the live screen: tracker count and velocity overlays only — no technique scoring, which arrives with CueMatcher in M33-02. `TrackerPunchEventSource` is the production implementation of the `PunchEventSource` port (M32-01), so the M32-08 screen needs only a source swap. On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §19 (top bar: L/R connection, degraded text), §21 (count-only feedback tier), §27 step 6.
- Spec §8.2 (readiness gate: per-hand readiness, capability summary, degraded warnings, Spotify status only when launched from Puncheokie), §12.5 (`TrackerPunchEvent`), §19.3 (reconnect), §4.3 (tracker-reported velocity, tracker units).
- Protocol H11 (`docs/protocol/hypotheses.md`): hand is NOT in the payload — it comes from the connection slot; the type byte's `'power'` value is a punch classification, never a unit.
- Related: M32-01, M32-02, M32-08, #112 M21-01, #110 M20-04, #115 M22-01.

## Method

### Files
- `src/protocol/TrackerPunchEventSource.ts` — `PunchEventSource` implementation wrapping `startPunchStream` for both slots (new).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/useWorkoutRunner.ts` — accept an injected source; surface degraded state (modify).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/live.tsx` — tracker source by default; sim + `SimControls` stay `__DEV__`-only (modify).
- `src/state/useWorkoutStore.ts` — `connection.left/right` fed from `useTrackerStore` slots (modify).

### Interfaces
```ts
export interface TrackerPunchEventSourceOptions {
  facade: BleManagerFacade
  adapter: TrackerProtocolAdapter
  slots: { left?: { deviceId: string }; right?: { deviceId: string } } // from useTrackerStore
}
export class TrackerPunchEventSource implements PunchEventSource {
  readonly id: 'tracker'
  capability: SourceCapability // starts 'hand-only'; upgraded from observed events (M32-02)
  constructor(opts: TrackerPunchEventSourceOptions)
  start(): Promise<void>  // one startPunchStream per assigned slot
  stop(): Promise<void>   // stops both PunchStreamControllers
  subscribe(listener: (e: TrackerPunchEvent) => void): () => void
}
```

### Behavior
1. `start()` calls `startPunchStream` (`src/protocol/PunchStream.ts`) once per assigned slot with `hand: 'left' | 'right'` from the slot — **hand comes from the slot assignment, never from frame bytes** (H11).
2. Capability is resolved from observed events via `resolveCapabilityTier` (M32-02); FightCamp v1 settles at `hand-broad-type` with velocity (D4).
3. Readiness handoff: the live route is entered only through the #112 readiness gate (`useBothReady()`), which shows capability summary, degraded warnings, and Spotify status only when launched from Puncheokie (spec §8.2).
4. A slot dropping to `recovering` (§11.5, #110) sets `degraded` text in `RoundTopBar`; `recovered: true` events after reconnect still count.
5. Per event: total/L/R counts increment; last/average tracker-reported velocity tiles update. No matching.

### Data flow
`useTrackerStore` slots → `TrackerPunchEventSource.start()` → per-slot `startPunchStream` → `TrackerPunchEvent` → `useWorkoutRunner` → throttled `useWorkoutStore` writes → zones.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `TrackerPunchEventSource` implements the `PunchEventSource` port unchanged; `useWorkoutRunner` needs zero interface changes (M32-01).
- [ ] Every event's `hand` comes from the slot that produced the frame, never from payload bytes (H11).
- [ ] `capability` upgrades via `resolveCapabilityTier` from observed events, reaching `hand-broad-type` + velocity on FightCamp v1 (M32-02, D4).
- [ ] The live route is reachable only through the #112 readiness gate; degraded warnings and Spotify status behave per spec §8.2.
- [ ] Tracker drop mid-round shows `degraded` text in `RoundTopBar`; reconnect (#110) resumes counting without restarting the session (spec §19.3).
- [ ] Velocity tiles are labeled "tracker-reported velocity" in tracker units — never a physical-unit, force, or energy label (spec §4.3); terminology guard passes.
- [ ] No technique scoring; any visible sequence-score surface stays labeled `hand-sequence match` (D4, spec §13.3).
- [ ] Verified on the tablet with both trackers (blue = left, red = right): counts and velocity update live for both hands.

## Test plan
- Unit: `TrackerPunchEventSource.test.ts` with a fake facade/adapter — per-slot start, hand stamping, capability upgrade, `stop()` teardown.
- Manual (hardware): both trackers through the gate; punch each hand; power-cycle one tracker mid-round → degraded text, then recovery.

## Non-goals
- Matching/scoring (M33-02); pacing (M33-05); persistence (M33-08); Voice Coach (M34).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M32-08 (live screen + `useWorkoutRunner`), M32-01 (port), #112 M21-01 (readiness-gate handoff), #110 M20-04 (reconnect), #115 M22-01 (session tables).
- Unblocks: M36-03 (bag testing runs on this stream); gives M33-02 its hardware path.

## Notes
- Hardware required: both FightCamp v1 trackers and the tablet dev client.
- Decision (do not re-litigate): capability comes from observed events, not a static adapter claim (M32-02).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Integrate CueMatcher into the live screen: per-punch feedback and extras policy
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M33 (doc §27 step 10). Inserts CueMatcher (#130) between the punch-event source and the store in `useWorkoutRunner`: matched punches brighten and complete tokens, feed `CueEngine.notifyMatch`, and drive the doc §21 per-punch feedback loop. At the FightCamp v1 tier this is hand + broad-type matching only, and every surface showing a sequence score says **hand-sequence match** (D4). On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §6 (one event per expected punch, event-time order, recovered events, hand vs type mismatch as separate outcomes, extras never disappear), §21 (per-punch feedback; extras policy encouraged / neutral / marked).
- Spec §13.3 (hand-sequence match label on every surface), §13.6 (matching + scoring dimensions), §15.3 (throttled store writes), §4.3 (tracker-reported velocity).
- Related: #130 M26-01 (CueMatcher), #131 M26-02 (outcome/label rules), M32-02 (`sequenceScoreLabel`), M32-08, M33-01.

## Method

### Files
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/useWorkoutRunner.ts` — instantiate CueMatcher; wire source → matcher → CueEngine/store (modify).
- `src/state/useWorkoutStore.ts` — per-cue match state: matched/expected per token, extras count, last outcome (extend).
- `src/components/workout/CueStage.tsx` — consume token match states (modify; render states exist from M32-06).

### Interfaces
Consumed, not defined here — names from #130 / M32-04 / M32-02 are binding:
```ts
matcher.onCueEvent(e)      // CueEngine 'cue-window-opened' | 'cue-window-closed'
matcher.onPunchEvent(ev)   // TrackerPunchEvent in receive order; recovered events per doc §6
matcher.subscribe((m: MatchResult) => {
  cueEngine.notifyMatch(m.cueId, m.expectedIndex, m.eventTimeMs)
  // store: token state, counters, lastVelocity, extras
})
sequenceScoreLabel(tier)   // M32-02 — 'hand-sequence match' at hand-broad-type
```

### Behavior
1. The runner subscribes the matcher to CueEngine `cue-window-opened/closed` and to the active `PunchEventSource`; match results call `CueEngine.notifyMatch`.
2. On a match: the expected token brightens/completes, in-cue and total counters increment, the latest tracker-reported velocity tile updates, an optional low-intensity haptic pulse fires (doc §21).
3. Extras follow the recipe policy — encouraged (volume blocks), neutral, or marked; extras remain counted and visible, never disappear (spec §13.6).
4. Hand mismatch and type mismatch are separate outcomes; broad-type agreement is a secondary metric with caveat text (#131, D4).
5. **Defense, footwork, and coach tokens are never auto-failed** — display-only, excluded from scoring and completion (D4, doc §21). Body-vs-head placement is unscored.
6. No red flash mid-combo; mismatch detail belongs in cue results and the round summary (doc §13, §21).

### Data flow
Source → matcher (windows from CueEngine) → `notifyMatch` + store (≤10 Hz, spec §15.3) → `CueStage` / `MetricsRail`. Match outcomes accumulate in the runner for M33-08 to persist as `cue_results`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CueMatcher consumes `cue-window-opened/closed` and calls `CueEngine.notifyMatch` per match — interfaces from #130 / M32-04 used verbatim.
- [ ] A matched punch brightens its token, increments counters, and updates the latest tracker-reported velocity tile within one frame; store writes ≤10 Hz (doc §21, spec §15.3, §4.3).
- [ ] One event assigns to at most one expected punch, in event-time order; `recovered: true` events are assignable only when the tracker timestamp supports reliable ordering (doc §6, spec §13.6).
- [ ] Extras are counted per the recipe extras policy and never disappear (spec §13.6).
- [ ] Defense/footwork/coach tokens are never auto-failed and never enter scoring or completion (D4); body-vs-head is unscored.
- [ ] Every sequence-score status string reads `hand-sequence match` via `sequenceScoreLabel(tier)` — never technique accuracy (D4, spec §13.3).
- [ ] No red flash during a combination (doc §13, §21; spec §19.4).
- [ ] Works identically against `SimulatedPunchSource` and `TrackerPunchEventSource`; terminology guard passes.

## Test plan
- Integration (jest, fake clock): scripted run of `combo-1-2-3-2` — token states, counters, all three extras-policy variants; hand-mismatch and recovered-event cases; label string asserted at `hand-broad-type`.
- Manual (after M33-01): same script on the bag; verify one-frame feedback and the haptic.

## Non-goals
- Matcher internals (#130); scoring-dimension math (#131); count-scored bursts (M33-06); persistence (M33-08); grading (M33-03).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: #130 M26-01 (CueMatcher over `CueInstance.expectedPunches`), #131 M26-02 (outcome/label rules), M32-08 (runner + live screen).
- Unblocks: M33-06, M33-08, M36-03.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): the matcher lives in the runner, not the store — the store holds view-model state only (spec §15.3).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement roundGrading and CountBadge with over/short/exact text and icon
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M33 (doc §27 step 7). Pure grading of a round's punch count against its target, plus the `CountBadge` component that renders it. The badge is the primary round result (doc §23) and is reused verbatim on the rest screen (M33-04) and the workout summary (M33-08). Counts only: the badge grades punch count against target — technique is never graded, and any sequence score rendered near it carries the **hand-sequence match** label (D4).

## Design references

- Doc §23 — green over / red short / gold exact; text + icon required; the three-phase rest consumes this badge; no letter grades; secondary badges are recognitions, not grades.
- Spec §19.4 — color must never be the only indicator; §4.3 — velocity fields shown near the badge stay "tracker-reported velocity"; §15.1 — grading is pure domain code.
- Related: M31-01 (`ProgramRound.targetPunches`), M33-04 (rest presentation), M33-08 (summary), M32-08 (adds `colors.gold` if it lands first).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/roundGrading.ts` — `gradeRound` + status-text formatting (new).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/roundGrading.test.ts` — see Test plan (new).
- `src/components/workout/CountBadge.tsx` — circular count badge (new).
- `src/theme/colors.ts` — add `gold` if not already present (modify).

### Interfaces
```ts
export type RoundOutcome = 'over' | 'short' | 'exact'
export interface RoundGrade { outcome: RoundOutcome; delta: number } // delta = actual - target
export function gradeRound(actual: number, target: number): RoundGrade
export function gradeStatusText(grade: RoundGrade): string // '+6 OVER' | '19 SHORT' | 'EXACT TARGET'
export type SecondaryBadgeId = 'pace-consistency' | 'velocity-consistency' | 'left-right-balance'
  | 'best-round' | 'exact-sequence-streak' | 'tracker-coverage'
export function CountBadge(props: { actual: number; target: number; size?: 'hero' | 'compact' }): JSX.Element
```

### Behavior
1. `gradeRound`: `actual > target` → `over`, `actual < target` → `short`, `actual === target` → `exact`; `delta` is signed.
2. `CountBadge` renders count, target, status text, and icon — the three doc §23 treatments verbatim:
   - green — `246 / 240` · `+6 OVER` (up icon)
   - red — `221 / 240` · `19 SHORT` (down icon)
   - gold — `240 / 240` · `EXACT TARGET` (target icon)
3. Gold uses `colors.gold`; over/short use `colors.success` / `colors.danger`. **Color is never the only indicator** — text and icon always render (spec §19.4).
4. No letter grades anywhere. Secondary badges (`SecondaryBadgeId`) are optional recognitions layered on by M33-04/M33-08; the exact-sequence streak is a `hand-sequence match` streak at the FightCamp tier.

### Data flow
Frozen round counts (M33-04) or summary totals (M33-08) → `gradeRound` → `CountBadge`. No store or repository access from this module.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `gradeRound(actual, target)` returns `{ outcome: 'over' | 'short' | 'exact', delta }` matching doc §23 for all three cases, including the delta sign.
- [ ] `CountBadge` renders exactly `246 / 240` + `+6 OVER`, `221 / 240` + `19 SHORT`, and `240 / 240` + `EXACT TARGET` for those inputs, each with an icon and status text alongside the color (doc §23, spec §19.4).
- [ ] The gold state uses `colors.gold` from `@/theme/colors`; the palette entry exists exactly once, shared with M32-08.
- [ ] No letter grade appears in any rendered output (doc §23).
- [ ] The badge grades counts only; any adjacent sequence-score text is labeled `hand-sequence match` (D4, spec §13.3).
- [ ] `roundGrading.ts` has zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, SQLite, or `src/ble/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `roundGrading.test.ts`: over/short/exact cases, delta signs, status-text strings byte-exact, property: outcome always consistent with delta sign.
- Component test: three snapshot renders (hero + compact), icon and text present in each.

## Non-goals
- Rest-phase orchestration (M33-04); summary totals and secondary-badge computation (M33-08).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-01 (`ProgramRound.targetPunches`).
- Unblocks: M33-04; reused by M33-08.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): the count target is the objective result — no letter grades by default (doc §23).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Round transition: freeze result at bell and three-phase rest presentation
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M33 (doc §27 step 7). At the bell the round result freezes and the one-minute rest becomes three presentation phases: result, recovery, next-round preview. Per D6 these are presentation sub-phases inside the single SessionEngine `rest` state — no new session states — and "skip rest" skips all three. Consumes `CountBadge` / `gradeRound` (M33-03) and the counts accumulated by the runner (M32-08).

## Design references

- Doc §23 — freeze at the bell; the three phases and their contents; example announcements; no letter grades.
- Spec §18.1 — the session machine owns `rest` and gains no sub-states (D6); §19.4 — text + icon alongside color; §4.3 — velocity averages stay "tracker-reported velocity".
- Related: M33-03 (badge), M32-08 (runner + store), M34-02/M34-03 (voice hooks land later behind the D1 gate), M36-03.

## Method

### Files
- `src/components/workout/RestPhases.tsx` — rest container + the three phase views (new).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/useWorkoutRunner.ts` — freeze snapshot on `rest-entered`; expose rest-elapsed time (modify).
- `src/state/useWorkoutStore.ts` — `frozenRoundResult` slice + rest-phase selector (extend).

### Interfaces
```ts
export type RestPhase = 'result' | 'recovery' | 'preview'
export function restPhaseAt(restElapsedMs: number, restDurationMs: number): RestPhase
// thresholds at 20 % and 75 % — 0–12 s / 12–45 s / 45–60 s for the standard 60 s rest
export interface FrozenRoundResult {
  roundIndex: number; actual: number; target: number; left: number; right: number
```
