```ts
  avgVelocity?: VelocityView // tracker-reported; undefined when the source has no velocity
  bestCombo?: string; trackerDropped: boolean
}
export function RestPhases(props: {
  frozen: FrozenRoundResult
  nextRound: { theme: string; stance: Stance; sampleCombos: string[] }
  restElapsedMs: number; restDurationMs: number
  onSkipRest(): void
}): JSX.Element
```

### Behavior
1. On `rest-entered` the runner snapshots counts into `FrozenRoundResult`; later events during rest never mutate it.
2. **0–12 s — result** (doc §23): `CountBadge` with over/short/exact status, round average tracker-reported velocity, Voice Coach summary hook (no-op port call until M34).
3. **12–45 s — recovery**: breathing animation (reduced-motion aware), left/right balance, best combo or best tracker-reported velocity, connection warning if a tracker dropped.
4. **45–60 s — next-round preview**: next theme, stance, two sample combinations, countdown, voice announcement hook.
5. "Skip rest" advances the SessionEngine out of `rest` — all three phases skipped together (D6); no per-phase skip.
6. Phase selection is a pure function of rest-elapsed time; the SessionEngine remains in `rest` throughout (spec §18.1).

### Data flow
SessionEngine `rest-entered` → runner freeze → store `frozenRoundResult` → `RestPhases` (phase from `restPhaseAt`). `onSkipRest` → runner → SessionEngine skip. Voice hooks publish through `VoiceOutputPort` only (silent until M34-05).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Counts freeze at `rest-entered`: punch events during rest never change the displayed result (doc §23, spec §18.2).
- [ ] `restPhaseAt` yields `result` / `recovery` / `preview` at 0–12 s / 12–45 s / 45–60 s for a 60 s rest, proportionally (20 % / 75 %) otherwise.
- [ ] The SessionEngine state remains `rest` the whole minute — no new §18.1 states (D6); sub-phases are presentation only.
- [ ] "Skip rest" skips all three phases and enters the next round (D6).
- [ ] Each phase renders its doc §23 contents; the result phase reuses `CountBadge` with text + icon alongside color (spec §19.4).
- [ ] Velocity readouts say "tracker-reported velocity" (spec §4.3); any sequence-score line is labeled `hand-sequence match` (D4, spec §13.3).
- [ ] No app audio in this issue — voice hooks stay behind the port (D1, M34).
- [ ] Reduced motion disables the breathing animation (doc §25).

## Test plan
- Unit: `restPhaseAt` boundaries (0, 11 999, 12 000, 44 999, 45 000, 59 999 for 60 s; plus a 30 s rest).
- Component: freeze semantics, per-phase content snapshots, skip-rest wiring.
- Manual on tablet: run `Three-Round Fundamentals`, watch one full rest cycle, skip one rest.

## Non-goals
- Grading math (M33-03); workout summary (M33-08); spoken summaries (M34-03/M34-05); pacing decisions during rest (M33-05).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M33-03 (`gradeRound`, `CountBadge`), M32-08 (runner, store, live screen).
- Unblocks: M36-03 (the bag protocol reviews rest pacing and readability).

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): sub-phase thresholds are fractions (20 % / 75 %) so non-standard rest lengths degrade gracefully; tuned in M36-03 if needed.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement PacingEngine: required pace and boundary-only adaptive adjustments
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M33 (doc §27 step 11, first half). The PacingEngine maintains required pace against the punch goal and proposes adjustments only at safe boundaries. It implements the doc §22 `fixed` and `adaptive` plan behaviors; `goal-seeking` mutation builds on it in M33-07. Pure domain code under `src/domain/programs/`; the live screen's pace tiles read its snapshots. On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §22 — the maintained quantities, boundary-only adjustment, three plan behaviors, ±10–15 % per-round cadence limit, single periodic cue; §25 — never encourage acceleration to recover an impossible target.
- Spec §18.3 — monotonic/work-clock time only; §15.1 — no RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports; §4.3 — pacing is counts and cadence, never a velocity label.
- Related: M31-03 (schedule + goals), M32-03 (timeline boundaries), M32-04 (CueEngine), M33-06 (allocation), M33-07 (goal-seeking + persistence).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/PacingEngine.ts` — engine (new).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/PacingEngine.test.ts` — see Test plan (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export interface PacingSnapshot {
  remainingPunches: number
  remainingActiveSeconds: number
  requiredPace: number // punches per minute
  projectedTotal: number
}
export type PacingBoundary = 'block' | 'rest' | 'round'
export type PacingCueText = 'Build the pace' | 'You are ahead; stay sharp'
export interface AdaptationDecision {
  boundary: PacingBoundary; atWorkElapsedMs: number
  inputs: PacingSnapshot & { mode: 'fixed' | 'adaptive' | 'goal-seeking'; roundIndex: number }
  action:
    | { kind: 'none'; reason?: 'fixed-plan' | 'within-band' | 'target-unreachable' }
    | { kind: 'cadence-scale'; factor: number } // clamped to the profile BPM range
    | { kind: 'gap-scale'; factor: number }
    | { kind: 'reallocate'; roundTargets: number[] } // goal-seeking only (M33-07)
  cueText?: PacingCueText
}
export class PacingEngine {
  constructor(opts: {
    totalGoal: number; schedule: ProgramRound[]
    mode: 'fixed' | 'adaptive' | 'goal-seeking'
    profile: CadenceProfile; maxRequiredPace: number
  })
  recordAccepted(count: number): void
  snapshot(activeElapsedSeconds: number): PacingSnapshot
  onBoundary(boundary: PacingBoundary, ctx: { roundIndex: number; atWorkElapsedMs: number }): AdaptationDecision
}
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. The engine maintains exactly the doc §22 quantities:
```text
remainingPunches = totalGoal - acceptedPunches
remainingActiveSeconds = sum(unelapsed active-work time)
requiredPace = remainingPunches / remainingActiveSeconds * 60
```
`remainingActiveSeconds` counts only `countsTowardGoal` rounds (M31-03).
2. **Adjustments happen only at safe boundaries** — after a cue block, during a rest, or at the start of the next round (doc §22). `recordAccepted` / `snapshot` never produce decisions.
3. `fixed`: every boundary returns `{ kind: 'none', reason: 'fixed-plan' }`.
4. `adaptive`: factors move gradually — **at most ±10–15 % cadence change per round**, clamped to the profile's BPM range (M31-02); theme and technique distribution preserved, blocks never rewritten.
5. `requiredPace > maxRequiredPace` (density ceiling, tuned M36-03) → `target-unreachable`, no action, no cue — never a catch-up cadence (doc §25).
6. `cueText` at most once per boundary, only when the band is crossed: behind → `Build the pace`; ahead → `You are ahead; stay sharp` (doc §22, exact strings).
7. **Invariants:** decisions only from `onBoundary`; times are `workElapsedMs`/monotonic (spec §18.3); deterministic for identical call sequences.

### Data flow
Runner feeds accepted counts (M33-02) and boundary events (CueEngine/SessionEngine) → `AdaptationDecision` → store tiles (`requiredPace`, projected total) and, in M33-07, `WorkoutRepository.appendAdaptation`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `remainingPunches`, `remainingActiveSeconds`, `requiredPace` reproduce the doc §22 formulas exactly, excluding non-`countsTowardGoal` rounds.
- [ ] No decision outside `onBoundary` (property test over interleaved `recordAccepted` / `snapshot` calls).
- [ ] Adaptive factors respect the ±10–15 % per-round limit and the profile BPM range (doc §22, M31-02).
- [ ] `fixed` mode never alters the plan.
- [ ] An unreachable target yields `target-unreachable` with no action and no cue (doc §22, §25).
- [ ] `cueText` values are exactly `Build the pace` and `You are ahead; stay sharp`, at most one per boundary (doc §22).
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, SQLite, `src/ble/**`; no `Date.now()` (spec §15.1, §18.3).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `PacingEngine.test.ts`: formula cases from the doc §10 20-minute matrix; behind/ahead/on-pace boundaries per mode; band clamping; unreachable target; determinism (same call sequence twice → deep-equal decisions).

## Non-goals
- Plan mutation and persistence (M33-07); goal allocation (M33-06); UI tile wiring beyond replacing the M32-08 placeholder.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-03 (`buildRoundSchedule`, goal tiers), M32-03 (boundary structure of the cue timeline).
- Unblocks: M33-07.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): the adaptive band is a factor with the per-round delta capped at 10–15 %; constants live in `tuning.ts`, tuned in M36-03.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Support volume-burst and open-pressure blocks with per-round goal allocation
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M33 (doc §27 step 8). Adds the two count-scored block kinds — `volume-burst` and `open-pressure` — to the cue timeline and engines, and implements `allocateRoundTargets` so the total punch goal is split across rounds. These blocks make high goals achievable: the tracker count, not individually enumerated commands, determines output (doc §14). At high goals the plan adds volume blocks rather than shrinking pauses (doc §17).

## Design references

- Doc §14 — timed volume burst (allowed pattern + short countdown; tracker count decides output; essential for high targets) and open pressure (total punches with optional hand/type constraints, e.g. finish every exchange with a 2, without prescribing every punch); §10 — focus scaling; §17 — at high goals primarily increase repeated and timed-volume blocks, never shorten every pause until commands become unintelligible; §22 — allocation feeds pacing.
- Spec §13.6 — extras encouraged in volume blocks, never disappear; §15.1 — purity.
- Related: M32-03 (timeline), M32-04 (CueEngine), M33-02 (matcher count feed), M31-03 (schedule/goals/focus), M33-07 (reallocation), M35-03 (generator emits these blocks).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/goalAllocation.ts` — `allocateRoundTargets` (new).
- `src/domain/programs/CueTimeline.ts` — count-scored cue expansion: no per-token expected punches; countdown metadata (modify).
- `src/domain/programs/CueEngine.ts` — count-scored completion at window close (modify).
- Tests alongside each.

### Interfaces
```ts
export function allocateRoundTargets(
  goal: number,
  schedule: ProgramRound[],
  focus: 'hands' | 'movement' | 'balanced',
): number[] // one per round; 0 for countsTowardGoal: false rounds; sums exactly to goal
export interface CountScoredCue {
  scoring: 'count' // sequence cues carry scoring: 'sequence'
  targetPunches: number
  allowedPattern?: string // display only, e.g. '1-2'
  constraint?: { finisher?: PunchNumber; hand?: 'lead' | 'rear' }
  countdownMs: number
}
```

### Behavior
1. `expandTimeline` turns `volume-burst` / `open-pressure` blocks into count-scored cues: an allowed pattern for display, `targetPunches`, and a countdown instead of per-token `token-due` scheduling; windows still clamp to the work interval (M32-03).
2. The CueEngine closes a count-scored cue at `windowCloseMs` with achieved count vs target — a low count is a result, not a failure (doc §21). The matcher (M33-02) feeds per-event counts; extras inside bursts are encouraged and always counted (spec §13.6).
3. Open-pressure constraints apply only when the capability tier supports them; at `hand-broad-type` a type-level constraint degrades to display-only (D4).
4. `allocateRoundTargets` distributes the goal over `countsTowardGoal` rounds, weighted by round active time and focus (movement rounds carry lower targets, doc §10); deterministic; sums exactly to `goal`.
5. **High-goal rule:** when a round target implies a pace above the exact-combo density ceiling (`tuning.ts`), the plan adds or lengthens volume blocks — it never compresses gaps below the intelligibility floor (doc §17).

### Data flow
Recipe goal + schedule → `allocateRoundTargets` → `ProgramRound.targetPunches` → PacingEngine (M33-05) and `CountBadge` targets (M33-03). Matcher counts → CueEngine count-scored completion → store (burst tile: achieved / target + countdown).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `volume-burst` and `open-pressure` cues are scored by tracker count against `targetPunches`; no per-token sequence scoring applies to them (doc §14).
- [ ] The live screen shows the allowed pattern and a countdown for a burst cue; extras during bursts are encouraged, counted, and never disappear (doc §21, spec §13.6).
- [ ] A type-level open-pressure constraint degrades to display-only at `hand-broad-type`; count readouts are counts, never technique accuracy (D4).
- [ ] `allocateRoundTargets(goal, schedule, focus)` sums exactly to `goal`, assigns 0 to `countsTowardGoal: false` rounds, and scales with focus per doc §10.
- [ ] Allocation is deterministic: identical inputs give identical arrays.
- [ ] At a goal implying a pace above the density ceiling the plan gains volume blocks; block gaps never drop below the floor constant (doc §17).
- [ ] Zero RN/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports in `goalAllocation.ts` and the modified domain files (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `goalAllocation.test.ts`: 20/30/40/60-minute schedules × three focuses; sum invariant; warm-up/cooldown exclusion; determinism.
- CueTimeline/CueEngine tests: burst expansion, count completion at window close, low-count result (not failure), constraint degradation at `hand-broad-type`.

## Non-goals
- Mid-workout reallocation (M33-07); generator selection of burst templates (M35-03); tuning ceiling/floor constants (M36-03).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M32-03 (timeline expansion), M33-02 (matcher count feed), M31-03 (schedule, goal tiers, focus scaling).
- Unblocks: M33-07, M35-03, M36-03.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): count-scored cues reuse the existing cue lifecycle (windows, `gap`) — no new cue or session machine.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Goal-seeking plan mutation with persisted realized stream and adaptation log
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M33 (doc §27 step 11, second half). Goal-seeking is the third plan behavior: when the athlete falls behind or runs far ahead, the engine mutates the remaining plan at safe boundaries — and every mutation is persisted with its inputs and monotonic time, together with the realized token stream, so a stored workout replays what actually happened, never the recipe (D8).

## Design references

- Doc §22 — goal-seeking reallocates the punch budget across remaining rounds, adds/lengthens volume blocks when behind, adds defense/footwork/recovery when far ahead, never inserts a catch-up block exceeding the maximum cadence; §16 — seed/plan reproducibility.
- Spec §8.6 + §19.1 — recalculable from stored data; §17.1 amendment — `workout_adaptations`, `generated_workouts.realized_tokens_json` NOT NULL; §15.1 — decision logic pure.
- Related: M33-05 (`AdaptationDecision`), M33-06 (`allocateRoundTargets`, bursts), M31-09 (`appendAdaptation`), M33-08 (summary reads the realized stream).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/PacingEngine.ts` — goal-seeking branch of `onBoundary` (modify).
- `src/domain/workout/goalAllocation.ts` — reallocation over remaining rounds (modify).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/useWorkoutRunner.ts` — apply decisions to the live timeline; persist (modify).
- Tests alongside each.

### Interfaces
```ts
export interface PlanMutation {
  roundTargets?: number[] // reallocated remaining-round targets
  insertBlocks?: { roundIndex: number; block: WorkoutBlock }[]
  //   volume-burst when behind; defense / footwork / active-recovery when ahead
  lengthenBlocks?: { blockId: string; addMs: number }[]
}
export function applyMutation(workout: GeneratedWorkout, m: PlanMutation): GeneratedWorkout
// pure; touches only not-yet-started rounds/blocks

// Persisted adaptation record (workout_adaptations row, spec §17.1 amendment):
// { id, generated_workout_id, decided_at_monotonic_ms, boundary: 'block' | 'rest' | 'round',
//   inputs_json: PacingSnapshot & { mode, roundIndex }, decision_json: PlanMutation }
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. At each boundary, goal-seeking computes the pacing snapshot (M33-05). Within the tolerance band → `{ kind: 'none' }`.
2. **Behind:** reallocate the remaining budget across remaining `countsTowardGoal` rounds via `allocateRoundTargets`, then add or lengthen volume-burst blocks (M33-06) until the implied pace fits — **never exceeding the configured maximum cadence** (doc §22); if it cannot fit, cap and record `target-unreachable`.
3. **Ahead:** insert defense/footwork calls or active-recovery gaps, honoring the enablement menu — disabled commands never appear, even indirectly (doc §7, §15).
4. Mutations touch only rounds/blocks that have not started; the current cue is never rewritten.
5. Every applied mutation: `WorkoutRepository.appendAdaptation(...)` with `decided_at_monotonic_ms`, `boundary`, `inputs_json`, `decision_json`; `realized_tokens_json` is updated to the post-mutation plan — recalculation replays the realized stream, never the recipe (D8, spec §8.6, §19.1).
6. The mutated plan still passes `validateGeneratedWorkout` (M31-01).

### Data flow
PacingEngine decision → `applyMutation` → runner swaps not-yet-expanded rounds in the CueEngine timeline → `appendAdaptation` + realized-stream update via `WorkoutRepository` (M31-09) → M33-08 summary and history recomputation read only persisted realized data.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Mutations occur only at block/rest/round boundaries and only affect not-yet-started rounds/blocks (doc §22).
- [ ] Behind → targets reallocate and volume blocks are added/lengthened; ahead → defense/footwork/active-recovery inserted, respecting the enablement menu (doc §22, §7).
- [ ] No mutation pushes cadence above the configured maximum; unreachable goals cap with `target-unreachable` (doc §22, §25).
- [ ] Every applied mutation writes a `workout_adaptations` row `{ generated_workout_id, decided_at_monotonic_ms, boundary, inputs_json, decision_json }` (spec §17.1, D8).
- [ ] `realized_tokens_json` always reflects the plan as actually run; replaying a mutated workout reproduces the summary without consulting the recipe (D8, spec §8.6, §19.1).
- [ ] `applyMutation` is pure — the input workout is never mutated — and its result passes `validateGeneratedWorkout` (spec §15.1, M31-01).
- [ ] Inserted tokens never include disabled commands.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- Unit: behind/ahead/within-band scenarios over a fixture workout — mutation shape, cadence cap, enablement respect, purity.
- Integration (in-memory SQLite via the M31-09 harness): scripted behind-pace workout; assert adaptation rows and the final realized stream; recompute and compare.

## Non-goals
- Non-mutating adaptive pacing (M33-05); summary rendering (M33-08); generator-side density planning (M35-03).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M33-05 (`AdaptationDecision`), M33-06 (`allocateRoundTargets`, burst blocks), M31-09 (`appendAdaptation`, realized-stream write).
- Unblocks: none — completes the doc §22 plan behaviors; exercised end-to-end by M36-03.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): persistence records the applied mutation and the full post-mutation realized stream, not a diff — `realized_tokens_json` is the single replay source (D8).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Build workout summary screen and persist cue_results with recalculation test
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M33 (doc §24; capstone of §27 steps 6–11). When a workout finishes, the runner persists everything in one transaction — the `sessions` row, `cue_results`, pending adaptations — and the summary screen renders doc §24 from the persisted realized stream. `workoutSummary.ts` is pure and versioned with its own `calculationVersion` so stored workouts stay recomputable after logic changes. Supersedes #132. On the Phase 5 DoD critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §24 — lead metrics, expandable analysis, the same green/red/gold treatment, save-as-preset / run-again entry points (wired in M36-01).
- Spec §8.5 — velocity-representation disclosure; §8.6 + §19.1 — recalculable from stored data; §17.1 amendment — `cue_results` schema; §4.3 — tracker-reported velocity; §13.3 — hand-sequence match label.
- Related: M33-02 (outcomes), M31-09 (`WorkoutRepository.writeCueResults`), #115 M22-01 (session tables), #117 M22-03 (MetricsEngine owns `session_metrics`), M33-03 (badge), M36-01 (replay).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/programs/workoutSummary.ts` — pure doc §24 computation, own `calculationVersion` (new).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/summary.tsx` — summary route (new).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/useWorkoutRunner.ts` — `finishing` → single-transaction persist (modify).
- `src/domain/programs/__tests__/workoutSummary.test.ts` + golden fixture (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export const WORKOUT_SUMMARY_CALCULATION_VERSION = '1.0.0' // independent of MetricsEngine's (#117)
export interface WorkoutSummaryData {
  totalPunches: number; target: number; grade: RoundGrade; completedRounds: number
  avgVelocity?: number; peakVelocity?: number; velocityRepresentation: string // spec §8.5
  leftRightSplit: { left: number; right: number }; avgRatePerMin: number
  mostProductiveRound: number; bestVelocityRound?: number; connectionCompleteness: number
  handSequenceMatchPercent?: number; extraPunches: number
  perRound: RoundSummary[]; recipeName: string; seed: string; generatorVersion: string
  calculationVersion: string
}
export function computeWorkoutSummary(args: {
  workout: GeneratedWorkout // realized stream, never the recipe (D8)
  cueResults: CueResultRow[]
  adaptations: AdaptationRow[]
}): WorkoutSummaryData
```
`cue_results` columns (spec §17.1 amendment): `session_id`, `generated_workout_id`, `block_id`, `token_index`, `expected_hand`, `expected_type` (nullable), `observed_event_id` (nullable), `outcome` (`matched` | `hand-mismatch` | `type-mismatch` | `missed` | `late` | `during-pause`), `offset_ms` (nullable), `velocity_raw` / `velocity_calibrated` / `velocity_unit` (nullable), `capability_tier`, `decoder_version`, `calculation_version`.

### Behavior
1. On SessionEngine `finishing`, the runner writes in **one transaction** via `WorkoutRepository.writeCueResults` (M31-09): the `sessions` row (`mode = 'puncheokie'`, `generated_workout_id` set), all `cue_results` rows, and any pending `workout_adaptations`. A crash before commit leaves no partial rows.
2. `computeWorkoutSummary` derives every doc §24 lead metric plus the expandable analysis from the realized stream + cue results only. Sequence metrics headline as **hand-sequence match**; broad-type agreement is secondary with caveat text (#131, D4).
3. The summary screen shows the lead metrics; the total-vs-target badge reuses `CountBadge` / `gradeRound` (M33-03); a spec §8.5 disclosure line; expandable sections below. `session_metrics` stays #117's exclusive property — never written here.
4. Golden recomputation: a fixture run is persisted, then the summary recomputed from persisted rows alone must deep-equal the live-run summary.

### Data flow
Runner match outcomes (M33-02) → cue-result accumulation → one-transaction write (M31-09) → `summary.tsx` reads via repository → `computeWorkoutSummary` → render. History recalculation (spec §8.6) reuses the same function keyed by `calculationVersion`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `finishing` persists the `sessions` row (`mode='puncheokie'`, `generated_workout_id`), all `cue_results`, and pending adaptations in a single transaction (spec §17.1, §19.1).
- [ ] `cue_results` columns match the spec §17.1 amendment exactly, including the six `outcome` values and nullable velocity columns.
- [ ] The summary discloses the velocity representation per spec §8.5 (tracker unit / calibrated tracker unit / confirmed physical unit / normalized index).
- [ ] All velocity figures read "tracker-reported velocity" in tracker units (spec §4.3); terminology guard passes.
- [ ] Every sequence-score surface is labeled `hand-sequence match` (D4, spec §13.3); broad-type agreement, if shown, is secondary with caveat text.
- [ ] The total-vs-target badge reuses `CountBadge` with text + icon (doc §24, spec §19.4); no letter grades.
- [ ] Golden test: recomputing the summary from persisted data alone is deep-equal to the live-run summary (spec §8.6, §19.1, D8).
- [ ] `workoutSummary.ts` is pure (spec §15.1) and stamped `WORKOUT_SUMMARY_CALCULATION_VERSION`, independent of #117's metrics version.
- [ ] No `session_metrics` rows are written — #117's MetricsEngine remains the exclusive writer.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- `workoutSummary.test.ts`: lead metrics over a fixture; golden recomputation pinned to `calculationVersion`.
- Repository integration (in-memory SQLite): transaction atomicity — a simulated failure mid-write leaves no partial rows.
- Component: disclosure line, badge, expandable sections render.

## Non-goals
- Save-as-preset and Run This Exact Workout Again (M36-01); CSV/JSON export (#120); the Velocity Lab session summary (#118).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M33-02 (match outcomes), M31-09 (`writeCueResults` single-transaction API), #115 M22-01 (`sessions` tables), #117 M22-03 (`calculation_version` convention; `session_metrics` ownership).
- Unblocks: M36-01.

## Notes
- Decision (do not re-litigate): the summary computes from the realized stream + `cue_results`, never the recipe (D8).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Spike: voice playback latency, audio focus, and Spotify coexistence on tablet
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M34 (doc §27 step 4). Go/no-go spike that decides how the Voice Coach produces sound: whether a cached asset can become audible within a bounded, low-jitter delay of its cue-clock deadline on the Lenovo TB125FU, and how Android audio focus behaves while Spotify plays. Neither `expo-audio` nor `expo-speech` is installed yet (`package.json` has no audio module), so this spike also performs the first audio prebuild + dev-client rebuild.

## Design references

- Doc §18 — the scheduler, not the speech engine, is the master clock; time-critical commands use short cached assets; voice at T−0.75 s, ready tone at T−0.10 s; ducking is a platform focus request, never stream mixing.
- Doc §5 — cached/prerecorded assets for numbers and commands; TTS only for descriptive audio.
- Spec §11.2 — version lock: same Expo SDK 57, dev-client rebuild, known-good APK first (CLAUDE.md rule 5). Spec §14.6 — no overlay of app audio on Spotify by default; never alter the stream. Spec §19.2 — report p95, not averages.
- Related: M34-04 (implements the decision), M34-02/M34-03 (lead-time defaults), M32-05 (sibling tablet spike — share one rebuild), M36-02 (end-to-end sync check).

## Method

### Question

Can `playAsset` on a preloaded cached asset hit its scheduled cue-clock time with jitter ≤ ~100 ms on the tablet, and what are the latency/jitter numbers for `expo-speech` TTS? What exactly happens to Spotify playback when the app requests transient may-duck audio focus?

### Time box

1 day. Go/no-go gate for the M34-04 scheduling path.

### Method

1. Install `expo-audio` + `expo-speech` (SDK 57-compatible), `npx expo prebuild`, rebuild the dev client; keep everything on the spike branch.
2. Throwaway `__DEV__` harness: a 30-rep loop records `performance.now()` at trigger and plays (a) a preloaded `expo-audio` asset, (b) a cold asset, (c) `Speech.speak('one two three two')`, (d) a single spoken number.
3. Measure trigger→audible with an external recording (second phone beside the speaker; inspect the waveform), cross-checked against playback-status callbacks. N ≥ 30 per case; report median, p95, jitter (p95 − median).
4. Repeat (a) while Spotify plays: request transient may-duck focus; note ducking, restore, permanent focus loss, and added latency on the first ducked play.
5. Compare `.m4a`, `.ogg`, `.wav` variants of one asset for start cost.

### Deliverable

`docs/puncheokie-voice-spike.md` with the tables, plus a decision comment answering: asset format; whether numbers must be prerecorded (or TTS is tolerable anywhere time-critical); ducking behavior; GO/NO-GO — if scheduled-asset jitter > ~100 ms, ship Coach Shorthand + tones first and defer Follow-the-Call (doc §18).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Latency table with median/p95/jitter, N ≥ 30 per case: preloaded asset, cold asset, `expo-speech` phrase and single number (doc §18, spec §19.2).
- [ ] Audio-focus findings: transient may-duck request → Spotify ducks and restores; the stream is never altered, recorded, or analyzed (spec §14.6).
- [ ] Decision states asset format and whether numbers must be prerecorded (doc §5, §18).
- [ ] Explicit GO or NO-GO with the > ~100 ms fallback: `coach-shorthand` + tones first, `follow-the-call` deferred (doc §18).
- [ ] Rebuild on the locked Expo SDK 57 with a known-good APK preserved first; module versions recorded (spec §11.2, CLAUDE.md rule 5).
- [ ] `docs/puncheokie-voice-spike.md` committed; `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` passes.
- [ ] Harness stays on the spike branch or behind `__DEV__`; nothing ships in `src/audio/`.

## Test plan

- Manual measurement protocol above, tablet only — never the emulator (CLAUDE.md testing expectations). Record device volume, Spotify account type, and screen state.

## Non-goals

- Production `VoiceOutputExpo` (M34-04), announcer scheduling (M34-03), the D1 settings gate (M34-05), the sync test with Spotify (M36-02).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: none — runs as a parallel fork.
- Unblocks: M34-04 (format + GO/NO-GO); informs M34-02/M34-03 lead-time defaults and M36-02.

## Notes

- Decision already made (do not re-litigate): D3 — the cue clock is the master clock; this spike measures whether audio can follow it, never whether timing should follow audio.
- Native modules ⇒ prebuild + dev-client rebuild; do not upgrade the Expo SDK to chase newer audio modules (rule 5).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Define VoiceOutputPort and VoiceCoachPolicy: modes, vocabulary, priority rules
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M34 (doc §27 step 4). Pure-domain contracts for the Voice Coach: the output port every spoken call goes through, the policy deciding what may be spoken (including the D1 playback gate), and the fixed asset vocabulary. M34-03 plans utterances against these types, M34-04 implements the port, M34-05 persists the policy. Names below are binding — later issues import them verbatim.

## Design references

- Doc §5, §18, §25 — cached assets for time-critical commands, TTS only descriptive; four voice styles; six-level priority order; metric announcements never interrupt a combination; no-voice mode; independent volumes.
- Spec §15.1 — `src/domain/coach/**` imports no React Native, Expo, or `src/audio/**`. Spec §13.5 — D1 gate. Spec §4.3 — tracker-reported velocity, tracker units.
- Related: M31-01 (`WorkoutToken` command unions), M34-03, M34-04, M34-05.

## Method

### Files

- `src/domain/coach/VoiceOutputPort.ts`, `VoiceCoachPolicy.ts`, `vocabulary.ts` (new).
- `src/domain/coach/__tests__/VoiceCoachPolicy.test.ts`, `vocabulary.test.ts` (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
export type VoiceMode = 'off' | 'minimal' | 'standard' | 'full'
export type VoiceStyle = 'call-and-go' | 'follow-the-call' | 'coach-shorthand' | 'minimal'
// Doc §18 order; lower = more urgent.
export const AUDIO_PRIORITY =
  { safety: 0, bell: 1, punchCommand: 2, defenseFootwork: 3, metric: 4, coachingReminder: 5 } as const
export type AudioPriority = (typeof AUDIO_PRIORITY)[keyof typeof AUDIO_PRIORITY]
export type VoiceAssetId =
  | '1' | '2' | '3' | '4' | '5' | '6' | 'body'
  | 'slip' | 'roll' | 'duck' | 'pull' | 'bob-weave'
  | 'pivot' | 'step-off' | 'circle' | 'cut-off-ring' | 'reset'
  | 'go' | 'stop' | 'switch' | 'bell' | 'tone-ready' | 'tone-repeat' | 'tone-warning'
export type ToneKind = 'ready' | 'repeat' | 'warning'
export interface Volumes { voice: number; bells: number; haptics: number } // 0..1
export interface VoiceOutputPort {
  playAsset(id: VoiceAssetId, atMs?: number): void // atMs: monotonic cue-clock deadline
  speak(text: string, priority: AudioPriority): void
  tone(kind: ToneKind): void
  cancel(belowPriority: AudioPriority): void
  setVolumes(v: Volumes): void
}
export interface VoiceCoachPolicy {
  mode: VoiceMode; style: VoiceStyle
  overlayOptIn: boolean // D1 — defaults false
  metricAnnouncements: 'off' | 'periodic' | 'round-summary'
  finalTenSecondWarning: boolean
}
export type SpokenCategory = 'punch-command' | 'stance-change' | 'defense' | 'footwork'
  | 'bell' | 'final-countdown' | 'metric' | 'coaching-reminder'
export function voiceAllowed(p: VoiceCoachPolicy, playbackActive: boolean): boolean
export function shouldSpeak(p: VoiceCoachPolicy, c: SpokenCategory, inCombo: boolean): boolean
export function comboPhraseAssets(tokens: WorkoutToken[]): VoiceAssetId[] // 1-2b-3 -> 1,2,body,3
export function velocityPhrase(kind: 'average' | 'last' | 'peak', value: number): string
```

### Behavior

1. `voiceAllowed` is false when `mode === 'off'` or third-party playback is active without `overlayOptIn` (D1); nothing else opens the gate.
2. `shouldSpeak` maps mode × style × category; `minimal` speaks only stance changes, special commands, round events, metric summaries; `metric`/`coaching-reminder` are always false while `inCombo` (doc §18).
3. `comboPhraseAssets` appends `'body'` after the number for body punches (D10). `velocityPhrase('average', 6.8)` → `"Average velocity six point eight"` — tracker units, never a physical unit (spec §4.3).
4. Nothing here owns time (D3): `atMs` deadlines come from cue-clock timestamps (M34-03); `speak()` is descriptive only, never punch commands.

### Data flow

`CueAnnouncer` (M34-03) evaluates the policy per `CueEvent` and emits port calls → `VoiceOutputExpo` (M34-04). M34-05 persists `VoiceCoachPolicy` and feeds playback status.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AUDIO_PRIORITY` matches doc §18 exactly: safety > bell/final-countdown > stance-change/punch-command > defense/footwork > metric > coaching-reminder.
- [ ] Mode `off` yields no true `shouldSpeak` for any category (doc §25).
- [ ] `voiceAllowed` false whenever playback is active and `overlayOptIn` false; `overlayOptIn` defaults `false` (D1, spec §13.5).
- [ ] `VoiceAssetId` covers exactly 1–6, `body`, five defense, five footwork, `go/stop/switch`, `bell`, three tones (doc §18).
- [ ] `shouldSpeak` false for `metric`/`coaching-reminder` while `inCombo` (doc §18).
- [ ] `comboPhraseAssets` handles `body` suffixes; rejects numbers outside 1–6 (doc §2, D10).
- [ ] `velocityPhrase` says "velocity" in tracker units — never force/energy/a physical unit (spec §4.3).
- [ ] Purity: zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `src/audio/**`, `src/ble/**` under `src/domain/coach/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `VoiceCoachPolicy.test.ts`: gate truth table (playback × optIn × mode); mode×style×category matrix; `inCombo` suppression.
- `vocabulary.test.ts`: `comboPhraseAssets` for `1-2b-3-2`; `velocityPhrase` wording.

## Non-goals

- Scheduling (M34-03), the Expo implementation (M34-04), settings/persistence/playback detection (M34-05).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M31-01 (`WorkoutToken` union — defense/footwork vocabularies stay identical).
- Unblocks: M34-03, M34-04, M34-05.

## Notes

- Decided (do not re-litigate): D1 gate semantics; D3 — the port carries deadlines, never creates them. Prose prefers "rear-hand/heavy punches"; `'power'` stays quoted, `punchType` context only.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement CueAnnouncer scheduling phrases and ready tones against the cue clock
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M34 (doc §27 step 4). `CueAnnouncer` turns `CueEngine` events (M32-04) into `VoiceOutputPort` calls: combo phrases, per-token calls, ready tones, bells, the final-ten-second warning, and deferred metric announcements. Per D3 the cue clock is the master clock — the announcer derives every deadline from the scheduled timestamps carried on `CueEvent`s and never runs a timer of its own, so TTS latency can never shift workout timing.

## Design references

- Doc §18 — voice at T−0.75 s, ready tone at T−0.10 s; prepare several cues ahead; priority preemption; metric announcements never interrupt a combination. Doc §20 — the cue lifecycle events consumed.
- Spec §18.3 — monotonic time only. Spec §15.1 — domain purity.
- Related: M32-04 (`CueEvent`, `SessionPhaseEvent`, `CueTimestamps`), M34-02 (policy/port/vocabulary), M34-05 (wires the announcer in and feeds playback status).

## Method

### Files

- `src/domain/coach/CueAnnouncer.ts` — announcer (new).
- `src/domain/coach/__tests__/CueAnnouncer.test.ts` (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
export interface CueAnnouncerOptions {
  policy: VoiceCoachPolicy
  output: VoiceOutputPort
  leadTimes: { announceMs: number; readyToneMs: number } // defaults 750 / 100 (doc §18); tuned in M36-03
}
export class CueAnnouncer {
  constructor(opts: CueAnnouncerOptions)
  onCueEvent(e: CueEvent): void              // subscribed to CueEngine (M32-04)
  onSessionPhase(e: SessionPhaseEvent): void // bells, pause/resume, cancellation
  onRoundClock(remainingMs: number): void    // final-countdown trigger from the session tick
  announceMetric(text: string): void         // descriptive TTS, e.g. velocityPhrase output
  setPolicy(p: VoiceCoachPolicy): void
  setThirdPartyPlayback(active: boolean): void // D1 input from M34-05
}
```

### Algorithm / state machine

1. Gate first: every entry point returns when `voiceAllowed(policy, playbackActive)` is false (D1). Visuals and haptics never route through the announcer.
2. `cue-previewing` → prepare only, no audio: resolve the phrase plan (`comboPhraseAssets` or `spokenPhrase`) so ≥2 cues are prepared ahead (doc §18).
3. `cue-announcing` → `call-and-go`/`coach-shorthand` play the full phrase as cached assets at `punchCommand` priority; the ready tone is emitted by deadline: `playAsset('tone-ready', timestamps.executionScheduledMs - leadTimes.readyToneMs)`. **The deadline comes from the event's scheduled timestamps — the announcer sets no timers** (D3, spec §18.3).
4. `token-due` → `follow-the-call` speaks each token's asset; `coach-shorthand` plays `tone('repeat')` at each repetition start; `minimal` is silent for punch tokens. Defense/footwork announce at `defenseFootwork`; stance changes and `go/stop/switch` at `punchCommand`; disabled categories are never voiced (doc §7).
5. `onSessionPhase`: `work-entered`/`rest-entered` → `playAsset('bell')`; `paused`/`cancelled` → `cancel(AUDIO_PRIORITY.safety)` so no stale phrase survives; `resumed` re-prepares from the current cue.
6. `onRoundClock`: when `remainingMs` first crosses 10 000 and `finalTenSecondWarning`, play `'tone-warning'` at `bell` priority, once per round (doc §25).
7. `announceMetric`: queue at `metric` priority; **never emitted while a combination is active** — held until the next `gap` or rest; a newer metric supersedes a held one (doc §18).

### Data flow

CueEngine `subscribe` → `onCueEvent`; SessionEngine phase events + tick → `onSessionPhase`/`onRoundClock` (wired by M34-05); port calls → `VoiceOutputExpo` (M34-04). No store or repository writes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Styles match doc §18: `call-and-go`/`coach-shorthand` speak the full phrase on `cue-announcing`; `follow-the-call` speaks per `token-due`; `minimal` announces only stance changes, special commands, round events, metric summaries.
- [ ] Ready-tone deadline equals `executionScheduledMs − readyToneMs` from `CueTimestamps`; no `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`Date.now()` in the announcer (D3, spec §18.3).
- [ ] ≥2 upcoming cue phrases prepared ahead (doc §18).
- [ ] `paused` cancels queued output below safety; nothing queued pre-pause plays after `resumed` (doc §18).
- [ ] Metric announcements deferred while a combination is active; never interrupt one (doc §18, §25).
- [ ] Disabled commands and switched-off categories produce zero port calls (doc §7).
- [ ] With `voiceAllowed` false (playback active, no opt-in) no port call is made at all (D1, spec §13.5).
- [ ] Bells on `work-entered`/`rest-entered`; final-ten-second warning once per round, only when enabled (doc §25).
- [ ] Purity: zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `src/audio/**` under `src/domain/coach/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `CueAnnouncer.test.ts` with a recording fake `VoiceOutputPort` and hand-built `CueEvent`s (until M32-04 merges): phrase plan per style (exact + ×4 repeated combo); ready-tone `atMs` arithmetic; pause/resume flush; metric deferral until `gap`; D1 gate matrix; final-countdown single fire; disabled-category silence.

## Non-goals

- Producing audio (M34-04); settings/persistence/detection (M34-05); cue transitions (M32-04); metric summary content (M33-08).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M34-02 (port, policy, vocabulary — imported verbatim); M32-04 (`CueEvent`/`SessionPhaseEvent`/`CueTimestamps`; until merged, drive tests with hand-made events).
- Unblocks: M34-05.

## Notes

- Decided (do not re-litigate): D3 — deadlines travel in `atMs` from cue-clock timestamps; honoring them is M34-04's job. Defaults `{ announceMs: 750, readyToneMs: 100 }` per doc §18; M36-03 tunes on the bag.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement VoiceOutputExpo: cached assets, TTS fallback, ducking, asset manifest
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M34 (doc §27 step 4). The infrastructure half of the Voice Coach: `VoiceOutputExpo` in `src/audio/` implements the M34-02 `VoiceOutputPort` with preloaded cached assets (`expo-audio`) for time-critical commands and `expo-speech` TTS for descriptive text, plus the asset manifest and Android audio-focus/ducking behavior — built to the format and latency budget the M34-01 spike decided. Adds native modules: `npx expo prebuild` + dev-client rebuild, staying on the locked Expo SDK 57.

## Design references

- Doc §18 — time-critical audio uses deterministic short assets; TTS only descriptive; ducking is a platform focus request; the priority order governs interruption. Doc §25 — independent volumes; usable when voice is unavailable.
- Spec §11.2 — version lock: same Expo SDK 57, dev-client rebuild, known-good APK first (CLAUDE.md rule 5 not violated). Spec §14.6 — never alter/record/analyze Spotify audio; separate stream. Spec §15.1 — infrastructure; domain never imports it.
- Related: M34-01 (format + GO), M34-02 (port contract), M34-05 (instantiates this, owns the D1 gate).

## Method

### Files

- `src/audio/VoiceOutputExpo.ts` — port implementation (new); `src/audio/voiceAssets/manifest.ts` — asset id → module map (new); `assets/voice/*` — clips in the M34-01 format (new).
- `package.json`, `app.config.ts` — add `expo-audio`, `expo-speech` (modify).
- `src/audio/__tests__/manifest.test.ts`, `voiceQueue.test.ts` (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
// src/audio/voiceAssets/manifest.ts
export interface VoiceAssetManifest {
  format: 'm4a' | 'ogg' | 'wav'        // fixed by the M34-01 decision
  assets: Record<VoiceAssetId, number> // require() module ids, one per VoiceAssetId
}
export const voiceAssetManifest: VoiceAssetManifest

// src/audio/VoiceOutputExpo.ts
export class VoiceOutputExpo implements VoiceOutputPort {
  constructor(opts?: { manifest?: VoiceAssetManifest; clock?: () => number })
  preload(): Promise<void>    // load every asset into players before the countdown ends
  readonly available: boolean // false => permanent no-audio mode
  playAsset(id: VoiceAssetId, atMs?: number): void
  speak(text: string, priority: AudioPriority): void
  tone(kind: ToneKind): void
  cancel(belowPriority: AudioPriority): void
  setVolumes(v: Volumes): void
  dispose(): Promise<void>
}
```

### Behavior

1. `preload()` creates one player per manifest asset so `playAsset` starts from memory; a cold play logs a warning via `@diagnostics/logger`.
2. `atMs`: a future monotonic deadline is held and fired on time; a past one plays immediately with lateness logged (safe field). The deadline came from the cue clock (D3) — this class follows it, never feeds timing back.
3. One audible channel with the doc §18 priority order: a more urgent item interrupts; `cancel(belowPriority)` flushes items strictly less urgent; equal priority is FIFO.
4. `speak()` routes to `expo-speech`, descriptive text only — metric readouts in tracker units ("Average velocity six point eight"), round previews, summaries. Punch commands never go through TTS (doc §18, D3).
5. Audio focus: request transient may-duck focus only while audible; abandon when the queue drains. The app plays on its own Android stream and never touches third-party audio (spec §14.6).
6. `setVolumes`: `voice` for speech/number assets, `bells` for bell/tone assets; music volume is never app-controlled beyond OS ducking (doc §25); `haptics` is a no-op here.
7. No-audio mode: failed init or `preload()` rejection sets `available = false`, methods become silent no-ops, one warning logged — the workout continues with visuals and haptics (doc §25).

### Data flow

M34-05's runner constructs and `preload()`s during the countdown → `CueAnnouncer` (M34-03) calls the port during work → players/TTS emit. Diagnostics via `@diagnostics/logger`; no store or SQLite writes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `VoiceOutputExpo` implements `VoiceOutputPort` from M34-02 with no signature drift; `src/domain/**` gains no import of `src/audio/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `voiceAssetManifest.assets` covers every `VoiceAssetId` (1–6, `body`, five defense, five footwork, `go/stop/switch`, `bell`, tones); `manifest.test.ts` fails on a missing id (doc §18).
- [ ] Preloaded `playAsset` trigger→audible on the tablet meets the M34-01 GO budget (jitter ≤ ~100 ms); value posted in the completion comment.
- [ ] Punch commands are only cached assets; `speak()` reachable only from descriptive paths (D3, doc §18).
- [ ] Transient may-duck focus requested only while audible, released after; Spotify ducks and restores; its audio never altered, recorded, or analyzed (spec §14.6).
- [ ] `cancel(belowPriority)` and interruption follow the doc §18 priority order exactly.
- [ ] Independent `voice` and `bells` volumes take effect (doc §25).
- [ ] No-audio mode: with init forced to fail, a simulated workout completes on visuals/haptics with one warning logged (doc §25).
- [ ] `npx expo prebuild` + dev-client rebuild documented; Expo SDK stays 57, locked versions unchanged (spec §11.2, CLAUDE.md rule 5).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- Unit (jest-expo mocks for `expo-audio`/`expo-speech`): manifest completeness; priority interrupt/flush matrix; `atMs` hold-vs-late with a fake clock; no-audio no-ops.
- Manual on tablet (hardware): preload during countdown; ducking with Spotify; volume changes mid-round; forced init failure.

## Non-goals

- What/when to speak (M34-03); the D1 gate, settings, detection (M34-05); professional voice recording — spike-approved generated clips are fine.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M34-01 (format, prerecorded-numbers decision, GO/NO-GO), M34-02 (port types).
- Unblocks: M34-05.

## Notes

- Native modules ⇒ rebuild: preserve a known-good APK first (rule 5); coordinate with M32-05's rebuild if both land the same week. Keep clips short (< 1 s where possible).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Voice Coach settings with Spotify-overlay opt-in (default off) and decision log
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M34 (doc §27 step 4). The user-facing assembly of the Voice Coach: a settings surface for mode, style, volumes, and announcement options; the persisted D1 Spotify-overlay opt-in defaulting OFF; a `ThirdPartyPlaybackDetector` feeding the gate; and the wiring of `CueAnnouncer` + `VoiceOutputExpo` into the live screen (M32-08). This is the policy-gated story — its behavior is what the Phase 7 Spotify policy review (#158) evaluates — and it delivers the Phase 5 DoD clause "when no third-party audio is playing, or after an explicit opt-in — spoken cues".

## Design references

- Doc §5, §18 — voice modes; ducking; usable without voice. Doc §25 — independent volumes for music/voice/bells/haptics, no-voice mode, periodic metric callouts, configurable final-ten-second warning.
- Spec §13.5 — D1 wording (gate, OFF default, label, never auto-enabled). Spec §14.6 — no overlay by default; never alter Spotify audio. Spec §25 — the D1 decision row, already landed by the docs PR; this issue verifies behavior matches it.
- Related: #158 (spec §22 Phase 7 task 10), M32-08, M34-03, M34-04.

## Method

### Files

- `src/app/settings/voice.tsx` — settings screen (new); `src/app/settings/index.tsx` — link row (modify).
- `src/state/useVoiceSettingsStore.ts` — persisted policy + volumes (new); `src/audio/ThirdPartyPlaybackDetector.ts` (new).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/useWorkoutRunner.ts`, `live.tsx` — instantiate output + announcer, feed phase/clock events, show gate status (modify).

### Interfaces

```ts
// src/audio/ThirdPartyPlaybackDetector.ts
export interface ThirdPartyPlaybackDetector {
  isActive(): Promise<boolean> // AudioManager.isMusicActive-style check
  subscribe(listener: (active: boolean) => void): () => void
}
export class AndroidPlaybackDetector implements ThirdPartyPlaybackDetector {}

// src/state/useVoiceSettingsStore.ts (zustand, persisted)
export interface VoiceSettingsState {
  policy: VoiceCoachPolicy // overlayOptIn starts false; only the user's toggle sets it
  volumes: Volumes
  setPolicy(patch: Partial<VoiceCoachPolicy>): void
  setVolumes(v: Volumes): void
}
```

### Behavior

1. Settings: voice mode, style, voice/bell volume sliders + haptics toggle, metric announcement frequency (`off/periodic/round-summary`), final-ten-second warning, and the overlay toggle — its label states plainly that it makes the coach speak over the user's music. Default OFF.
2. Gate: the runner queries the detector at workout start and subscribes for changes; `voiceAllowed(policy, active)` (M34-02) decides. When playback is active without opt-in, the live screen shows a one-line notice of why voice is silent, pointing at settings.
3. Never auto-enabled: `overlayOptIn` is written only by the user's toggle press — never by defaults, migrations, presets, or mode changes.
4. Persistence: policy and volumes survive restarts (zustand persist over the app storage layer; nothing secret, so not SecureStore).
5. Wiring: `useWorkoutRunner` constructs `VoiceOutputExpo`, awaits `preload()` during the countdown, feeds `onSessionPhase`/`onRoundClock` and playback status to `CueAnnouncer`, applies volumes.
6. Voice off is first-class: with mode `off` or the gate closed, the workout is fully usable — visual and haptic cues always retained (doc §18, §25).

### Data flow

Settings ↔ `useVoiceSettingsStore` → runner → announcer/output. Detector → runner → `setThirdPartyPlayback`. No new SQLite tables; nothing about Spotify content is stored beyond the playback boolean.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With no third-party playback active, the Voice Coach is fully available in every mode and style (D1, spec §13.5).
- [ ] With Spotify or any third-party player active, zero app speech unless `overlayOptIn` is true; the toggle defaults OFF (D1, spec §13.5, §14.6).
- [ ] The toggle's label states it speaks over the user's music; `overlayOptIn` is never set true by any code path other than the user's explicit toggle; it persists across restarts (D1, spec §13.5).
- [ ] Voice plays on the app's own Android stream with transient may-duck focus; Spotify audio is never altered, recorded, or analyzed (spec §14.1, §14.6).
- [ ] Shipped behavior matches the spec §25 D1 decision row landed by the docs PR (verify — do not add a new row); a comment linking this issue is posted on #158 for the Phase 7 review (spec §22 Phase 7 task 10).
- [ ] Fully usable with voice off: visual + haptic cues retained in every phase (doc §18, §25).
- [ ] Independent volume controls for voice and bells plus a haptics toggle; music volume never app-controlled beyond OS ducking (doc §25).
- [ ] Final-ten-second warning only when enabled; metric announcements honor the chosen frequency and never interrupt a combination (doc §18, §25).
- [ ] Metric TTS uses tracker units — "Average velocity six point eight" — never force, energy, or a physical unit (spec §4.3); terminology guard passes.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` pass.

## Test plan

- Unit: gate matrix with a fake detector (playback × optIn × mode); store persistence round-trip; runner wiring (announcer receives phase + clock events).
- Component: settings screen mutates the store; toggle label text asserted.
- Manual on tablet (hardware): Spotify playing → silent by default, notice shown; enable toggle → speech + ducking audible; disable mid-workout → silence within one cue; relaunch → toggle retained; no playback → full availability.

## Non-goals

- The formal audio/visual sync protocol with Spotify (M36-02); the policy review itself (#158); announcer/output internals (M34-03, M34-04).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M34-03 (announcer), M34-04 (output + preload), M32-08 (live screen and runner). Related: #158 receives the verification comment.
- Unblocks: M36-02.

## Notes

- Decided (do not re-litigate): D1 gate semantics; D3 — nothing in this wiring derives timing from audio. `AndroidPlaybackDetector` should use an `AudioManager.isMusicActive`-style signal; prefer an `expo-audio` equivalent over a custom native read (check M34-01 notes).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: ComboTemplate contract, seededRandom PRNG, and validated starter combo library
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M35 (doc §27 step 12). This task lays the generator's foundation: the `ComboTemplate` contract, the deterministic seeded PRNG, and a 16-template starter library guarded by `validateLibrary()`. Every later M35 issue builds on these names — `planRounds` (M35-02) filters `COMBO_LIBRARY`, `arrangeBlocks` (M35-03) sequences templates, M35-04 pins determinism, M35-05 grows the library to 40–60 templates. Not on the Phase 5 DoD critical path (the DoD runs on the M31-05 samples), but it gates all of M35.

## Design references

- Doc §15 — the `ComboTemplate` shape (verbatim), the 16 starter combinations, and the library rules `validateLibrary()` enforces.
- Doc §16 — a deterministic seed is stored with the workout; the same recipe + generator version + seed must reproduce the same plan.
- Spec §15.1 — pure TS under `src/domain/workout/`; no React/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports.
- Related: M31-01 (`WorkoutToken`, `parseCombo`/`formatCombo`), M31-02 (beat semantics), M35-02, M35-03, M35-05.

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/ComboTemplate.ts` — the contract (new).
- `src/domain/workout/seededRandom.ts` — mulberry32 PRNG behind a string seed (new).
- `src/domain/workout/comboLibrary.ts` — `COMBO_LIBRARY` (16 templates) + `validateLibrary()` (new).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/{seededRandom,comboLibrary}.test.ts` — see Test plan (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export interface ComboTemplate {          // doc §15 verbatim — do not rename fields
  id: string; name: string; tokens: WorkoutToken[];
  difficulty: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;
  tags: Array<'jab-led' | 'straight' | 'hook' | 'uppercut' | 'body' | 'defense'
    | 'footwork' | 'pressure' | 'counter' | 'switch-safe'>;
  punchCount: number; expectedDurationBeats: number;
  allowedStances: Array<'orthodox' | 'southpaw' | 'either'>;
  requiredEnabledCommands: string[];
  followUpTags?: string[]; forbiddenFollowUpTags?: string[];
}
export interface Rng { next(): number; int(lo: number, hi: number): number;
  pick<T>(arr: readonly T[]): T; shuffle<T>(arr: readonly T[]): T[] }
export function seededRandom(seed: string): Rng   // mulberry32 over a string hash
export const COMBO_LIBRARY: ComboTemplate[]
export interface LibraryViolation { templateId: string; rule: string; detail: string }
export function validateLibrary(library: ComboTemplate[]): LibraryViolation[]
```

### Behavior
1. `seededRandom` hashes the seed string (xmur3 or FNV-1a) into 32-bit state and runs mulberry32. **The same seed yields the same sequence on every platform; `Math.random` never appears under `src/domain/workout/`.**
2. The 16 starter templates (doc §15, lowercase `b` per D10): `1`, `1-2`, `1-1-2`, `1-2-1`, `1-2-3`, `1-2-3-2`, `1-1-2-3`, `1-2-5-2`, `1-2b-3-2`, `1b-2-3-2`, `1-slip-2`, `1-2-roll-3-2`, `1-2-pivot-2`, `1-1-step off-2`, `3b-2-3-2`, `1-6-3-2`. Author punch tokens via `parseCombo` (M31-01) plus hand-tuned `beatOffset`s — offsets are uneven, per the doc §17 `1-2-3-2` example, never equal delays.
3. `validateLibrary()` returns one violation per broken doc §15 rule: `beatOffset`s non-decreasing and within `expectedDurationBeats`; `punchCount` equals the punch tokens present; no stance change inside a combo (stance never appears at token level); no more than two same-side heavy punches in a row unless the template is an explicit drill (contract has no drill flag — mark drills with a `-drill` id suffix and waive only those); every defense token is followed by a plausible counter or reset; `requiredEnabledCommands` lists exactly the commands the tokens use, so a disabled command can never appear indirectly through a template.

### Data flow
`COMBO_LIBRARY` is imported by `roundPlanner.ts` (M35-02) and `blockArranger.ts` (M35-03). `seededRandom(recipe.seed)` is created once per generation by `WorkoutGenerator` (M35-03) and threaded through. `validateLibrary` runs in tests (and as a dev assertion in M35-03), never at workout runtime.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `ComboTemplate` matches doc §15 field-for-field and compiles against the M31-01 `WorkoutToken` union (doc §15, §26).
- [ ] `seededRandom` accepts any string seed; the same seed reproduces the same `next()`/`int()`/`pick()`/`shuffle()` outputs (doc §16).
- [ ] A golden test pins the first 8 `next()` values for a fixed seed so an accidental algorithm change fails loudly (spec §21.1).
- [ ] All 16 doc §15 starter combos exist in `COMBO_LIBRARY` with tags, difficulty, and uneven beat offsets; body punches carry `body: true` and serialize with lowercase `b` via `formatCombo` (D10).
- [ ] `validateLibrary(COMBO_LIBRARY)` returns `[]`, and each rule fires on a deliberately broken fixture template (doc §15).
- [ ] No template can produce a stance change mid-combination (doc §11, §15).
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, `src/ble/**`; no `Math.random` or `Date.now()` under `src/domain/workout/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- Unit `seededRandom.test.ts`: golden first-8 values; `int(lo,hi)` inclusive bounds over 1,000 draws; `shuffle` returns a permutation; seeds differing by one character diverge.
- Unit `comboLibrary.test.ts`: 16 ids present; every template round-trips `formatCombo(parseCombo(...))`; `validateLibrary` clean on the library plus one failing case per rule.

## Non-goals
- Round planning (M35-02), arrangement and `GENERATOR_VERSION` (M35-03), the 40–60 template expansion with `followUpTags` authoring at scale (M35-05).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-01 (`WorkoutToken`, `parseCombo`/`formatCombo`, typed validation errors), M31-02 (beat semantics behind `expectedDurationBeats`).
- Unblocks: M35-02, M35-05.

## Notes
- Decisions (do not re-litigate): D10 — `body: boolean` in data, lowercase `b` in string notation, uppercase B badge only in the visual layer. Mulberry32 is locked here so M35-04's fixtures stay stable.
- Prose and comments say "heavy punches"/"rear-hand punches"; the tracker value keeps its spec §4.3 name, tracker-reported velocity.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement round-theme planner: themes, motif budgets, bias weights, stance modes
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M35 (doc §27 step 12). `planRounds` turns a validated `WorkoutRecipe` plus the round schedule into one `RoundPlan` per round: a theme, a small recurring motif set, hand-bias weights, the round's stance behavior, and defense/footwork call budgets. It is the strategy layer between the recipe (M31-04) and the block arranger (M35-03): the arranger only ever sequences what the plan allows, which is how the doc §7 "controlled variety" and "preference fidelity" goals are enforced structurally.

## Design references

- Doc §16 — the ten-theme catalog and one theme per round; variation through themes and sequencing, not constant novelty.
- Doc §7 — controlled variety, jab-led realism, preference fidelity; §15 — 3–6 recurring motifs per round, no more than two materially new motifs in one round.
- Doc §11 — bias as a generator weight (lead share 58–68 % under lead bias), switch-on-command only at explicit reset points announced "Reset. Switch stance.", never mid-combination.
- Doc §12 — defense/footwork frequency budgets: light ≈ 2–3, moderate ≈ 5–8, heavy ≈ 9–14 calls per round.
- Spec §13.2 — stance vocabulary (D2: `orthodox`/`southpaw`, block-level `switch`).
- Related: M31-03 (`buildRoundSchedule`, `GOAL_TIERS`, focus scaling), M31-04 (`WorkoutRecipe`, `validateRecipe`), M35-01 (`COMBO_LIBRARY`, `Rng`), M35-03 (consumer).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/roundPlanner.ts` — `RoundTheme`, `RoundPlan`, `planRounds` (new).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/roundPlanner.test.ts` — see Test plan (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
export type RoundTheme =
  | 'establish-the-jab' | 'double-jab-entries' | 'straight-punch-volume'
  | 'lead-hook-counters' | 'body-to-head-changes' | 'defense-and-counter'
  | 'footwork-and-exits' | 'switch-stance-fundamentals' | 'pressure-combinations'
  | 'final-high-volume'                          // doc §16 catalog
export interface RoundPlan {
  roundIndex: number
  theme: RoundTheme
  motifs: ComboTemplate[]                        // 3–6 recurring motifs for this round
  newMotifCount: number                          // vs previous round; ≤ 2
  biasWeights: { lead: number; rear: number }    // lead + rear = 1
  stance: 'inherit' | 'orthodox' | 'southpaw' | 'switch'   // BlockStance vocabulary (D2)
  switchOnCommand: boolean                       // stance changes only at reset points
  defenseCallBudget: number
  footworkCallBudget: number
}
export function planRounds(recipe: WorkoutRecipe, schedule: ProgramRound[], rng: Rng): RoundPlan[]
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. Plan only `kind: 'round'` schedule entries; warm-up/cooldown get a fixed technical theme with no new-motif pressure and zero call budgets.
2. Theme assignment (doc §16): early rounds draw jab/straight themes; `defense-and-counter` and `footwork-and-exits` appear only when the recipe enables those command groups; `switch-stance-fundamentals` only under a switch stance mode; the last scored round is `pressure-combinations` or `final-high-volume`. All draws use the passed `rng` — **`planRounds` never creates its own RNG** (doc §16 determinism).
3. Motifs: filter `COMBO_LIBRARY` by `requiredEnabledCommands` ⊆ enabled commands, `allowedStances`, difficulty vs `maximumComboPunches` and complexity, and theme-matching tags; pick 3–6 per round, carrying motifs forward so **no round introduces more than two materially new motifs** (doc §15, §16).
4. Bias weights (doc §11): `balanced` → 0.50/0.50; `lead` → lead share drawn in 0.58–0.68; `rear` mirrored; `left`/`right` resolve through `defaultStance` to lead/rear before weighting.
5. Stance (doc §11, D2): `fixed` → `inherit` every round; `switch-by-round` → alternate `inherit`/`switch`; `switch-on-command` → `switchOnCommand: true`, changes allowed **only at explicit reset points**, surfaced as the "Reset. Switch stance." announcement — never inside a combination.
6. Budgets (doc §12): defense `off` → 0, light → `rng.int(2, 3)`, moderate → `rng.int(5, 8)`, heavy → `rng.int(9, 14)`; footwork identically from `footworkFrequency`. Movement focus biases draws to the top of the band, hands focus to the bottom.

### Data flow
`WorkoutGenerator.generate` (M35-03) calls `validateRecipe` → `buildRoundSchedule` → `planRounds(recipe, schedule, rng)` and hands each `RoundPlan` to `arrangeBlocks`. Plans are intermediate values inside generation; nothing is persisted here.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `RoundTheme` covers exactly the ten doc §16 themes; every scored round receives one theme (doc §16).
- [ ] Every plan carries 3–6 `motifs` and `newMotifCount ≤ 2` relative to the previous round (doc §15, §16).
- [ ] Motifs never require a command the recipe disables — preference fidelity (doc §7, §12).
- [ ] `lead` bias draws lead share within 0.58–0.68; `left`/`right` map through `defaultStance` (doc §11).
- [ ] `switch-on-command` plans permit stance changes only at reset points; no plan can place one inside a combination (doc §11).
- [ ] Defense and footwork budgets land inside the doc §12 bands for every frequency setting.
- [ ] Same `recipe` + same-seeded `Rng` ⇒ deep-equal `RoundPlan[]` (doc §16).
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, `src/ble/**` under `src/domain/workout/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- Unit `roundPlanner.test.ts`: fixed seed × all four durations — themes, motif counts, new-motif ceiling, budget bands; a disabled-defense recipe yields zero defense budget and no defense-tagged motifs; lead-bias draws stay in band over 200 seeds; switch-by-round alternates; determinism deep-equal case.

## Non-goals
- Token/beat sequencing and `GeneratedWorkout` assembly (M35-03); library content (M35-01, M35-05); rendering stance-change cards (M32-06).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M31-04 (`WorkoutRecipe`, `validateRecipe`), M31-03 (`buildRoundSchedule`, `GOAL_TIERS`, focus scaling), M35-01 (`COMBO_LIBRARY`, `Rng`).
- Unblocks: M35-03.

## Notes
- Decisions (do not re-litigate): D2 stance vocabulary; bias is a weight, never a hard filter — a one-hand-only mode is a separate drill type (doc §11).
- Prose and comments say "heavy punches"/"rear-hand punches" (spec §4.3).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement block arranger: constraint-based template selection with beat offsets
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M35 (doc §27 step 12). This story delivers the generator itself: `arrangeBlocks` turns each `RoundPlan` into a beat-timed `WorkoutBlock[]`, and `WorkoutGenerator.generate` assembles the full `GeneratedWorkout` — schedule, `roundPunchTargets`, `expectedTechniqueDistribution`, `estimatedActivePunchesPerMinute`, `warnings` — from a recipe alone. From here the Recipe screen can produce endless valid workouts (M35-06) and replay them exactly (M36-01). Doc §15 is explicit: combinations come from the curated library plus constraints, never from selecting random numbers independently.

## Design references

- Doc §15 — generation rules (jab share, jab-led starts, length tiers, same-side heavy-punch limit, exit/reset after longer heavy combinations); §16 — determinism contract; §17 — beats → ms via the cadence profile; the pace control adjusts punch density, block gaps, and exact-vs-volume proportion together; §7 — no command overload; §26 — `WorkoutRecipe`/`GeneratedWorkout` contracts.
- Spec §14.6 + D3 — cadence BPM is authored by the recipe/generator and scheduled on the monotonic clock; it is never derived from audio, Audio Features, track metadata, or playback position. The workout is identical with music off.
- Related: M35-02 (`planRounds`), M33-06 (`allocateRoundTargets`, volume-burst/open-pressure kinds), M31-01 (`validateGeneratedWorkout`), M31-02 (`beatsToMs`, `blockDurationMs`), M35-04 (test suite), M35-06/M36-01 (consumers).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/blockArranger.ts` — `arrangeBlocks` (new).
- `src/domain/workout/WorkoutGenerator.ts` — `WorkoutGenerator`, `GENERATOR_VERSION` (new).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/blockArranger.test.ts` — see Test plan (new; M35-04 adds the deep suites).

### Interfaces
```ts
export const GENERATOR_VERSION = '1.0.0'   // bump on any behavior change, incl. library changes; stored per D8
export function arrangeBlocks(plan: RoundPlan, recipe: WorkoutRecipe, rng: Rng): WorkoutBlock[]
export class WorkoutGenerator {
  generate(recipe: WorkoutRecipe): GeneratedWorkout   // recipe.seed + GENERATOR_VERSION ⇒ reproducible
}
```

### Algorithm / state machine
1. `generate`: `validateRecipe` (reject on conflicts) → `buildRoundSchedule` → a single `rng = seededRandom(recipe.seed)` → `planRounds` → per round `arrangeBlocks` → assemble `GeneratedWorkout` with `roundPunchTargets` from `allocateRoundTargets` (M33-06). **One `Rng` threaded everywhere; no module ever draws independent random numbers** (doc §15, §16).
2. `arrangeBlocks` fills the round's work interval: select motif templates honoring `followUpTags`/`forbiddenFollowUpTags`, place defense/footwork calls up to the plan budgets, and spend the punch budget across exact-combo, repeated-combo, and (M33-06) volume blocks. Gap beats separate blocks; an exit, reset, or movement beat follows longer heavy-punch combinations (doc §15).
3. Distribution constraints (doc §15): jab share 35–55 % of punches depending on focus; 60–80 % of structured combinations open with a jab or double jab; combo-length tiers — beginner 2–3 punches, intermediate 3–5, 4–8-punch strings only in advanced or pressure blocks; never more than two same-side heavy punches in a row outside explicit drill templates.
4. Pace (doc §17, §10): the cadence profile maps beats to milliseconds via M31-02; the pace control moves density, gaps, and the exact-vs-volume proportion together. **At high punch goals the arranger adds repeated and timed-volume blocks — it never just shrinks every pause until commands become unintelligible.**
5. Preference fidelity (doc §7, §12): templates whose `requiredEnabledCommands` are not all enabled are filtered before selection, so disabled commands cannot appear even indirectly through a template.
6. Outputs: `expectedTechniqueDistribution` (share per punch number plus body share), `estimatedActivePunchesPerMinute`, and `warnings[]` (Extreme-tier warning, movement-focus reductions, constraint-forced deviations). The result must pass `validateGeneratedWorkout` (M31-01).

### Data flow
The Recipe screen (M35-06) and `presets.tsx` (M36-01) call `WorkoutGenerator.generate`; the result is persisted via `WorkoutRepository.saveGeneratedWorkout` (M31-09) with `seed` + `GENERATOR_VERSION` (D8), and expanded by `CueTimeline` (M32-03) at session start.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `generate` is a pure function of `(recipe, GENERATOR_VERSION)`: the same recipe including `seed` yields deep-equal output; changing any field or the seed changes the plan (doc §16).
- [ ] All randomness flows through one `seededRandom(recipe.seed)` `Rng`; no `Math.random` or `Date.now()` under `src/domain/workout/**` (doc §16, spec §18.3).
- [ ] Generated workouts satisfy doc §15: jab share 35–55 %, 60–80 % jab-led combinations, length tiers by complexity, ≤2 same-side heavy punches outside drills.
- [ ] Disabled punches, defenses, footwork, and coach calls never appear, including through templates (doc §7, §12, §15).
- [ ] All token timing derives from `beatOffset` × the authored cadence profile via M31-02 — never from audio or track metadata (doc §17, spec §14.6, D3).
- [ ] Raising `totalPunchGoal` grows volume/repeated blocks instead of eliminating gaps; the Extreme tier emits a `warnings` entry (doc §10, §17).
- [ ] `roundPunchTargets` sums to the goal within the M33-06 tolerance; `estimatedActivePunchesPerMinute` matches the recipe-summary math (doc §26).
- [ ] Output passes `validateGeneratedWorkout`; `recipe.generatorVersion` is stamped from `GENERATOR_VERSION` (doc §26, spec §8.6).
- [ ] Zero React/Expo/SQLite/BLE imports (spec §15.1); `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- Unit `blockArranger.test.ts`: one fixed-seed round per focus — budgets spent, follow-up constraints honored, gap beats present, exit-after-heavy-combination rule; a movement-focus round stays within its reduced punch budget. Determinism and the statistical invariants land in M35-04.

## Non-goals
- The exhaustive determinism/invariant suite and snapshot fixtures (M35-04); library growth (M35-05); Recipe-screen wiring (M35-06); adaptive mutation of a running plan (M33-07).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M35-02 (`planRounds`, `RoundPlan`), M33-06 (`allocateRoundTargets`, volume-burst/open-pressure block kinds).
- Unblocks: M35-04, M35-06, M36-01.

## Notes
- Decisions (do not re-litigate): D3 (cadence authored, never derived from audio); D8 (persist seed + `GENERATOR_VERSION` + realized stream); D10 (`b` notation).
- Prose says "heavy punches"/"rear-hand punches"; `'power'` appears only quoted as the vendor `punchType` classification (spec §4.3).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Generator determinism and invariant tests: seeds, disabled commands, jab share
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M35 (doc §27 step 12). The generator's promises — determinism, preference fidelity, realistic distributions — are contracts that later work relies on (exact replay in M36-01, recalculation per spec §8.6). This task turns them into an executable suite: property-style invariant tests over many seeds plus snapshot fixtures pinned to `GENERATOR_VERSION`, in the mold of the golden-byte pin tests in `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/__tests__/FightCampV1Decoder.test.ts`.

## Design references

- Doc §16 — "The same recipe, generator version, and seed must reproduce the same plan"; supports replay, debugging, sharing, comparison across decoder versions.
- Doc §15 — the generation rules under test (jab share, jab-led starts, length tiers, same-side heavy-punch limit, motif rules); §7 — preference fidelity.
- Spec §21.1 — unit tests for pure domain functions; the decoder golden tests are the house pattern for pinned fixtures; the suite must run on Windows without Bluetooth hardware.
- Related: M35-03 (system under test), M35-01 (`seededRandom`), M35-05 (library growth strengthens coverage), M36-01 (replay relies on these guarantees).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/WorkoutGenerator.determinism.test.ts` — seed reproduction + fixture pinning (new).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/WorkoutGenerator.invariants.test.ts` — statistical and structural invariants (new).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/fixtures/generated/*.json` — snapshot fixtures, one per pinned recipe, each embedding the `GENERATOR_VERSION` that produced it (new).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/fixtures/regenerate.ts` — the only writer of those fixtures; run deliberately, never in CI (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
// test helpers only — no production exports
export function recipeMatrix(): WorkoutRecipe[]   // pinned recipes: 4 durations × focus × stance modes × frequencies
export function collectStats(w: GeneratedWorkout): {
  jabShare: number; jabLedShare: number; maxComboLength: number
  maxSameSideHeavyRun: number; commandsUsed: Set<string>; motifCountPerRound: number[]
}
```

### Behavior
1. **Determinism:** for each matrix recipe and 100 distinct seeds, `generate` runs twice and the results are deep-equal; different seeds produce different plans; `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(w))` round-trips losslessly (the persistence path in M31-09 depends on it).
2. **Invariants per generated workout:** commands used ⊆ enabled commands — a disabled punch, defense, footwork, or coach call never appears, even via a template; jab share within 35–55 %; 60–80 % of structured combinations jab-led; combo lengths within the tier for the recipe's complexity (2–3 / 3–5 / 4–8 only advanced-pressure); ≤2 same-side heavy punches in a row outside drill templates; 3–6 motifs per round with ≤2 new; `roundPunchTargets` sums to the goal within the M33-06 tolerance; the workout passes `validateGeneratedWorkout` (M31-01).
3. **Snapshot fixtures:** a handful of pinned recipes store their full `GeneratedWorkout` as JSON. The test asserts deep equality against the fixture **and** that the fixture's embedded version equals `GENERATOR_VERSION`. **Bumping `GENERATOR_VERSION` fails the suite until fixtures are regenerated deliberately via `regenerate.ts`** — a silent behavior change can never ride along (spec §8.6). Library edits that change output (M35-05) also require a bump plus regeneration.

### Data flow
CI-only. Fixtures live beside the tests, mirroring `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/fixtures/`; `regenerate.ts` is the single writer and its header documents the regeneration procedure.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Same `recipe` + `GENERATOR_VERSION` + `seed` ⇒ deep-equal `GeneratedWorkout`, verified over 100 seeds per matrix recipe (doc §16).
- [ ] Disabled commands never appear in any generated workout across the matrix × seeds (doc §7, §12, §15).
- [ ] Jab share stays within 35–55 % and jab-led share within 60–80 % across the matrix (doc §15).
- [ ] Length tiers, the same-side heavy-punch limit, and motif rules (3–6 per round, ≤2 new) hold everywhere (doc §15, §16).
- [ ] Snapshot fixtures embed their `GENERATOR_VERSION`; a version bump without regenerated fixtures fails CI, and regeneration is documented in the test-file header (spec §8.6, §21.1).
- [ ] The suite runs on Windows without Bluetooth hardware and finishes in reasonable CI time — size the seed loops accordingly (spec §21.1).
- [ ] Test helpers import nothing from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, `src/ble/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- This issue *is* the test plan. Named cases: `reproduces deep-equal workouts across 100 seeds`, `never emits disabled commands`, `keeps jab share in band`, `keeps combinations jab-led in band`, `respects combo-length tiers`, `limits same-side heavy runs`, `keeps motif budgets`, `sums round targets to goal`, `fixture matches GENERATOR_VERSION`, `fixture version bump requires regeneration`.

## Non-goals
- Fixing generator behavior (findings go to M35-03/M35-05 follow-ups); library-wide authoring stats (M35-05); runtime performance benchmarks.

## Dependencies
