- Blocked by: M35-03 (`WorkoutGenerator`, `GENERATOR_VERSION`, `arrangeBlocks`).
- Unblocks: none directly — M36-01 replay and M35-06 rely on the guarantees this suite pins.

## Notes
- Follow the FightCampV1Decoder golden-test pattern: fixtures are evidence; regenerating them is a deliberate, reviewed act.
- Stats prose says "heavy punches"; the tracker value keeps its spec §4.3 name, tracker-reported velocity.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Expand combo library to 40–60 tested templates with follow-up constraints
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M35 (doc §27 step 12). Doc §27 gates the procedural generator on "a curated library of approximately 40–60 tested combo templates". M35-01 shipped the 16 starters; this task grows `COMBO_LIBRARY` to 40–60 templates covering every tag, authors `followUpTags`/`forbiddenFollowUpTags` so the arranger can chain templates plausibly, and adds a library-wide statistics test so the pool itself cannot drift out of the doc §15 bands.

## Design references

- Doc §15 — the template contract, generation rules, and follow-up constraints; repetition is part of the training experience.
- Doc §27 step 12 — the generator is only as good as its curated library; expansion precedes heavy reliance on procedural output.
- Related: M35-01 (contract, `validateLibrary`), M35-02/M35-03 (consumers), M35-04 (fixtures must be regenerated when the pool changes output).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/comboLibrary.ts` — extend `COMBO_LIBRARY` to 40–60 templates (modify).
- `src/domain/workout/__tests__/comboLibrary.stats.test.ts` — library-wide statistics (new).

### Interfaces
```ts
// no new exports — the library grows behind the M35-01 surface
export const COMBO_LIBRARY: ComboTemplate[]   // 40–60 entries after this issue
```

### Behavior
1. Author the remaining templates across all doc §15 tags — `'jab-led'`, `'straight'`, `'hook'`, `'uppercut'`, `'body'`, `'defense'`, `'footwork'`, `'pressure'`, `'counter'`, `'switch-safe'` — and all five difficulty levels, using `parseCombo` notation (lowercase `b`, D10) plus hand-tuned, uneven `beatOffset`s (doc §17).
2. Every template obeys `validateLibrary()` (M35-01): no stance changes inside combos, ≤2 same-side heavy punches in a row outside explicit drills, defense followed by a plausible counter or reset, `requiredEnabledCommands` exactly matching the tokens, and an exit/reset/movement beat after longer heavy-punch strings.
3. Author `followUpTags`/`forbiddenFollowUpTags` deliberately: defense templates prefer `'counter'` follow-ups; `'pressure'` strings demand a reset or footwork follow-up; body-commit templates may forbid an immediate `'uppercut'` chain. These constraints are what M35-03's `arrangeBlocks` consumes when sequencing.
4. The stats test treats the library as data under test: tag coverage, difficulty spread, jab-led share of multi-punch templates, punch-count tiers represented, unique ids, and no orphan follow-up tags (every referenced tag exists on at least one template).

### Data flow
Consumed by `planRounds` (motif selection) and `arrangeBlocks` (sequencing/chaining). No runtime code changes — a richer pool simply widens what a seed can produce. Because output for existing seeds changes, this lands with a `GENERATOR_VERSION` bump and deliberate M35-04 fixture regeneration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `COMBO_LIBRARY.length` is between 40 and 60 with unique `id`s; `validateLibrary(COMBO_LIBRARY)` returns `[]` (doc §15).
- [ ] Every tag has ≥3 templates and every difficulty 1–5 is represented (doc §15).
- [ ] ≥60 % of multi-punch templates open with a jab or double jab so the arranger can hold the 60–80 % jab-led band without starving (doc §15).
- [ ] Every `followUpTags`/`forbiddenFollowUpTags` value names an existing tag; at minimum the `'defense'` and `'pressure'` templates carry follow-up constraints (doc §15).
- [ ] Beginner (2–3), intermediate (3–5), and advanced/pressure (4–8) punch-count tiers are all populated (doc §15).
- [ ] String notation uses lowercase `b`; body punches carry `body: true` (D10).
- [ ] `GENERATOR_VERSION` is bumped and the M35-04 snapshot fixtures are regenerated deliberately in the same PR (spec §8.6).
- [ ] Library data stays pure TS with no new imports (spec §15.1); `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- Unit `comboLibrary.stats.test.ts`: named cases `has 40-60 valid templates`, `covers every tag and difficulty`, `keeps jab-led majority`, `has no orphan follow-up tags`, `keeps punch-count tiers populated`, `ids are unique`. Re-run `WorkoutGenerator.invariants.test.ts` (M35-04, if landed) as the integration check against the expanded pool.

## Non-goals
- Contract or validator changes (M35-01); arranger logic (M35-03); bag-tested timing constants (`tuning.ts` is tuned in M36-03).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M35-01 (`ComboTemplate`, `COMBO_LIBRARY`, `validateLibrary`).
- Unblocks: none directly — M35-03 output quality and M35-04 coverage improve immediately.

## Notes
- Repetition is deliberate: rounds recycle 3–6 motifs (doc §15, §16); author families of related templates rather than 60 novelties.
- Template names and comments say "heavy punches"/"rear-hand punches" (spec §4.3).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Wire WorkoutGenerator into the Recipe screen with Surprise Me and warnings
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M35 (doc §27 step 12). Until now the Recipe screen (M31-06/M31-07) starts workouts from the hand-authored samples (M31-05). This task wires `WorkoutGenerator.generate` in behind the same Start flow: the tuned recipe drives generation, generator `warnings` surface before start, Surprise Me draws a fresh seed within the saved constraints, and the seed is visible on the summary card so a workout can be identified and re-run later (M36-01).

## Design references

- Doc §8 — the Recipe Summary shown before start; save, duplicate, and Surprise Me honoring saved constraints.
- Doc §16 — the seed is stored with the workout; the same recipe + generator version + seed reproduces the plan.
- Related: M31-06/M31-07 (screen + advanced panel + conflict rendering), M31-05 (samples remain), M35-03 (generator), M31-09 (persistence), M36-01 (re-run).

## Method

### Files
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/recipe.tsx` — generate on Start, warnings list, Surprise Me button (modify).
- `src/components/workout/RecipeSummaryCard.tsx` — add seed, `estimatedActivePunchesPerMinute`, and a technique-distribution line (modify).
- `src/state/useWorkoutStore.ts` — hold the last `GeneratedWorkout`; regenerate on recipe change or Surprise Me (extend).

### Interfaces
```ts
// store slice additions (consumed by live.tsx via useWorkoutRunner)
export interface RecipeGenerationSlice {
  generated?: GeneratedWorkout
  generateFromRecipe(recipe: WorkoutRecipe): void   // stamps GENERATOR_VERSION, keeps recipe.seed
  surpriseMe(): void                                // fresh random seed, same constraints
  selectSample(id: string): void                    // M31-05 samples still selectable
}
```

### Behavior
1. Start-from-recipe calls `WorkoutGenerator.generate(recipe)` in the store; generation is synchronous pure domain code and the screen never reaches into generator internals (spec §15.1 direction).
2. Generator `warnings` render as an inline list above Start (Extreme-tier warning, movement-focus goal reduction, constraint-forced deviations) and are never silently dropped; `validateRecipe` conflicts from M31-07 still block Start — warnings do not.
3. Surprise Me: the app layer draws a fresh seed (e.g. `expo-crypto` random UUID — the domain never self-seeds), keeps every other recipe field, regenerates, and refreshes the summary card. Repeated taps keep producing new plans that honor the same constraints (doc §8).
4. `RecipeSummaryCard` shows the seed (shortened, with a copy affordance), `estimatedActivePunchesPerMinute`, and the technique-distribution line derived from `expectedTechniqueDistribution` (doc §8).
5. The M31-05 samples remain selectable and bypass generation; the store records which path produced `generated` so the summary and persistence stay truthful.

### Data flow
Recipe controls → store recipe slice → `generateFromRecipe` → `GeneratedWorkout` in store → `RecipeSummaryCard` + Start → `useWorkoutRunner` (M32-08) → persisted via `saveGeneratedWorkout` (M31-09) with `seed` + `GENERATOR_VERSION` (D8).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Starting from a tuned recipe runs a generated workout end-to-end on the simulated source (doc §8, §16).
- [ ] Samples from `listSampleWorkouts()` are still selectable and start unchanged (doc §8).
- [ ] `warnings` are visible before start; `validateRecipe` conflicts still block Start while warnings never do (doc §12).
- [ ] Surprise Me produces a different plan each tap while honoring every enablement; disabled commands never appear (doc §7, §8).
- [ ] The seed and `estimatedActivePunchesPerMinute` appear on `RecipeSummaryCard`; the persisted row carries `seed` + `GENERATOR_VERSION` (doc §16, spec §8.6).
- [ ] Seed creation lives in the app layer; `src/domain/workout/**` gains no RN/Expo imports and never self-seeds (spec §15.1).
- [ ] Summary text says "punches/minute" and, wherever velocity appears, "tracker-reported velocity" (spec §4.3); the terminology guard passes.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan
- Component tests (jest-expo): `generateFromRecipe`/`surpriseMe` produce valid workouts and change only the seed; the warnings list renders; the sample path bypasses generation; `RecipeSummaryCard` snapshot includes the seed line.
- Manual on tablet: tune a recipe, tap Surprise Me three times (three distinct plans), start, and confirm the live screen runs the generated plan.

## Non-goals
- Saved presets and Run This Exact Workout Again (M36-01); adaptive mutation of a running plan (M33-07); library growth (M35-05).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: M35-03 (`WorkoutGenerator`, `GENERATOR_VERSION`, `warnings`), M31-07 (advanced panel and inline conflict rendering).
- Unblocks: none directly — M36-01 depends on M35-03 but gains its user-facing seed handle here.

## Notes
- Decisions (do not re-litigate): D8 — persist recipe params, `generator_version`, `seed`, and the realized token stream; the summary-card seed is the user-facing handle for replay.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Saved recipe presets and Run This Exact Workout Again with seed reuse
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M36 (doc §27 step 13). Delivers the preset library (`presets.tsx`) and exact replay: summary and history offer "Run This Exact Workout Again" (doc §24), reusing the stored `seed` + `generator_version` and replaying the persisted realized stream — never regenerating from the recipe (D8). Closes the Phase 5 DoD re-run clause.

## Design references

- Doc §8 — save/duplicate named presets; §16 — recipe + generator version + seed reproduces the plan; §24 — summary shows recipe + seed and offers exact re-run.
- Spec §8.6 — history recalculates with newer versions without altering original data.
- Related: M31-09 (`WorkoutRepository`), M33-08 (summary), M35-03 (`generatorVersion`), M35-06 (Surprise Me).

## Method

### Files
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/presets.tsx` — preset screen (new); `_layout.tsx` entry, `summary.tsx` re-run action (modify).
- `src/storage/repositories/WorkoutRepository.ts` — preset CRUD + `rerunExactWorkout` (extend); `src/state/useWorkoutStore.ts` — presets slice + pending re-run (extend).

### Interfaces
```ts
// src/storage/repositories/WorkoutRepository.ts (extends M31-09)
export class WorkoutRepository {
  listRecipes(): Promise<Array<{ id: string; name: string; updatedAt: string }>>
  saveRecipe(recipe: WorkoutRecipe, name: string): Promise<string>
  duplicateRecipe(recipeId: string, newName: string): Promise<string>
  renameRecipe(recipeId: string, newName: string): Promise<void>
  deleteRecipe(recipeId: string): Promise<void>   // never cascades
  rerunExactWorkout(generatedWorkoutId: string): Promise<RerunPlan>
}
export type RerunPlan =
  | { kind: 'exact'; workout: GeneratedWorkout }
  | { kind: 'version-drift'; workout: GeneratedWorkout;
      stored: { seed: string; generatorVersion: string }; currentGeneratorVersion: string }
```

### Behavior
1. `presets.tsx` lists presets with `summarizeRecipe` lines (M31-04); selecting one loads `recipe.tsx`.
2. `rerunExactWorkout` loads the stored `generated_workouts` row. **The stored realized stream is authoritative — never re-expanded from the recipe** (D8).
3. On drift (stored ≠ current `generatorVersion`) a warning names both versions and offers: run the stored plan exactly (default) or regenerate with the current generator. **Never regenerate silently.**
4. Preset delete leaves `generated_workouts`/`cue_results` untouched (spec §8.6).

### Data flow
Summary/history → `rerunExactWorkout` → `useWorkoutStore` → the same `useWorkoutRunner` path as a fresh generation; screens reach the repository only through the store (spec §15.1).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `presets.tsx` supports save/duplicate/rename/delete with `summarizeRecipe` lines; delete asks for confirmation (doc §8, spec §19.4).
- [ ] Preset CRUD round-trips through `workout_recipes` preserving `recipe_schema_version` (spec §17.1).
- [ ] Summary and history offer `Run This Exact Workout Again` using stored `seed`, `generator_version`, and `realized_tokens_json` — never a fresh generation (doc §24, D8).
- [ ] Re-running the same `generatedWorkoutId` twice yields deep-equal token streams (doc §16).
- [ ] On version drift a warning names both versions and offers exact replay (default) or regenerate-with-current (doc §16, spec §8.6).
- [ ] Deleting a preset never deletes `generated_workouts` or `cue_results` rows (spec §8.6).
- [ ] No React/Expo/SQLite imports under `src/domain/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] Velocity reads "tracker-reported velocity"; sequence scores read **hand-sequence match** (spec §4.3, §13.3, D4).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `WorkoutRepository.presets.test.ts` (in-memory SQLite): CRUD round-trip; exact re-run returns the stored stream; drift flagged with an injected version; delete keeps workout rows.
- Component test: drift warning shows both versions and two actions.

## Non-goals

- Generator changes (M35-03), Surprise Me (M35-06), summary computation (M33-08), CSV/JSON export (later phase).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M31-09 (repository + tables), M33-08 (summary + persisted rows), M35-03 (`generatorVersion` + regenerate path).
- Unblocks: the Phase 5 DoD re-run clause (checked in the M36-03 go/no-go).

## Notes

- Decision (do not re-litigate): exact re-run replays the stored realized stream; regeneration only as an explicit choice after the drift warning (D8).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Audio/visual sync test with Spotify playing in the background
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M36 (doc §27 step 14). A documented, repeatable test protocol — in the controlled-scenario style of `docs/protocol/README.md` — measuring voice/visual cue alignment and audio-focus behavior while Spotify plays in the background, in both states of the D1 overlay toggle. Results land in `docs/puncheokie-validation.md` and feed the Phase 7 Spotify policy review (#158) (spec §14.6).

## Design references

- Doc §18 — the scheduler, not the speech engine, is the master clock; ducking allowances; the timing example (preview T−1.50 s, voice T−0.75 s, tone T−0.10 s) defines "aligned".
- Spec §14.6 — timeline independent of track timing; no app-audio overlay by default. Spec §21.5 — Spotify offline tests.
- D1 — overlay toggle defaults OFF, never auto-enabled; D3 — cadence never derived from audio.
- Related: M34-05 (opt-in), M32-08 (live screen), #142 (deep link), #158 (policy review).

## Method

### Files
- `docs/puncheokie-validation.md` — new section "Audio/visual sync with Spotify": protocol + recorded results (create the file if M36-03 has not already; each issue owns its section). No `src/**` changes.

### Interfaces
No exports introduced. Consumed: `CueTimestamps` scheduled-vs-actual fields on `CueEvent` (M32-04) via a `__DEV__` log; the M34-05 overlay toggle; a screen recording with a visible clock.

### Protocol
1. Setup: Lenovo TB125FU with the M34-05 dev-client build; both FightCamp v1 trackers worn blue = left, red = right (simulated source acceptable where punches are irrelevant); Spotify test playlist via the #142 deep-link path.
2. Baseline (no Spotify): run `Three-Round Fundamentals`, voice Standard; measure spoken-phrase onset vs token activation vs `voiceScheduledMs` for ≥20 cues; record median/p95.
3. Toggle OFF (default): start playback, then the workout. Toggle reads OFF on a fresh install; no app-generated audio overlays playback; visuals/haptics match the baseline.
4. Toggle ON: explicit opt-in (label states it speaks over the music, never pre-enabled). Repeat the alignment run; record ducking (transient may-duck focus, recovery after each phrase); playback never paused, skipped, or altered.
5. Timeline independence (D3): identical recipe + seed across music-off / OFF / ON — identical cue schedules. Pause/seek/skip the track mid-round: zero effect on cue timing.
6. Edge cases (spec §21.5): playback stops mid-round; Spotify offline — workout continues undisturbed.
7. Repeat every scenario ≥3 times; record results tables (median/p95 ms, ducking, anomalies) with device build, app commit, voice-asset version.

### Data flow
Recordings/logs → results tables in the doc → findings comment on #158; defects are filed against M34, not fixed here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/puncheokie-validation.md` contains "Audio/visual sync with Spotify" with the full protocol and results, ≥3 repetitions per scenario (doc §27 step 14).
- [ ] Alignment measured over ≥20 cues per run against `voiceScheduledMs`/`voiceActualMs`; median and p95 reported (doc §18).
- [ ] Toggle OFF (default): fresh install shows OFF, no app audio overlays playback, visuals and haptics unaffected (D1, spec §14.6).
- [ ] Toggle ON: explicit opt-in path recorded; ducking and recovery described; playback never paused or altered (doc §18, D1).
- [ ] Identical cue schedules in all three audio states; Spotify pause/seek/skip, playback stop, and offline leave cue timing and the workout undisturbed (D3, spec §14.6, §21.5).
- [ ] Findings summarized in a comment on #158 linking the doc section — measured behavior only, no policy conclusions (spec §14.6).
- [ ] Hardware steps executed on the Lenovo TB125FU; tracker identity recorded where worn (blue = left, red = right).
- [ ] The doc section says "tracker-reported velocity" wherever velocity appears; `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` passes (spec §4.3).

## Test plan

- Manual/hardware only — this issue is itself a test protocol. Raw recordings stay under git-ignored `captures/`; only results tables are committed.

## Non-goals

- Fixing latency/ducking defects (file against M34-04/M34-05); beat alignment or audio analysis of any kind (D3); the bag protocol (M36-03); the policy review itself (#158).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M34-05 (overlay opt-in on device), M32-08 (live screen), #142 (Spotify playback launched from Puncheokie).
- Unblocks: #158 (Phase 7 policy review input).

## Notes

- Decisions (do not re-litigate): the toggle defaults OFF and is never auto-enabled (D1); the workout clock never derives from audio (D3).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Bag-testing protocol to tune graces, windows, cadence, and density ceilings
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M36 (doc §27 step 15). On-bag sessions with both trackers replace the design's provisional timing numbers with evidence-backed constants in `src/domain/workout/tuning.ts`: window graces, lead times, cadence maxima, density ceilings. Also the Phase 5 go/no-go: the spec §22 DoD is walked on the bag and signed off or bounced back with filed issues.

## Design references

- Doc §6 — window `[cueStart − graceBefore, cueEnd + graceAfter]`; §17 — profiles (technical 80–90 … sprint 130–150 BPM); §18 — untested lead defaults (1.50 / 0.75 / 0.10 s).
- Spec §21.4 — the punch test list this adapts; §18.2 — accepted events fall inside work; §22 — Phase 5 DoD.
- Related: M32-03/M32-04 (windows, leads), M33-02 (matching), M33-05 (maxima), M31-03/M35-03 (density warnings), M36-01 (re-run).

## Method

### Files
- `src/domain/workout/tuning.ts` + `__tests__/tuning.test.ts` — tuned constants with evidence comments (new).
- `docs/puncheokie-validation.md` — section "Bag-testing protocol" (create if M36-02 has not).
- Call sites switch to `TUNING`: `CueTimeline.ts`, `CueEngine`/`CueAnnouncer`, `PacingEngine.ts`, `punchGoals.ts`, `WorkoutGenerator.ts` (modify).

### Interfaces
```ts
// src/domain/workout/tuning.ts — tuned timing constants (pure TS); doc §18 lead defaults
// 1500/750/100 ms until tuned. Each value carries an evidence comment (bag session + date).
export type CadenceProfileId = 'technical' | 'steady' | 'pressure' | 'sprint'
export interface TuningConstants {
  graceBeforeMs: number
  graceAfterMs: number
  previewLeadMs: number
  announceLeadMs: number
  readyToneMs: number
  cadenceMaxBpmByProfile: Record<CadenceProfileId, number>
  densityCeilingPerMinByProfile: Record<CadenceProfileId, number>  // active punches/min
}
export const TUNING: TuningConstants
```

### Protocol
Per `docs/protocol/README.md` rules: one variable at a time, ≥3 repetitions, evidence recorded. Setup: Lenovo TB125FU dev-client at the heavy bag; both FightCamp v1 trackers worn blue = left, red = right; `Three-Round Fundamentals` plus a pressure recipe; screen-record with a visible clock.
1. 10 alternating punches on a steady 1-2 block — event times vs window edges size the graces.
2. Rapid combination at pressure cadence — do honest final punches fall outside `windowEnd + graceAfter`?
3. Strike during rest and during pause — events persist raw but match no cue (spec §18.2).
4. Orthodox vs switch sequence — hand mapping and the **hand-sequence match** label hold (D4).
5. Cadence ramp per profile → `cadenceMaxBpmByProfile`; density ramp on volume blocks → `densityCeilingPerMinByProfile`.
6. Gloved lead-time check per profile — adjust the three lead values.
7. Go/no-go: walk the spec §22 Phase 5 DoD end-to-end on the bag (including the M36-01 re-run); record pass/fail per clause.

### Data flow
Bag sessions → doc results tables → `TUNING` → CueTimeline, CueEngine/CueAnnouncer, PacingEngine, punchGoals, WorkoutGenerator; verdict → issue comment + epic #6.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/puncheokie-validation.md` gains "Bag-testing protocol": every adapted spec §21.4 scenario run on the Lenovo TB125FU with both trackers blue = left / red = right, ≥3 repetitions, captures exported, results recorded (spec §21.4).
- [ ] `TUNING` exported with all seven fields and per-value evidence comments citing session + date (doc §6, §17, §18).
- [ ] `graceBeforeMs`/`graceAfterMs` set from measured offsets; `CueTimeline` uses them, windows stay clamped to work (doc §6, spec §18.2).
- [ ] Lead times replace the doc §18 defaults at CueEngine/CueAnnouncer; `cadenceMaxBpmByProfile` bounds every PacingEngine adjustment; `densityCeilingPerMinByProfile` drives the Extreme (M31-03) and generator (M35-03) warnings (doc §10, §17, §18).
- [ ] Strikes during rest/pause persist raw but never match a cue (spec §18.2, CLAUDE.md rule 1); scoring reads **hand-sequence match**, velocity reads "tracker-reported velocity" (D4, spec §4.3).
- [ ] Go/no-go verdict on the Phase 5 DoD recorded in the doc and as an issue comment, issues filed for failing clauses (spec §22).
- [ ] `tuning.ts` imports no React/Expo/SQLite/BLE (spec §15.1); `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `tuning.test.ts`: shape complete; graces positive and below the smallest inter-cue gap; maxima within doc §17 bands or explicitly justified; ceilings monotonic across profiles.
- Manual: the protocol above; M32-09/M35-04/M33-08 suites re-run green after the constant switch.

## Non-goals

- Matcher changes (#130/M33-02), pacing algorithm (M33-05), generator constraints (M35-03), voice fixes (M34), Spotify sync (M36-02).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M33-02 (live matching on the bag), M33-04 (rest phases for scenario 3), M33-06 (volume blocks for the density ramp).
- Unblocks: Phase 5 DoD sign-off (go/no-go).

## Notes

- Decision (do not re-litigate): tuned constants live in this one module; consumers never hard-code timing literals.
- If a tuned value changes generator output, bump `generatorVersion` and regenerate the M35-04 fixtures (doc §16); the DoD re-run step needs M36-01 landed.
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Define confirmation contracts, confidence tiers, and the haptic vocabulary
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M37 (doc §28). Establishes the pure contracts every other M37 issue imports: the outcome of resolving one strike against the expected tokens, the four-cue haptic vocabulary, the five plausibility signals, and the four confidence tiers. Nothing here computes or renders — it fixes the vocabulary so the scorer (M37-02), the live screen (M37-04), the border (M37-05), the gratification layer (M37-06), and persistence (M37-07) cannot drift. On the M37 critical path; everything else in this milestone is blocked by it.

## Design references

- Doc §28.2 — per-strike resolution rules and the haptic table (`confirm`, `extra`, `combo-complete`, `streak`).
- Doc §28.4 — the five signals (`handOrder`, `timing`, `separation`, `intensity`, `exclusivity`) and the tier thresholds.
- Doc §28.6 / D11 — confidence, signals and `CONFIDENCE_VERSION` persist so results recompute; signals the tier cannot supply are omitted, never zeroed.
- Doc §3 / D4 — the tier vocabulary and the **hand-sequence match** label discipline.
- Spec §15.1 — `src/domain/**` imports no React Native, Expo, SQLite or BLE.

## Method

### Files

- `src/domain/feedback/ConfirmationTypes.ts` — all contracts below (new).
- `src/domain/feedback/__tests__/ConfirmationTypes.test.ts` — type-level and helper tests (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
export type ConfidenceTier = 'confirmed' | 'likely' | 'partial' | 'unconfirmed'
export type HapticCue = 'confirm' | 'extra' | 'combo-complete' | 'streak'
export type PlausibilitySignal =
  | 'handOrder' | 'timing' | 'separation' | 'intensity' | 'exclusivity'

/** One strike resolved against the active combination's expected tokens. */
export type StrikeResolution =
  | { kind: 'filled'; tokenIndex: number; eventId: string; offsetMs: number }
  | { kind: 'extra'; eventId: string; reason: 'wrong-hand' | 'all-filled' | 'outside-window' }

/** Per-signal value plus whether the capability tier could supply it at all. */
export interface SignalReading { signal: PlausibilitySignal; value: number; available: boolean }

export interface ComboConfidence {
  confidence: number            // 0..1, weighted mean over AVAILABLE signals only
  tier: ConfidenceTier
  readings: SignalReading[]     // every signal, including unavailable ones (value ignored)
  expectedPunchCount: number
  confirmedCount: number
  extraCount: number
  confidenceVersion: string
}

export const CONFIDENCE_VERSION = '1.0.0'
export const TIER_THRESHOLDS = { confirmed: 0.85, likely: 0.6, partial: 0.3 } as const

export function tierFor(confidence: number): ConfidenceTier
/** Label text for any surface that shows a result. Always ends in the §3 tier label. */
export function confidenceLabel(c: ComboConfidence, tierLabel: string): string
export function hapticForResolution(r: StrikeResolution): HapticCue
```

### Algorithm / state machine

1. `tierFor` maps confidence to a tier using `TIER_THRESHOLDS`, descending. **A combination with any unfilled expected node can never be `confirmed`** — `tierFor` takes confidence only, so the scorer (M37-02) is responsible for clamping; that responsibility is stated here and asserted in M37-02's tests.
2. `hapticForResolution` returns `confirm` for `filled` and `extra` for `extra`. `combo-complete` and `streak` are emitted by the gratification layer (M37-06), not by strike resolution.
3. `confidenceLabel` composes the tier word with the caller-supplied capability label so no module can hard-code a claim: e.g. `confidenceLabel(c, 'hand-sequence match')` → `"combination confirmed — hand-sequence match"`. **There is no code path that produces a technique claim.**
4. `SignalReading.available === false` means the connected tracker cannot supply that signal. Consumers must skip it; `value` is meaningless.

### Data flow

M37-02 produces `ComboConfidence` from `CueInstance` + matched events; M37-04 consumes `StrikeResolution` for node state and haptics; M37-05 renders the border from `confirmedCount / expectedPunchCount`; M37-06 reads `tier` for celebration; M37-07 persists `confidence`, `tier`, `readings` and `confidenceVersion`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ConfidenceTier`, `HapticCue`, `PlausibilitySignal`, `StrikeResolution`, `SignalReading` and `ComboConfidence` are exported from `src/domain/feedback/ConfirmationTypes.ts` exactly as above (doc §28.2, §28.4).
- [ ] `TIER_THRESHOLDS` matches doc §28.4: `confirmed` ≥ 0.85, `likely` ≥ 0.6, `partial` ≥ 0.3, otherwise `unconfirmed`.
- [ ] `tierFor` is total over 0..1 and covered by boundary tests at exactly 0.85, 0.6 and 0.3.
- [ ] `SignalReading` carries `available`, and a doc comment states that unavailable signals are **omitted from the mean, never scored as zero** (D11).
- [ ] `confidenceLabel` always appends the caller-supplied capability label; a test asserts no exported helper can emit a technique claim (D4).
- [ ] `hapticForResolution` maps `filled`→`confirm` and `extra`→`extra`; the four-cue union has no fifth member (doc §28.2).
- [ ] `CONFIDENCE_VERSION` is exported and referenced by M37-02 and M37-07 rather than re-declared.
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite` or `src/ble/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `ConfirmationTypes.test.ts`: tier boundaries (0.849/0.85/0.6/0.599/0.3/0.299/0/1); `hapticForResolution` for both resolution kinds and all three `extra` reasons; `confidenceLabel` output shape for each tier; a lint-style test asserting the module source contains no technique words.

## Non-goals

- Computing confidence (M37-02), rendering (M37-04, M37-05), celebration (M37-06), persistence (M37-07).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M31-01 (`WorkoutToken`, `PunchNumber`), M32-03 (`CueInstance` shape for `tokenIndex` semantics).
- Unblocks: M37-02, M37-03, M37-04, M37-05, M37-06, M37-07, M37-08.

## Notes

- Decision (do not re-litigate): unavailable signals are omitted from the mean, never zeroed (D11) — the `available` flag exists so no consumer can get this wrong silently.
- Keep the haptic union at exactly four cues; the athlete cannot distinguish more through a wrap (doc §28.2).
- On completion, comment with files added, constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Implement ComboPlausibilityScorer with capability-aware signal omission
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M37 (doc §28.4). Implements the plausibility model: given one combination instance and the punch events that landed in its window, compute the five signals, take the weighted mean **over the signals the connected tracker can actually supply**, and produce a `ComboConfidence`. This is the intellectual core of M37 — it is what lets the app say "that was probably a 1-2-3" when the tracker can only prove that a left, a right and a left arrived. Pure domain, versioned, deterministic. On the M37 critical path.

## Design references

- Doc §28.1 — confirmation is evidential, not definitive; the tracker cannot prove technique.
- Doc §28.4 — the five signals and the tier thresholds; the omit-never-zero rule.
- Doc §6 — acceptance windows, one-event-one-slot, event-time ordering, extras never disappear.
- Doc §3 / D4 — capability tiers; FightCamp v1 sits at hand + broad type (H11).
- Spec §15.1 (purity), §18.3 (monotonic time only), §8.6 (recalculable results).

## Method

### Files

- `src/domain/feedback/ComboPlausibility.ts` — scorer and weights (new).
- `src/domain/feedback/__tests__/ComboPlausibility.test.ts` — see Test plan (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
import type { CapabilityTier } from '@domain/workout/capabilityTier'   // M32-02

export interface PlausibilityWeights {
  handOrder: number; timing: number; separation: number
  intensity: number; exclusivity: number
}
/** Starting weights; tuned on the bag in M36-03 via tuning.ts. */
export const DEFAULT_WEIGHTS: PlausibilityWeights

export interface ScoreComboInput {
  cue: CueInstance                 // M32-03: expectedPunches, windows, token offsets
  events: TrackerPunchEvent[]      // accepted events inside the window, event-time ordered
  resolutions: StrikeResolution[]  // from the same pass that drove node flashes (M37-04)
  tier: CapabilityTier
  cadenceBpm: number
  weights?: PlausibilityWeights
}

export function scoreCombo(input: ScoreComboInput): ComboConfidence
export function availableSignals(tier: CapabilityTier): PlausibilitySignal[]
```

### Algorithm / state machine

1. **Availability first.** `availableSignals(tier)` decides which signals can be computed at all: `handOrder` and `exclusivity` need hand only; `timing` and `separation` additionally need a usable per-event time; `intensity` needs the broad type flag or velocity. Anything not listed is emitted as `{ available: false }` and **excluded from both numerator and denominator**.
2. **`handOrder`** — longest common subsequence between the expected hand sequence and the observed hand sequence, divided by `expectedPunchCount`. Using LCS (not raw equality) means one extra strike in the middle does not destroy the score; extras are penalised by `exclusivity` instead, so the two effects stay separable.
3. **`timing`** — for each filled node, `1 - |offsetFromWindowCentre| / (windowHalfWidth)`, clamped to 0..1, averaged over filled nodes. Unfilled nodes contribute nothing (they are already reflected in `handOrder`), so timing never double-penalises a miss.
4. **`separation`** — compares observed inter-strike intervals against the interval the block's cadence implies (`beatsToMs`, M31-02). Intervals far below the expected minimum indicate one motion registering as several; score falls off as the ratio departs from 1. **This is the guard against a single flail reading as a combination.**
5. **`intensity`** — where the tier supplies it, compares the emphasis the combination implies (rear-hand and hook/uppercut tokens are expected heavier than a jab) with the observed vendor type flag and tracker-reported velocity. Agreement in rank order, not absolute value, because velocity is in tracker units (spec §4.3).
6. **`exclusivity`** — `1 - extras / (expectedPunchCount + extras)`.
7. **Mean.** `confidence = Σ(w_i · v_i) / Σ(w_i)` over available signals only. **Clamp:** if any expected node is unfilled, confidence is capped just below the `confirmed` threshold, so `confirmed` always means every node was filled (doc §28.4).
8. `tier = tierFor(confidence)`. Result carries every reading, including unavailable ones, plus `CONFIDENCE_VERSION`.
9. **Invariants:** pure; no wall time; no `Date.now()`; identical inputs give identical output; an unavailable signal changes the mean by exactly nothing.

### Data flow

M33-02's matching pass produces `resolutions`; the CueEngine's `cue-window-closed` (M32-04) triggers `scoreCombo`; the result flows to M37-05 (border), M37-06 (gratification) and M37-07 (persistence).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scoreCombo` returns a `ComboConfidence` (M37-01) with one `SignalReading` per signal, `available: false` for signals the tier cannot supply (doc §28.4, D11).
- [ ] An unavailable signal provably does not change `confidence`: a test scores the same events at two tiers and asserts the mean over shared signals is identical.
- [ ] `handOrder` uses longest-common-subsequence so a single interleaved extra does not zero it, and a test pins that behaviour.
- [ ] `separation` drops below 0.5 when three strikes arrive inside one expected inter-punch interval (doc §28.4 flail guard).
- [ ] Confidence is capped below `TIER_THRESHOLDS.confirmed` whenever `confirmedCount < expectedPunchCount`.
- [ ] `intensity` compares rank order only and never treats tracker units as a physical quantity (spec §4.3).
- [ ] FightCamp v1 (`hand-broad-type`) yields all five signals except any requiring distinct technique; a test asserts the exact available set.
- [ ] `scoreCombo` is deterministic and pure: no `Date.now()`, no imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite`, `src/ble/**` (spec §15.1, §18.3).
- [ ] `CONFIDENCE_VERSION` is imported from `ConfirmationTypes.ts`, not redeclared.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `ComboPlausibility.test.ts`: (a) perfect 1-2-3 at hand-broad-type → `confirmed`; (b) same events at hand-only → same confidence over shared signals; (c) correct hands, one late strike → `likely`; (d) two of three filled → capped below `confirmed`, tier `partial`; (e) three strikes inside one interval → `separation` < 0.5; (f) one interleaved extra → `handOrder` intact, `exclusivity` reduced; (g) southpaw switch combination; (h) property: output is invariant under repeated calls with identical input.

## Non-goals

- Node rendering (M37-04), border (M37-05), celebration (M37-06), persistence (M37-07), weight tuning (M36-03).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M37-01 (contracts), M32-02 (`CapabilityTier`), M32-03 (`CueInstance`), M31-02 (`beatsToMs`), M33-02 (resolutions from the matching pass).
- Unblocks: M37-05, M37-06, M37-07, M37-08.

## Notes

- Decision (do not re-litigate): LCS for `handOrder` and a separate `exclusivity` signal, so "wrong order" and "too many punches" stay independently visible.
- `DEFAULT_WEIGHTS` are a starting point only; M36-03 replaces them with bag-tuned constants and must bump `CONFIDENCE_VERSION` when it does.
- On completion, comment with files added, the weights chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Add HapticPort and the Expo haptics driver
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M37 (doc §28.2). Adds the haptic channel: a pure domain port describing the four-cue vocabulary and an Expo driver that plays it. Haptics are an Expo/Android API, so by spec §15.1 they cannot live in `src/domain/**` — the same port-and-driver split already used for the Voice Coach (D13, M34-02/M34-04). Small but blocking: the live screen (M37-04) and the gratification layer (M37-06) both fire cues through this port.

## Design references

- Doc §28.2 — the four cues and their patterns (`confirm` one light pulse, `extra` one very short lighter pulse, `combo-complete` medium double, `streak` medium triple).
- Doc §25 — haptic intensity is user-adjustable and the channel can be switched off; the workout stays usable without it.
- Spec §15.1 — domain imports no Expo; §19.4 — haptics with user-adjustable intensity; §11.2 — native modules require a prebuild and a new dev client.

## Method

### Files

- `src/domain/feedback/HapticPort.ts` — port + no-op implementation (new, pure).
- `src/haptics/HapticsExpo.ts` — `expo-haptics` driver (new, infra).
- `src/domain/feedback/__tests__/HapticPort.test.ts` — no-op and dispatch tests (new).
- `package.json`, `app.config.ts` — add `expo-haptics` (modify).

### Interfaces

```ts
// src/domain/feedback/HapticPort.ts  (pure)
export interface HapticSettings { enabled: boolean; intensity: 'light' | 'medium' | 'strong' }
export interface HapticPort {
  play(cue: HapticCue): void          // fire-and-forget; never throws, never awaits
  setSettings(s: HapticSettings): void
}
export const NOOP_HAPTICS: HapticPort  // used when disabled or unavailable

// src/haptics/HapticsExpo.ts  (Expo)
export function createExpoHaptics(initial?: HapticSettings): HapticPort
```

### Algorithm / state machine

1. `play` is **fire-and-forget and must never throw or block** — it is called from the punch hot path, inside the same tick that flashes a node. Any driver error is swallowed and logged once through `@diagnostics/logger`, never per event.
2. Cue → pattern mapping in the driver: `confirm` → one light impact; `extra` → one selection-level tick; `combo-complete` → two medium impacts ~80 ms apart; `streak` → three medium impacts ~80 ms apart. Intensity scales the impact style, not the pulse count, so the four cues stay distinguishable at every setting.
3. `enabled: false` short-circuits before touching Expo. `NOOP_HAPTICS` is returned when the device reports no haptic support, so callers never branch.
4. Rate limiting: at most one `confirm`/`extra` per accepted punch and never more than one multi-pulse cue in flight — a `combo-complete` arriving during a `streak` is dropped rather than queued, because overlapping patterns read as noise through a wrap.

### Data flow

M37-04 calls `play('confirm' | 'extra')` from strike resolution; M37-06 calls `play('combo-complete' | 'streak')` from the gratification layer; settings come from the Puncheokie settings slice alongside the Voice Coach volumes (M34-05).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `HapticPort`, `HapticSettings` and `NOOP_HAPTICS` are exported from `src/domain/feedback/HapticPort.ts` with **zero** imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite` or `src/ble/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `createExpoHaptics` lives in `src/haptics/HapticsExpo.ts` and is the only module importing `expo-haptics`.
- [ ] The four cues map to the doc §28.2 patterns; a test asserts each cue produces a distinct call sequence against a stubbed Expo module.
- [ ] `play` never throws: a test forces the driver to reject and asserts the caller is unaffected and the error is logged once, not per call.
- [ ] `enabled: false` produces no Expo calls at all.
- [ ] Overlapping multi-pulse cues are dropped, not queued.
- [ ] `expo-haptics` is added to `package.json` and the Expo SDK version is unchanged (spec §11.2, CLAUDE.md rule 5); the issue notes that a prebuild and dev-client rebuild are required.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `HapticPort.test.ts`: `NOOP_HAPTICS` swallows every cue; a fake port records dispatch order; driver-level tests inject a stub `expo-haptics` and assert pattern shape, the disabled short-circuit, the throw-safety path and overlap dropping.
- Manual on the tablet (folded into M37-04's device pass): each cue is distinguishable through a wrap at each intensity.

## Non-goals

- Deciding *when* to fire a cue (M37-04, M37-06); the settings UI (M34-05 owns the shared settings screen); audio (M34).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M37-01 (`HapticCue`).
- Unblocks: M37-04, M37-06.

## Notes

- `expo-haptics` is a native module: `npx expo prebuild --platform android` plus `npx expo run:android` before it works on the tablet. Same Expo SDK, so the version lock (CLAUDE.md rule 5) is not violated. M32-05 may already have added it — check before installing twice.
- On completion, comment with files added, the pattern constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Node confirmation flash and per-strike haptics on the live screen
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M37 (doc §28.2). Wires strike resolution into the live screen: every accepted punch resolves to a hand from its tracker slot, finds the expected token it most plausibly fills, flashes that node, and fires a haptic. This is the moment the athlete feels the app respond, and it is the visible half of "haptically flashes a punch number's node". Depends on the live screen (M32-08) and the matching pass (M33-02) already existing.

## Design references

- Doc §28.2 — resolution rule, confirming flash versus neutral acknowledgement, and the explicit prohibition on a red flash mid-combination.
- Doc §13 — token visual grammar; active/completed/upcoming states; no red flash during a combination.
- Doc §21 — per-punch feedback: token brightens, counter increments, latest velocity tile updates, optional haptic.
- Doc §25 / spec §19.4 — never colour-only; reduced-motion variant; haptics optional.
- H11 — hand comes from the connection slot, never from the payload.

## Method

### Files

- `src/domain/feedback/resolveStrike.ts` — pure resolution function (new).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/useWorkoutRunner.ts` — call resolution per accepted event, dispatch node state + haptic (modify).
- `src/components/workout/PunchToken.tsx` — add `confirmed` visual state (modify).
- `src/state/useWorkoutStore.ts` — per-token confirmation state on the live slice (modify).
- `src/domain/feedback/__tests__/resolveStrike.test.ts` (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
export function resolveStrike(args: {
  cue: CueInstance                    // M32-03
  event: TrackerPunchEvent            // hand already stamped from the slot
  filled: ReadonlySet<number>         // tokenIndexes already filled for this instance
  nowWorkElapsedMs: number
}): StrikeResolution                  // M37-01

/** Live-slice addition. */
export interface TokenConfirmState {
  tokenIndex: number
  status: 'upcoming' | 'active' | 'confirmed'
  flashSeq: number                    // increments per flash so the view can re-animate
}
```

### Algorithm / state machine

1. **Hand from the slot.** The event's `hand` is stamped upstream from the `deviceId` → slot assignment (`useTrackerStore`); this issue never reads a hand out of a payload (H11).
2. **Resolution.** Choose the *earliest unfilled* expected punch whose `hand` equals the event hand and whose acceptance window contains `nowWorkElapsedMs`. Found → `{ kind: 'filled', tokenIndex, offsetMs }`. Not found → `{ kind: 'extra', reason }` where reason distinguishes `wrong-hand`, `all-filled` and `outside-window`, because the three mean different things in the round summary.
3. **One event, at most one node** (doc §6). `filled` is the authority; a node cannot be filled twice.
4. **Filled →** set that token to `confirmed`, bump `flashSeq`, fire `confirm` haptic (M37-03). The token brightens, gains an accent ring and a check glyph — shape and glyph carry the state as well as colour (spec §19.4).
5. **Extra →** counters and the extras readout increment, `extra` haptic fires, and **no token changes state**. There is no red flash, no shake and no failure sound anywhere in this path (doc §28.2, §13).
6. Reduced motion: the token switches state without the flash animation; `flashSeq` still increments so assistive tech announces the change.
7. Store writes stay inside the existing ≤10 Hz throttle (spec §15.3); a burst of strikes coalesces into one render without losing any `flashSeq` increment.

### Data flow

`PunchEventSource` → runner → `resolveStrike` → (a) `useWorkoutStore` token state, (b) `HapticPort.play`, (c) the same resolution array is accumulated for the instance and handed to `scoreCombo` (M37-02) at window close.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `resolveStrike` is pure and picks the earliest unfilled same-hand expected punch whose window contains the event (doc §28.2, §6).
- [ ] A second strike can never re-fill an already-filled node; a test asserts one-event-one-slot.
- [ ] `extra` resolutions distinguish `wrong-hand`, `all-filled` and `outside-window`.
- [ ] A filled node renders `confirmed` with accent ring **and** check glyph; a test asserts the state is not conveyed by colour alone (spec §19.4).
- [ ] An unmatched strike increments counters and the extras readout and changes no token state; a test asserts **no** red/failure state exists on this path (doc §28.2).
- [ ] `confirm` fires on filled and `extra` on unmatched, through `HapticPort` (M37-03) — the screen never imports `expo-haptics` directly.
- [ ] Hand is taken from the slot assignment, never from the payload; a test with a payload-borne hand field asserts it is ignored (H11).
- [ ] Reduced motion swaps the flash for a plain state change while still bumping `flashSeq`.
- [ ] Store writes remain throttled to ≤10 Hz and no `flashSeq` increment is lost under a 10-strike burst (spec §15.3).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `resolveStrike.test.ts`: correct-hand in window → filled; wrong hand → extra/`wrong-hand`; all filled → extra/`all-filled`; outside window → extra/`outside-window`; earliest-unfilled preference with two candidate nodes; southpaw combination.
- Component/store tests: token renders `confirmed` with glyph; extras change no token; burst throttling preserves `flashSeq`.
- Manual on the tablet with `SimulatedPunchSource` (M32-01) and then a real tracker: flash and pulse feel simultaneous with the strike.

## Non-goals

- Confidence scoring (M37-02), the border (M37-05), celebration and streaks (M37-06), persistence (M37-07).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M37-01, M37-03, M32-03 (`CueInstance`), M32-06 (`PunchToken`), M32-08 (live screen), M33-02 (matching pass this hooks into).
- Unblocks: M37-05, M37-06, M37-02 (consumes the resolution array).

## Notes

- Decision (do not re-litigate): earliest-unfilled same-hand-in-window resolution. It is deliberately simple and deliberately generous — the tracker cannot do better, and mis-resolution is corrected at window close by `scoreCombo`.
- On completion, comment with files added, the throttle behaviour observed on device, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Progressive combo affirmation border with completion sweep
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M37 (doc §28.3). The affirmation border is the combination-level counterpart to the per-node flash: a border around the active combination strip that fills as expected nodes are confirmed and sweeps once when the combination closes at `confirmed` or `likely`. It is the "affirmation border around punches if they happen in combo sequence" the design calls for, and it is the only place the confidence tier becomes visible mid-round.

## Design references

- Doc §28.3 — progressive fill (k/n), completion sweep with tier glyph and label, stop-and-fade on shortfall, reduced-motion stepping.
- Doc §28.5 — the border sweep is the combination-level gratification response.
- Doc §28.6 / D11 / D4 — labels read "combination confirmed — hand-sequence match"; never a technique claim.
- Doc §13 — no red flash mid-combination; §19.4 — never colour-only.

## Method

### Files

- `src/components/workout/AffirmationBorder.tsx` — the border component (new).
- `src/components/workout/CueStage.tsx` — wrap the token strip in the border (modify).
- `src/components/workout/__tests__/AffirmationBorder.test.tsx` (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
export interface AffirmationBorderProps {
  confirmedCount: number
  expectedCount: number
  /** Set once the window closes; absent while the combination is live. */
  outcome?: { tier: ConfidenceTier; label: string }
  reducedMotion?: boolean
  children: React.ReactNode
}
export function AffirmationBorder(p: AffirmationBorderProps): React.ReactElement
```

### Behavior

1. **Progressive fill.** With no `outcome`, the border is drawn `confirmedCount / expectedCount` of the way around the strip. `expectedCount === 0` (a display-only block) renders no border at all — defense, footwork and coach tokens are never scored (D4) and must never appear to be failing.
2. **Completion.** When `outcome.tier` is `confirmed` or `likely`, the border completes and sweeps once, then settles showing the tier glyph and `outcome.label`. Tier is carried by **glyph + label + border thickness**, not colour alone (spec §19.4).
3. **Shortfall.** When `outcome.tier` is `partial` or `unconfirmed`, the border **stops where it is and fades**. No red, no shake, no failure animation, no sound (doc §28.3). The shortfall is reported in the cue result and the round summary instead.
4. **Reduced motion.** Fill steps between discrete states and the sweep becomes a single state change; the glyph and label are identical, so no information is motion-only.
5. **Never regresses.** Fill is monotonic within one combination instance; a late extra strike cannot reduce it. A repeat instance mounts fresh at zero.
6. Rendering is driven entirely by props — the component holds no timers and reads no store, so it is trivially testable and re-mountable per repeat instance.

### Data flow

`CueStage` passes `confirmedCount` from the live slice (M37-04) and, on `cue-window-closed` (M32-04), `outcome` derived from `scoreCombo` (M37-02) via `confidenceLabel` (M37-01).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Border fill is `confirmedCount / expectedCount` and is monotonic within an instance (doc §28.3).
- [ ] `expectedCount === 0` renders no border, so display-only blocks never look like a failed combination (D4).
- [ ] `confirmed` and `likely` produce the completion sweep; `partial` and `unconfirmed` stop-and-fade with **no** red state, shake or failure sound; a test asserts no such style or asset exists on this path (doc §28.3).
- [ ] Tier is conveyed by glyph **and** text **and** border thickness in addition to colour (spec §19.4).
- [ ] The label is produced by `confidenceLabel` and always ends in the capability label — a test asserts the rendered string contains `hand-sequence match` and no technique claim (D4, D11).
- [ ] `reducedMotion` steps instead of animating and loses no information.
- [ ] The component is prop-driven, holds no timers, reads no store, and re-mounts cleanly per repeat instance.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `AffirmationBorder.test.tsx`: fill at 0/1/2/3 of 3; `expectedCount === 0` renders nothing; each of the four tiers renders the right terminal state; label contains the capability phrase; reduced-motion path; monotonicity when `confirmedCount` is re-sent lower.
- Manual on the tablet: the sweep is legible at arm's length and does not distract during the next combination.

## Non-goals

- Computing confidence (M37-02), per-node flash (M37-04), streaks and celebration escalation (M37-06), persistence (M37-07).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M37-01 (`ConfidenceTier`, `confidenceLabel`), M37-02 (`outcome` source), M37-04 (`confirmedCount`), M32-07 (`CueStage`).
- Unblocks: M37-06.

## Notes

- Decision (do not re-litigate): shortfall fades, never reddens. Mismatch feedback belongs to the cue result and the round summary (doc §13, §28.3).
- Use `@/theme/colors`; the tier palette should reuse `success`/`accent`/`textSecondary` rather than introducing new hues.
- On completion, comment with files added, the sweep duration chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Gratification tiers, streaks, and Focus mode
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M37 (doc §28.5). The gratification layer: decides when a combination earns acknowledgement, tracks streaks, escalates in bounded steps, and offers a Focus mode that turns all of it off. This is the "gratification system … anytime a combo from the UX completed successfully, or plausibly successfully" the design calls for — with the four governing rules that keep it a training instrument rather than a slot machine.

## Design references

- Doc §28.5 — the five levels (node, combination, streak, round, session) and the four rules: never celebrate what did not happen, never punish, always optional, never used to push pace.
- Doc §28.4 — celebration fires at `confirmed` or `likely`, never at `partial` or below.
- Doc §25 — never escalate to drive the athlete toward an unreachable target; everything disable-able.
- D1 — the optional tone obeys the Voice Coach gate and does not play over third-party playback without an explicit opt-in.
- Doc §23, §24 — round and session levels reuse the existing count badge and summary.

## Method

### Files

- `src/domain/feedback/gratification.ts` — pure policy and streak state machine (new).
- `src/domain/feedback/__tests__/gratification.test.ts` (new).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/useWorkoutRunner.ts` — drive the policy from `cue-window-closed` (modify).
- `src/components/workout/StreakBadge.tsx` — streak counter and threshold pulse (new).
- `src/state/useWorkoutStore.ts` — streak and celebration slice (modify).

### Interfaces

```ts
export type GratificationEvent =
  | { kind: 'combo'; tier: ConfidenceTier; label: string }
  | { kind: 'streak'; length: number; threshold: 3 | 5 | 10 }

export interface GratificationSettings {
  mode: 'full' | 'focus'        // focus = counters and timer only
  tone: boolean                 // optional short tone on combination close
}

export interface StreakState { current: number; best: number }

export function nextStreak(s: StreakState, tier: ConfidenceTier): StreakState
export function gratificationFor(
  tier: ConfidenceTier, streak: StreakState, settings: GratificationSettings,
): GratificationEvent[]
export const STREAK_THRESHOLDS: readonly [3, 5, 10]
```

### Algorithm / state machine

1. **Eligibility.** A combination produces a `combo` event only at `confirmed` or `likely`. `partial` and `unconfirmed` produce **no event at all** — the border still shows progress (M37-05), but nothing celebrates (doc §28.5 rule 1).
2. **Streaks.** `nextStreak` increments on `likely` or better and **resets to zero** on `partial` or `unconfirmed`. `best` is a running maximum for the round summary. A `streak` event fires only when `current` lands exactly on a value in `STREAK_THRESHOLDS`, so 3/5/10 pulse once each rather than every subsequent combination.
3. **Escalation is bounded.** The full ladder is: node micro-flash (M37-04) → border sweep + `combo-complete` haptic + optional tone (M37-05, M37-03) → streak badge pulse + `streak` haptic → round badge (M33-03) → session summary (M33-08). **There is no level above `streak` mid-round**, so intensity cannot ratchet upward indefinitely.
4. **Never punitive.** The module has no failure event, no negative branch and no sound or haptic for a missed combination (doc §28.5 rule 2).
5. **Focus mode.** `mode: 'focus'` makes `gratificationFor` return an empty array unconditionally; counters, timer and border fill continue. One switch, no partial states (rule 3).
6. **Never used to push pace.** The policy takes only tier and streak — it has no access to required pace or the goal, so it structurally cannot escalate to chase a target (rule 4, doc §25).
7. **Tone gating.** `settings.tone` only requests a tone; the audio layer applies the D1 third-party-playback gate. This module never decides that it is safe to play over music.

### Data flow

`cue-window-closed` (M32-04) → `scoreCombo` (M37-02) → `nextStreak` + `gratificationFor` → haptics (M37-03), border outcome (M37-05), streak badge, and the round/session aggregates consumed by M33-03 and M33-08.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `gratificationFor` returns a `combo` event only for `confirmed` and `likely`; `partial` and `unconfirmed` return `[]` (doc §28.5 rule 1).
- [ ] `nextStreak` increments on `likely` or better and resets on `partial`/`unconfirmed`; `best` tracks the maximum.
- [ ] A `streak` event fires exactly once at each of 3, 5 and 10 and not on intermediate values.
- [ ] `mode: 'focus'` returns `[]` for every input while counters, timer and border fill are unaffected (rule 3).
- [ ] The module exports **no** failure/miss event and contains no negative feedback branch; a test asserts the event union has exactly two members (rule 2).
- [ ] `gratificationFor` takes only tier, streak and settings — it cannot read pace or goal (rule 4, doc §25).
- [ ] `settings.tone` only requests a tone; the D1 gate is applied downstream and a test asserts this module never inspects playback state.
- [ ] `StreakBadge` conveys threshold pulses with shape/text as well as colour and honours reduced motion (spec §19.4).
- [ ] Pure: no imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite` or `src/ble/**` in `gratification.ts` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `gratification.test.ts`: eligibility across all four tiers; streak increment/reset table; threshold firing at 3/5/10 and silence at 4/6/11; focus mode returns empty for every tier; the event union has two members; a run of 12 combinations producing the expected event sequence.
- Component test: `StreakBadge` pulse at each threshold and its reduced-motion variant.
- Manual on the tablet: a 5-combination streak feels rewarding and not distracting; Focus mode is genuinely silent.

## Non-goals

- Confidence scoring (M37-02), border rendering (M37-05), round badge (M33-03), session summary (M33-08), audio playback (M34).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M37-01 (`ConfidenceTier`), M37-02 (tier source), M37-03 (haptics), M37-05 (border outcome).
- Unblocks: M37-07 (persists streak/tier aggregates), M33-08 (summary consumes them).

## Notes

- Decision (do not re-litigate): the policy is deliberately blind to pace and goal, so rule 4 is structural rather than a convention someone can break later.
- Streak thresholds 3/5/10 are starting constants; M36-03 may retune them on the bag.
- On completion, comment with files added, threshold constants chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Persist combo_results with signals and CONFIDENCE_VERSION
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M37 (doc §28.6, D11). Persists one `combo_results` row per combination instance carrying the confidence, the tier, every input signal and `CONFIDENCE_VERSION`, so a better decoder or a retuned weight set can recompute historical sessions without touching raw events (D8, spec §8.6). Without this, confidence is a throwaway animation input; with it, it is a recalculable result.

## Design references

- Doc §28.4, §28.6 — signals, tiers, versioning; D11 — persistence requirement and the omit-never-zero rule that `signals_json` must faithfully record.
- Spec §17.1 — the `combo_results` column list.
- Spec §8.6, §19.1 — recalculation from stored data without altering raw events; D8 — the realized stream precedent.
- Spec §15.4, §15.1 — SQLite lives in the storage layer; domain stays pure.

## Method

### Files

- `src/storage/migrations/00N_combo_results.ts` — TS `Migration` appended to `MIGRATIONS` (new).
- `src/storage/repositories/WorkoutRepository.ts` — `writeComboResults`, `listComboResults` (modify).
- `src/storage/repositories/__tests__/comboResults.test.ts` — in-memory SQLite tests (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
export interface ComboResultRow {
  id: string
  sessionId: string
  generatedWorkoutId: string
  blockId: string
  repeatIndex: number
  expectedPunchCount: number
  confirmedCount: number
  extraCount: number
  confidence: number
  confidenceTier: ConfidenceTier
  signalsJson: string            // SignalReading[] incl. available:false entries
  confidenceVersion: string
  startedAtMonotonicMs: number
  windowCloseMonotonicMs: number
}

// WorkoutRepository additions
writeComboResults(rows: ComboResultRow[]): Promise<void>   // single transaction
listComboResults(sessionId: string): Promise<ComboResultRow[]>
```

### Algorithm / state machine

1. **Migration follows the TS `Migration` pattern** used by `001_initial.ts` and appended to the `MIGRATIONS` array — the runner cannot load a `.sql` file. Columns exactly as spec §17.1, with `session_id` and `generated_workout_id` foreign keys and an index on `session_id`.
2. `signals_json` stores the full `SignalReading[]` **including entries with `available: false`**. This is the point of the table: a later reader must be able to distinguish "the tracker could not measure this" from "this scored badly" (D11). A row that dropped unavailable entries would be unrecoverable.
3. `writeComboResults` writes all rows for a session in **one transaction**, alongside the existing `cue_results` write (M33-08), so a session's scoring is atomic.
4. `confidence_version` is written from `CONFIDENCE_VERSION` (M37-01) at write time, never inferred at read time — that is what makes historical rows interpretable after the algorithm changes.
5. Recalculation path: `listComboResults` plus the realized token stream (D8) and stored punch events are sufficient to re-run `scoreCombo` at a newer version and compare. Raw events are never modified (spec §8.6).

### Data flow

M37-02 produces `ComboConfidence` at each `cue-window-closed`; the runner accumulates them for the session; M33-08's summary write calls `writeComboResults` in the same transaction as `cue_results` and the `sessions` row.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration creates `combo_results` with exactly the spec §17.1 columns, foreign keys to `sessions` and `generated_workouts`, and an index on `session_id`.
- [ ] The migration is a TS `Migration` object appended to `MIGRATIONS` in the existing runner — **not** a `.sql` file.
- [ ] `signals_json` round-trips the full `SignalReading[]` including `available: false` entries; a test asserts an unavailable signal survives write→read distinguishable from a zero-valued available one (D11).
- [ ] `writeComboResults` is a single transaction and composes with the `cue_results` write from M33-08 without a second commit.
- [ ] `confidence_version` is persisted from `CONFIDENCE_VERSION` at write time.
- [ ] A recalculation test writes rows at version A, re-scores the same stored events under version B, and asserts the raw punch events are byte-identical afterwards (spec §8.6, §19.1).
- [ ] Repository code imports no domain-mutating logic and the domain imports no SQLite (spec §15.1, §15.4).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `comboResults.test.ts` against in-memory SQLite: migration applies cleanly and is idempotent; write/read round-trip for all four tiers; `available: false` preservation; transaction atomicity (a forced failure mid-write leaves no partial rows); recalculation leaves raw events untouched.

## Non-goals

- Computing confidence (M37-02), the summary UI (M33-08), the realized token stream (M31-08 / M33-07).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M37-01 (`ConfidenceTier`, `CONFIDENCE_VERSION`), M37-02 (`ComboConfidence`), M31-08 (workouts migration this appends after), M31-09 (`WorkoutRepository`).
- Unblocks: M33-08 (summary reads these), M37-08 (fixtures assert persisted shape).

## Notes

- Check the highest existing migration number before naming the file; the runner applies in array order.
- Decision (do not re-litigate): unavailable signals are persisted explicitly rather than omitted from the JSON, so a future reader can never mistake a capability gap for a poor score.
- On completion, comment with files added, the migration number used, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Plausibility fixture tests across capability tiers
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M37 (doc §28, D11). Fixture suite that pins the plausibility model across capability tiers using recorded event streams, so the two properties that matter most cannot regress silently: an absent tracker capability never reads as athlete failure, and no surface ever claims technique. Runs headless in CI with no hardware, alongside the existing decoder fixtures.

## Design references

- Doc §28.4 — signals, thresholds, the omit-never-zero rule.
- Doc §28.5 — celebration eligibility; §28.6 — labelling.
- D4 / D11 — hand-sequence match everywhere; graded, capability-aware, never punitive.
- Spec §21.1 (pure-domain unit tests), §21.2 (fixture determinism), §12.7 (replay runs without Bluetooth hardware).

## Method

### Files

- `src/domain/feedback/__tests__/fixtures/` — recorded combination attempts as JSON (new).
- `src/domain/feedback/__tests__/plausibility.fixtures.test.ts` — the suite (new).
- `src/domain/feedback/__tests__/fixtures/README.md` — how to add a fixture (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
interface PlausibilityFixture {
  name: string
  cue: CueInstance                 // expected tokens + windows
  events: TrackerPunchEvent[]      // event-time ordered
  cadenceBpm: number
  expect: Record<CapabilityTier, {
    tier: ConfidenceTier
    availableSignals: PlausibilitySignal[]
    celebrates: boolean            // gratificationFor(...).length > 0
  }>
}
```

### Protocol

Each fixture is scored at **every** capability tier and asserted against the recorded expectation, so a change to `availableSignals` shows up as a diff rather than a silent shift.

Fixtures to author:

1. **clean-1-2-3-orthodox** — perfect L-R-L in window → `confirmed` at every tier that supports it; celebrates.
2. **clean-1-2-3-southpaw-switch** — same combination under a switch block; asserts the stance mapping feeds the expected hands (D2).
3. **one-late-strike** — third strike lands just inside `graceAfter` → `likely`, still celebrates.
4. **two-of-three** — one node never filled → capped below `confirmed`, tier `partial`, **does not celebrate** (doc §28.5 rule 1).
5. **flail-triple** — three events inside one expected inter-punch interval → `separation` collapses; asserts the guard against one motion registering as a combination.
6. **interleaved-extra** — an extra strike between correct nodes → `handOrder` intact, `exclusivity` reduced, extras still counted and never dropped (doc §6).
7. **wrong-hand-order** — R-L-L against an expected L-R-L → low `handOrder`, tier `partial` or below, no celebration.
8. **hand-only-tier** — the clean fixture scored with only hand available → `intensity` and `separation` unavailable; **confidence over the shared signals is identical to the richer tier**. This is the fixture that proves D11.
9. **display-only-block** — a defense-counter block with zero expected punches → no confidence, no celebration, no failure (D4).

### Data flow

Fixtures feed `scoreCombo` (M37-02) and `gratificationFor` (M37-06) directly. No BLE, no Expo, no database.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All nine fixtures exist as JSON under `__tests__/fixtures/` with a README explaining how to add one.
- [ ] Every fixture is scored at **every** `CapabilityTier` and asserted against its recorded expectation.
- [ ] `hand-only-tier` asserts that confidence over the shared signals equals the richer tier's — the omit-never-zero guarantee (D11).
- [ ] `two-of-three` asserts tier `partial` **and** `celebrates: false` (doc §28.5 rule 1).
- [ ] `flail-triple` asserts `separation` below 0.5 (doc §28.4).
- [ ] `interleaved-extra` asserts extras are counted and never dropped (doc §6).
- [ ] `display-only-block` asserts no confidence, no celebration and no failure state is produced (D4).
- [ ] A suite-wide assertion scans every produced label and fails on any technique claim, allowing only the capability label (D4, D11).
- [ ] The suite runs headless in CI with no Bluetooth hardware and no Expo modules (spec §12.7, §21.2).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- The suite is the deliverable. It must be deterministic: fixtures carry explicit monotonic times, no clock is read, and re-running produces identical output (spec §21.2).
- Fixtures are pinned to `CONFIDENCE_VERSION`; a version bump requires deliberately re-recording expectations, and the README says so.

## Non-goals

- Tuning the weights (M36-03 does that on the bag and will update these expectations), UI tests (M37-04, M37-05), device testing.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M37-02 (`scoreCombo`), M37-06 (`gratificationFor`), M32-02 (`CapabilityTier`), M32-03 (`CueInstance`).
- Unblocks: M36-03 (bag tuning re-records these expectations).

## Notes

- Prefer real recorded events over hand-written ones where a capture exists; follow the fixture conventions in `src/protocol/fightcamp-v1/fixtures/`.
- When M36-03 retunes weights it must bump `CONFIDENCE_VERSION` and re-record these fixtures in the same commit, so the pairing stays honest.
- On completion, comment with files added, the fixtures recorded, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Spike: backdrop rendering technology, performance and battery budget
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M38 (spec §31.4). Picks the rendering technology for the workout backdrop and establishes its performance and battery budget on the real device. Everything else in M38 is written against whatever this spike chooses, so it lands first. Marked `go-no-go`: if no candidate holds the §19.2 latency budget without overheating the tablet across a 60-minute session, the backdrop ships as the static gradient floor only and the animated library is deferred.

## Design references

- Spec §31.4 — the backdrop is the lowest-priority consumer of the device; the cue pipeline's p95 latency must be unchanged with the heaviest backdrop running.
- Spec §31.2 — the four `source` kinds the model allows (`gradient`, `mesh`, `lottie`, `video`); this spike decides which are actually implementable here.
- Spec §19.2 (p95 ≤ 250 ms), §11.2 (native modules need a prebuild and a new dev client; the Expo SDK version is locked — CLAUDE.md rule 5), §11.11 (foreground, keep-awake).
- Puncheokie doc §19 Backdrop, §25 (reduced motion), D17.

## Method

### Candidates already evaluated on paper

| Candidate | Verdict |
|---|---|
| [`expo-ios-mesh-gradient`](https://github.com/rit3zh/expo-ios-mesh-gradient) | **Rejected.** README states platform support as "✅ iOS (SwiftUI based) / ❌ Android (not supported)"; it wraps SwiftUI `MeshGradient`. This application is Android-first and the target device is the Lenovo TB125FU, so it cannot be used. Revisit only if iOS ships. |
| [`react-native-expo-backgrounds`](https://github.com/UrielCisneros/react-native-expo-backgrounds) | **Rejected as a dependency.** MIT, but 0 stars / 0 forks / 8 commits is no maintenance track record for a core presentation surface, it supplies a single `SpaceBackground` rather than a themeable library, and its effect is a gyroscope-driven parallax starfield. The tablet is mounted at the bag: a gyroscope-reactive backdrop will jitter on every impact, which fights the §31.3 legibility rule, and it pulls in `expo-sensors` for a sensor nothing else needs. The MIT licence does permit adapting the starfield technique as one authored library entry — evaluate that under M38-03, not as a runtime dependency. |

### Build, depend, or vendor

Three sourcing strategies are open, and the spike must pick one per source kind rather than assume:

- **Build.** An animated gradient or mesh is a small amount of code over a rendering primitive we already need. This is the default for `gradient` and `mesh`: it carries no supply-chain risk, no licence question, and no upstream that can break on an Expo upgrade.
- **Depend.** Take a maintained package as a runtime dependency. Justified only for a substantial, well-maintained library — `@shopify/react-native-skia` and `lottie-react-native` are the only two candidates here that clear that bar. Judge on maintenance activity, New Architecture support, Android support, and whether it pins us on future Expo upgrades (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
- **Vendor.** Copy a permissively-licensed implementation into the repository, adapt it, and own it. Appropriate for a small self-contained effect where we want the technique but not the dependency. If vendoring: keep the upstream licence text with the file, record the source commit and every modification in `ATTRIBUTION.md`, and strip anything we do not need — for the starfield example that means removing the gyroscope reactivity entirely, since a bag-mounted tablet would jitter it on every impact.

State the choice per source kind in the deliverable with the reasoning, so M38-03 and M38-04 know what they are building against.

### Candidates to measure on the tablet

1. **`@shopify/react-native-skia`** — cross-platform GPU rendering with shaders and mesh gradients; New Architecture compatible and substantially faster on Android in v2. Needs the Android NDK (already installed, NDK 27.2). Verify against the locked Expo SDK: there is a known import-ordering failure reported on SDK 54 (`ReferenceError: Property 'SkiaViewApi' doesn't exist`) that must be confirmed absent on ours.
2. **`lottie-react-native`** — authored vector loops; small assets, cross-platform, mature.
3. **`expo-video`** — looping video for photographic ambience; simplest to author, heaviest on bundle size and battery.
4. **Reanimated-animated `expo-linear-gradient`** — the cheap floor; also the mandated always-available fallback of spec §31.4 regardless of what wins.

### Protocol

Build one representative `active`-motion backdrop per candidate, run it behind a simulated Puncheokie live screen (M32-08 / M32-01) for 10 minutes, and record:

- p95 and p99 cue-to-render latency **with** the backdrop and **without** it, same scripted punch stream;
- sustained frame rate of both the backdrop and the UI, and whether the backdrop renders off the JavaScript thread;
- battery drain per hour and peak device temperature; whether Android throttles within 60 minutes;
- installed application size delta per candidate, and per-asset size for a 30-second loop;
- behaviour under battery saver and under an OS reduced-motion setting.

### Deliverable

`docs/backdrop-tech-spike.md` recording the measurements per candidate, the chosen technology with its rationale, the auto-degrade thresholds M38-04 will implement (frame-drop rate, thermal signal, battery-saver flag), the per-loop asset budget M38-03 will author against, and a go/no-go on the animated library.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the four measurable candidates has recorded numbers for latency, frame rate, battery, temperature and size delta; no candidate is dismissed without data (spec §31.4).
- [ ] p95 cue latency with the winning candidate is within measurement noise of the no-backdrop baseline and still meets §19.2.
- [ ] The winner's rendering is confirmed to run off the JavaScript thread, or the spike explains why a dropped backdrop frame still cannot delay a cue.
- [ ] Concrete auto-degrade thresholds are proposed as constants M38-04 can implement.
- [ ] A per-loop asset budget in megabytes is proposed for M38-03.
- [ ] The Expo SDK version is unchanged; any new native module is noted as requiring `npx expo prebuild` plus a dev-client rebuild (spec §11.2, CLAUDE.md rule 5).
- [ ] The two rejected packages above are recorded with their verdicts so the decision is not relitigated.
- [ ] A build / depend / vendor choice is recorded **per source kind** with its reasoning; any vendored code carries its upstream licence, source commit and a list of modifications.
- [ ] A go/no-go is recorded: if nothing clears the budget, the backdrop ships as `{ kind: 'gradient' }` only.
- [ ] Nothing measured or implemented reads audio, playback position or track metadata (D17, spec §31.1).

## Test plan
