- Measurement is the deliverable. Every run uses the same scripted punch stream from `SimulatedPunchSource` so latency comparisons are like-for-like, and each configuration is run three times with the median reported.
- Hardware: Lenovo TB125FU tablet, screen awake, mains disconnected for the battery runs.

## Non-goals

- Authoring the library (M38-03), the renderer component (M38-04), selection UI (M38-05), or wiring into the live screen (M38-06).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M32-01 (simulated punch source) and M32-08 (live screen) to measure against something realistic; M32-05 if it has already settled orientation and keep-awake.
- Unblocks: M38-02, M38-03, M38-04, M38-07.

## Notes

- The static gradient floor is not optional: spec §31.4 requires `{ kind: 'gradient' }` to work on every device regardless of which animated technology wins, because it is the terminal auto-degrade state.
- Prefer a technology that can express a slowly-drifting mesh gradient, since that is the cheapest way to cover several moods from one renderer without shipping video.
- On completion, comment with the measurement table, the chosen technology, and the proposed threshold and budget constants.

issues.title: Define BackdropTheme contracts, mood taxonomy, and the contrast scrim
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M38 (spec §31.2, §31.3, §31.5). The pure contracts for the backdrop system: the theme shape, the mood taxonomy, deterministic selection from a mood, and the scrim maths that guarantee foreground legibility. Everything visual in M38 imports from here, and because the scrim is a pure function the whole library becomes checkable in CI without rendering anything (M38-08). No React, no Expo.

## Design references

- Spec §31.2 — `BackdropTheme`, `BackdropMood`, `MotionIntensity`, the four `source` kinds, `peakLuminance`, `attribution`.
- Spec §31.3 — contrast floors: 4.5:1 for body text and metric values, 3:1 for large text, the round timer, cue tokens and the count badge.
- Spec §31.5 — selection is a recipe parameter; mood-level choices resolve through the deterministic seed.
- Spec §19.4 — contrast; §15.1 — domain purity. D17 — nothing here reads audio.

## Method

### Files

- `src/domain/presentation/BackdropTheme.ts` — contracts + mood taxonomy (new).
- `src/domain/presentation/backdropScrim.ts` — contrast and scrim maths (new).
- `src/domain/presentation/selectBackdrop.ts` — deterministic selection (new).
- `src/domain/presentation/__tests__/` — see Test plan (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
export type BackdropMood = 'calm' | 'focus' | 'gritty' | 'hype' | 'nocturne' | 'clinical'
export type MotionIntensity = 'still' | 'subtle' | 'active'

export interface MeshPoint { x: number; y: number; color: string }
export type BackdropSource =
  | { kind: 'gradient'; stops: string[] }
  | { kind: 'mesh'; points: MeshPoint[] }
  | { kind: 'lottie'; asset: string }
  | { kind: 'video'; asset: string }

export interface BackdropTheme {
  id: string; name: string; mood: BackdropMood
  source: BackdropSource
  motion: MotionIntensity
  loopDurationMs: number
  peakLuminance: number          // 0..1, measured at authoring time
  accent?: string
  attribution?: { author: string; license: string; url?: string }
}

/** What the athlete or recipe chose. */
export type BackdropChoice =
  | { kind: 'off' }
  | { kind: 'theme'; id: string }
  | { kind: 'mood'; mood: BackdropMood }

export function selectBackdrop(
  choice: BackdropChoice, library: readonly BackdropTheme[], seed: string,
): BackdropTheme | null

// --- scrim -----------------------------------------------------------------
export interface ContrastFloors { body: number; large: number }
export const CONTRAST_FLOORS: ContrastFloors            // { body: 4.5, large: 3 }

export function relativeLuminance(hex: string): number
export function contrastRatio(a: number, b: number): number
/** Smallest scrim opacity (0..1) that holds both floors, or null if unreachable. */
export function requiredScrimOpacity(
  theme: BackdropTheme, scrimColor: string, textColor: string, largeTextColor: string,
): number | null
/** Convenience: does this theme qualify for the library at all? */
export function isLegible(theme: BackdropTheme, palette: { scrim: string; text: string; large: string }): boolean
```

### Algorithm

1. **`relativeLuminance`** implements the standard sRGB relative-luminance formula (linearise each channel, then `0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B`); `contrastRatio` is `(L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05)` with the lighter value first.
2. **`requiredScrimOpacity`** composites the scrim colour over `peakLuminance` at increasing opacity and returns the smallest value at which **both** floors hold. It searches monotonically and returns `null` when even full opacity fails — a theme that can only be read behind an opaque scrim is not a backdrop, and M38-03 must reject it rather than ship it dimmed to invisibility.
3. **`selectBackdrop`** — `off` returns `null`; `theme` returns that id or `null` if absent; `mood` filters the library by mood and picks deterministically from the workout seed, so the same recipe and seed always yield the same backdrop. **Selection never consults a clock, a random source, or anything audio-related.**
4. **Invariants:** every function is pure and total; no `Date.now()`; no imports outside the domain.

### Data flow

M38-03's library is validated against `isLegible` at authoring time and in CI (M38-08). M38-04's renderer calls `requiredScrimOpacity` to size its scrim. M38-05 writes a `BackdropChoice` into the recipe; M38-06 resolves it with `selectBackdrop` using the workout's stored seed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `BackdropTheme`, `BackdropMood`, `MotionIntensity`, `BackdropSource` and `BackdropChoice` are exported exactly as above (spec §31.2).
- [ ] `CONTRAST_FLOORS` is `{ body: 4.5, large: 3 }` matching spec §31.3.
- [ ] `relativeLuminance` and `contrastRatio` are verified against known reference pairs (white on black = 21:1; identical colours = 1:1).
- [ ] `requiredScrimOpacity` returns the **smallest** opacity holding both floors, and `null` when unreachable at full opacity.
- [ ] `selectBackdrop` is deterministic: the same `(choice, library, seed)` returns the same theme across 100 repeat calls and across process restarts.
- [ ] `selectBackdrop({kind:'off'})` returns `null`, and an unknown theme id returns `null` rather than throwing.
- [ ] No function reads audio state, playback position, track metadata, a clock, or a random source (D17, spec §31.1).
- [ ] Zero imports from `react-native`, `expo-*`, `expo-sqlite` or `src/ble/**` (spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `backdropScrim.test.ts` — reference contrast pairs; a bright theme requiring a heavy scrim; a theme that is unreachable and returns `null`; monotonicity of the opacity search.
- `selectBackdrop.test.ts` — determinism across seeds; mood filtering; `off`; unknown id; empty library.

## Non-goals

- The library contents (M38-03), rendering (M38-04), the picker (M38-05), persistence (M38-05/M31-09).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M38-01 (confirms which `source` kinds are actually implementable before the union is fixed).
- Unblocks: M38-03, M38-04, M38-05, M38-06, M38-08.

## Notes

- `peakLuminance` is measured once at authoring time and stored in the manifest rather than computed at runtime; M38-03 owns how it is measured and must document the method.
- The scrim colour comes from `@/theme/colors` at the call site, not from this module, so the palette stays the single source of truth.
- On completion, comment with files added, the scrim search implementation chosen, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Author the bundled starter backdrop library with licensing record
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M38 (spec §31.6, §31.3). Authors the bundled starter backdrop library: one or two entries per mood, each measured for `peakLuminance`, each recorded with its author and licence, all validated against the legibility floor before they ship. This is the "library we can customize for different emotions/themes/ambiance" — the data behind the picker, and the thing a future session extends by adding manifest entries rather than touching rendering code.

## Design references

- Spec §31.6 — bundled with the application, no backend and no runtime fetch (§15.6); every entry records author, licence and source; the licence must permit redistribution inside a distributed application; user-supplied loops are out of scope for the first release.
- Spec §31.2 — the `BackdropTheme` shape and `peakLuminance`; §31.3 — the contrast floor a theme must clear to qualify.
- Spec §31.4 — `{ kind: 'gradient' }` is the guaranteed-available floor and the terminal auto-degrade state, so at least one gradient entry per mood is mandatory.
- D17 — moods describe the feel the athlete wants, never anything derived from music.

## Method

### Files

- `src/presentation/backdrops/backdropLibrary.ts` — the manifest, typed as `readonly BackdropTheme[]` (new).
- `src/presentation/backdrops/assets/` — loop assets for non-gradient entries (new).
- `src/presentation/backdrops/ATTRIBUTION.md` — author, licence, source URL and modification note per asset (new).
- `src/presentation/backdrops/__tests__/backdropLibrary.test.ts` — manifest validation (new; M38-08 extends).

### Interfaces

```ts
import type { BackdropTheme, BackdropMood } from '@domain/presentation/BackdropTheme'

export const BACKDROP_LIBRARY: readonly BackdropTheme[]
/** Every mood has at least one entry, and at least one of them is a gradient. */
export function backdropsForMood(mood: BackdropMood): readonly BackdropTheme[]
export const DEFAULT_BACKDROP_ID: string
```

### Content

One gradient entry per mood is mandatory; richer entries are added on top as the chosen technology (M38-01) allows.

| Mood | Intent |
|---|---|
| `calm` | warm-up, cooldown, active recovery — slow drift, low contrast movement |
| `focus` | technique rounds — near-static, minimal distraction |
| `gritty` | pressure rounds — darker, textured, heavier |
| `hype` | high-volume and final rounds — brighter, faster drift |
| `nocturne` | low-light training — deep and dim, the darkest entry |
| `clinical` | measurement and calibration work — flat, neutral, effectively still |

`DEFAULT_BACKDROP_ID` points at a `focus` gradient: the cheapest, least distracting option, so the default costs nothing and never competes with the cue stage.

### Authoring rules

1. **Measure `peakLuminance` rather than guess it.** Render the loop, sample the brightest region a foreground element can overlap across the whole loop period, and record the maximum. Document the procedure in `ATTRIBUTION.md` so later additions are measured the same way.
2. **Validate before shipping.** Every entry must satisfy `isLegible` (M38-02) against the app palette. An entry that only reads behind a near-opaque scrim is rejected and reworked, not dimmed into uselessness.
3. **Respect the asset budget** from M38-01. Prefer gradients and meshes over video; video is a last resort for photographic ambience.
4. **Licence discipline.** Only assets whose licence permits redistribution inside a distributed application. Record author, licence, source URL and whether the asset was modified. Anything ambiguous is not used.
5. **`motion` must be honest.** An entry labelled `subtle` may not animate like an `active` one; the auto-degrade ladder (M38-04) depends on these labels meaning what they say.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `BACKDROP_LIBRARY` is exported as `readonly BackdropTheme[]` and every entry typechecks against the M38-02 contract.
- [ ] Every `BackdropMood` has at least one entry, and at least one entry per mood is `{ kind: 'gradient' }` (spec §31.4 floor).
- [ ] Every entry passes `isLegible` against the app palette; a test iterates the whole manifest and fails on any that does not (spec §31.3).
- [ ] Every non-gradient entry has an `attribution` block with author, licence and source URL, and a matching row in `ATTRIBUTION.md` recording whether it was modified (spec §31.6).
- [ ] `peakLuminance` is a measured value and the measurement procedure is documented in `ATTRIBUTION.md`.
- [ ] Total asset size is within the M38-01 budget; the installed-size delta is recorded in the completion comment.
- [ ] `DEFAULT_BACKDROP_ID` resolves to an existing `focus` gradient entry.
- [ ] No asset is fetched at runtime and nothing here contacts a network (spec §15.6, §31.6).
- [ ] Mood names and descriptions carry no implication that the backdrop responds to music (D17).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `backdropLibrary.test.ts` — ids are unique; every mood covered; a gradient exists per mood; every entry legible; every non-gradient has attribution; `DEFAULT_BACKDROP_ID` resolves and is a gradient; `loopDurationMs` is positive and within a sane range.
- Visual check on the tablet: each entry rendered behind the live screen at its scrim opacity, confirming cue tokens and the timer read clearly.

## Non-goals

- Rendering (M38-04), the picker (M38-05), the legibility fixture suite itself (M38-08), user-supplied loops (out of scope for this release per spec §31.6).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M38-01 (asset budget and which source kinds are viable), M38-02 (`BackdropTheme`, `isLegible`).
- Unblocks: M38-04, M38-05, M38-08.

## Notes

- `react-native-expo-backgrounds` is MIT-licensed and its parallax starfield is a plausible `nocturne` entry if adapted as an authored asset — but it is rejected as a runtime dependency (see M38-01), and its gyroscope reactivity must be dropped: the tablet is mounted at the bag and would jitter on every impact.
- Keep the manifest data-only. Anything conditional belongs in the renderer, so adding a mood later is a pure data change.
- On completion, comment with the entries authored, the installed-size delta, and the licence of every bundled asset.

issues.title: Implement BackdropRenderer with motion levels and auto-degrade
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M38 (spec §31.3, §31.4). The renderer: one component that takes a `BackdropTheme`, draws its loop beneath the computed contrast scrim, and degrades itself under reduced motion, thermal pressure, battery saver or sustained frame drops without ever interrupting the workout. This is the only module that touches the rendering technology chosen in M38-01, so swapping that technology later means editing this file and nothing else.

## Design references

- Spec §31.4 — the backdrop is the lowest-priority consumer of the device; renders off the JavaScript thread where possible; auto-degrades `active` → `subtle` → `still` silently; reduced motion forces `still`; an explicit off switch always exists; `{ kind: 'gradient' }` is the guaranteed floor.
- Spec §31.3 — the scrim and its contrast floors; §19.2 — the latency budget a dropped backdrop frame must never threaten.
- Puncheokie doc §19 Backdrop, §25 (reduced motion, everything defeatable). D17 — nothing here observes audio.

## Method

### Files

- `src/presentation/backdrops/BackdropRenderer.tsx` — the component (new).
- `src/presentation/backdrops/useBackdropDegrade.ts` — degrade policy hook (new).
- `src/presentation/backdrops/__tests__/BackdropRenderer.test.tsx` (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
export interface BackdropRendererProps {
  theme: BackdropTheme | null        // null = off; renders nothing but the base background
  /** Caller-provided palette so the scrim matches the app theme. */
  palette: { scrim: string; text: string; large: string }
  /** Overrides the computed level; used by tests and by the settings preview. */
  forceMotion?: MotionIntensity
  reducedMotion?: boolean
  children: React.ReactNode
}
export function BackdropRenderer(p: BackdropRendererProps): React.ReactElement

export interface DegradeSignals {
  reducedMotion: boolean
  batterySaver: boolean
  thermalPressure: 'nominal' | 'fair' | 'serious'
  droppedFrameRate: number           // rolling 0..1
}
export function useBackdropDegrade(requested: MotionIntensity): MotionIntensity
export const DEGRADE_THRESHOLDS: { droppedFrameRate: number; sustainedMs: number }
```

### Behavior

1. **Composition.** Renders, back to front: the app background colour, the theme's loop, the scrim, then `children`. `children` is the entire live screen, so every foreground element sits above the scrim by construction and no caller can accidentally place UI beneath it.
2. **Scrim.** Opacity comes from `requiredScrimOpacity` (M38-02) for this theme and palette. If it returns `null` the renderer refuses the theme and falls back to the default gradient rather than shipping unreadable UI — a defensive path that M38-03's validation should already make unreachable.
3. **Degrade ladder.** `useBackdropDegrade` lowers the level one step at a time: `active` → `subtle` → `still`. Reduced motion or battery saver forces `still` immediately. Sustained dropped frames above `DEGRADE_THRESHOLDS.droppedFrameRate` for `sustainedMs` steps down once, then re-evaluates. **Degrading is silent and one-way within a session** — no oscillation, no toast, no interruption; recovery waits for the next session so the athlete never sees the backdrop pulsing between levels mid-round.
4. **`still`** renders a single representative frame, or the flat gradient for non-gradient sources. It costs nothing per frame.
5. **Off-thread.** Animation is driven by whatever mechanism M38-01 chose that keeps it off the JavaScript thread. **A dropped backdrop frame must never delay a cue, a timer tick, or a punch acknowledgement**, and the component holds no state the cue pipeline reads.
6. **No audio.** The loop advances on its own presentation clock. There is no input from playback, position, metadata or a microphone (D17).

### Data flow

M38-06 wraps the Puncheokie live screen in this component with the theme resolved by `selectBackdrop`. M38-05's picker renders it in a small preview with `forceMotion` so the athlete sees the real thing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `BackdropRenderer` composites background → loop → scrim → `children`, so foreground UI is always above the scrim (spec §31.3).
- [ ] Scrim opacity is taken from `requiredScrimOpacity` (M38-02); a `null` result falls back to the default gradient rather than rendering unreadable UI.
- [ ] `theme = null` renders children over the plain app background with no loop and no measurable cost.
- [ ] `reducedMotion` or battery saver forces `still` immediately (spec §31.4, doc §25).
- [ ] Sustained dropped frames step the level down exactly one notch and do not oscillate; a test drives the signals and asserts the ladder and the absence of oscillation.
- [ ] `still` renders a single frame or flat gradient and starts no animation loop.
- [ ] The component holds no state read by the cue pipeline, and a test asserts that forcing backdrop frame drops does not change cue timing in the simulated harness (spec §19.2, §31.4).
- [ ] Nothing in the component or hook reads audio, playback position, track metadata or the microphone (D17, spec §31.1).
- [ ] The renderer is the only module importing the chosen rendering library; a test or lint rule asserts no other file does.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `BackdropRenderer.test.tsx` — composition order; `null` theme; scrim opacity applied from the pure function; `null` opacity falls back; `forceMotion` honoured.
- `useBackdropDegrade` — table-driven over `DegradeSignals`: reduced motion, battery saver, each thermal level, dropped-frame rates above and below threshold, and a sequence asserting one-way stepping with no oscillation.
- Manual on the tablet: each motion level at each mood; confirm cue tokens stay readable and the workout is unaffected when the backdrop is forced to drop frames.

## Non-goals

- Choosing the technology (M38-01), the library (M38-03), selection UI (M38-05), live-screen wiring (M38-06), on-device measurement (M38-07).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M38-01 (technology + thresholds), M38-02 (`requiredScrimOpacity`, contracts), M38-03 (a library to render).
- Unblocks: M38-05, M38-06, M38-07.

## Notes

- Keep every conditional here rather than in the manifest, so adding a mood or an asset later stays a pure data change (M38-03).
- Use `@/theme/colors` at the call site for the palette; the renderer takes it as a prop so it never reaches into the theme module directly and stays testable.
- On completion, comment with files added, the degrade thresholds implemented, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Backdrop picker with mood browsing, live preview, and recipe persistence
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M38 (spec §31.5). The athlete's control over ambience: a picker that browses the library by mood, previews each entry live, and stores the choice on the workout recipe so it persists and reproduces. Mood-level choices resolve through the workout's existing deterministic seed, so "Run This Exact Workout Again" (M36-01) reproduces the same visuals as well as the same combinations.

## Design references

- Spec §31.5 — selection is a recipe parameter persisted in `workout_recipes.params_json`, stamped on the generated workout, and mood choices resolve through the seed.
- Spec §31.4 — the off switch is always available; §31.2 — `BackdropChoice` is `off` / `theme` / `mood`.
- Puncheokie doc §8 — the Recipe screen's progressive disclosure; §19 — settings are locked during work.
- D17 — the picker offers moods, never anything derived from a connected playlist.

## Method

### Files

- `src/components/workout/BackdropPicker.tsx` — mood tabs, entry grid, live preview, off switch (new).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/recipe.tsx` — surface the picker in the recipe flow (modify).
- `src/domain/workout/WorkoutRecipe.ts` — add `backdrop: BackdropChoice` with a default (modify).
- `src/state/useWorkoutStore.ts` — recipe slice carries the choice (modify).
- `src/components/workout/__tests__/BackdropPicker.test.tsx` (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
export interface BackdropPickerProps {
  value: BackdropChoice
  onChange: (next: BackdropChoice) => void
  library: readonly BackdropTheme[]
  seed: string                 // so a mood choice previews the theme it will actually pick
}
export function BackdropPicker(p: BackdropPickerProps): React.ReactElement

// WorkoutRecipe addition (M31-04 owns the surrounding type)
backdrop: BackdropChoice       // defaults to { kind: 'theme', id: DEFAULT_BACKDROP_ID }
```

### Behavior

1. **Browse by mood.** Moods are the top-level control, because the athlete is choosing a feel, not a file. Selecting a mood stores `{ kind: 'mood', mood }` and lets the engine resolve within it; drilling in and tapping a specific entry stores `{ kind: 'theme', id }`. Both are first-class, and the difference is explained in one line of copy.
2. **Preview honestly.** Each entry previews in a tile using the real `BackdropRenderer` (M38-04) at its real scrim opacity, with representative foreground elements — a cue token, the timer — composited on top. A preview that looks good but renders unreadably at full size is worse than no preview. A mood tile previews the entry `selectBackdrop` would actually choose for the current seed.
3. **Off is a peer, not a hidden setting.** "No backdrop" sits alongside the moods as an equally prominent choice (spec §31.4).
4. **Persistence.** The choice is a recipe parameter, so it saves with named presets, duplicates with them, and is stamped onto the generated workout. It is not a global app setting: different workouts can legitimately want different rooms.
5. **Reproducibility.** Because a mood resolves through the workout seed, replaying a stored workout yields the same backdrop. A test asserts this end to end.
6. **Locked during work.** The picker is unreachable while a session is in `work` (doc §19); it is available in the recipe flow and during rest or pause.
7. **Reduced motion.** When the OS reports reduced motion, previews render `still` and the screen says so, rather than silently showing something the workout will not deliver.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The picker offers every `BackdropMood`, a drill-in to specific entries, and an equally prominent "No backdrop" option (spec §31.4).
- [ ] Selecting a mood stores `{ kind: 'mood', mood }`; selecting an entry stores `{ kind: 'theme', id }`; "No backdrop" stores `{ kind: 'off' }`.
- [ ] Previews use the real `BackdropRenderer` at real scrim opacity with a cue token and timer composited on top (spec §31.3).
- [ ] A mood tile previews the entry `selectBackdrop` resolves for the current seed, not an arbitrary member of the mood.
- [ ] `WorkoutRecipe.backdrop` defaults to `{ kind: 'theme', id: DEFAULT_BACKDROP_ID }` and round-trips through save, duplicate and reload of a named preset (spec §31.5, M36-01).
- [ ] Replaying a stored workout resolves the same backdrop; a test asserts identical resolution for the same recipe and seed.
- [ ] The picker is unreachable while the session phase is `work` (doc §19).
- [ ] Under reduced motion, previews render `still` and the screen states that motion is reduced (doc §25).
- [ ] No control offers to derive a backdrop from a connected playlist, a track, or any audio property (D17, spec §31.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `BackdropPicker.test.tsx` — each choice kind is emitted correctly; the off option is present and reachable; mood preview matches `selectBackdrop` for the seed; reduced motion forces still previews; the picker is disabled during `work`.
- Store/persistence test — a recipe with a mood choice saved, duplicated, reloaded and replayed resolves the same theme.
- Manual on the tablet: browse every mood, pick one, run a workout, confirm the running backdrop matches the preview.

## Non-goals

- The renderer (M38-04), the library contents (M38-03), live-screen wiring (M38-06), user-supplied loops (out of scope, spec §31.6).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M38-02 (`BackdropChoice`, `selectBackdrop`), M38-03 (library to browse), M38-04 (renderer for previews), M31-04 (`WorkoutRecipe`), M31-06 (Recipe screen to host it).
- Unblocks: M38-06; feeds M36-01 (presets and exact replay).

## Notes

- Keep the mood-versus-entry distinction to one sentence of copy. Most athletes will pick a mood once and never open the drill-in.
- The choice belongs to the recipe, not to global settings — resist making it an app-wide preference, or exact replay stops being exact.
- On completion, comment with files added, the default choice shipped, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: Composite the Puncheokie live screen over the backdrop
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M38 (spec §31, Puncheokie doc §19 Backdrop). Puts the backdrop on screen: wraps the Puncheokie live workout in `BackdropRenderer`, resolves the recipe's choice through the workout seed, and proves the four zones still read cleanly over every entry in the library. This is the issue where the feature becomes visible, and the one that must demonstrate the legibility guarantee against real UI rather than a preview tile.

## Design references

- Puncheokie doc §19 — the four zones and their contents; the new Backdrop subsection.
- Spec §31.3 — cue tokens, round timer and count badge hold their contrast floor over every backdrop; §31.4 — degrade and off paths.
- Puncheokie doc §13 — the visual grammar that must read identically on the brightest and darkest loops; §28.3 — the affirmation border, which is the thinnest, most fragile element over a moving surface.
- D17 — the loop is independent of playback.

## Method

### Files

- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/live.tsx` — wrap the zone tree in `BackdropRenderer` (modify).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/useWorkoutRunner.ts` — resolve the theme once at session start (modify).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/summary.tsx` — carry the same backdrop into the summary for continuity (modify).
- `src/app/(tabs)/punchcraft/__tests__/liveBackdrop.test.tsx` (new).

### Interfaces

```ts
// resolved once, at session start, and held for the session
const theme = selectBackdrop(workout.recipe.backdrop, BACKDROP_LIBRARY, workout.seed)
// live.tsx
<BackdropRenderer theme={theme} palette={{ scrim: colors.background, text: colors.textPrimary, large: colors.textPrimary }}>
  <RoundTopBar … /> <CueStage … /> <MetricsRail … /> <Controls … />
</BackdropRenderer>
```

### Behavior

1. **Resolve once.** The theme is resolved at session start and held for the whole session. It never changes mid-workout — not on round change, not on mood, and certainly not on anything audio-related. A backdrop that shifted between rounds would pull attention exactly when the athlete needs it on the cue stage.
2. **Wrap the whole zone tree** so every zone sits above the scrim by construction; no zone renders its own background that would defeat it.
3. **Zones keep their own surfaces.** The top bar and metrics rail retain their existing surface colours so their content never floats directly on a moving loop; the cue stage is the only zone that reads primarily against the backdrop, and it is the one the contrast floor is sized for.
4. **Summary continuity.** The summary screen uses the same theme, so the workout ends in the room it ran in.
5. **Off and degrade pass through** untouched from M38-04; this issue adds no policy of its own.
6. **No layout change.** The four-zone geometry of doc §19 is unchanged — the backdrop sits behind it and nothing reflows.

### Verification against the whole library

A test renders the live screen over **every** entry in `BACKDROP_LIBRARY` and asserts each foreground element's computed contrast against the scrimmed backdrop clears its floor. This is the end-to-end counterpart to M38-08's manifest-level check: M38-08 proves the manifest is legible in principle, this proves the actual screen is legible in practice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The live screen's four zones render inside `BackdropRenderer` with the theme resolved from `recipe.backdrop` and the workout seed (spec §31.5).
- [ ] The theme is resolved once at session start and does not change for the duration of the session.
- [ ] A test renders the live screen over every entry in `BACKDROP_LIBRARY` and asserts cue tokens, round timer and count badge clear their contrast floors (spec §31.3).
- [ ] The affirmation border (doc §28.3) remains clearly visible at every fill fraction over the brightest entry in the library.
- [ ] The four-zone layout is byte-identical with the backdrop off; no reflow, no geometry change (doc §19).
- [ ] The summary screen renders the same theme as the session it summarises.
- [ ] With `{ kind: 'off' }` the screen renders exactly as it did before this issue.
- [ ] Nothing in the live path reads audio, playback position or track metadata (D17).
- [ ] Cue latency is unchanged with the heaviest backdrop running, verified in the simulated harness (spec §19.2, §31.4).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- `liveBackdrop.test.tsx` — library-wide contrast sweep over the real zone tree; off renders unchanged; theme resolution is stable across re-renders; layout identical with and without.
- Manual on the tablet: run a full workout on the brightest and the darkest entries; confirm the cue stage, the affirmation border and the count badge all read at arm's length under room lighting and under gym lighting.

## Non-goals

- The renderer or its degrade policy (M38-04), the picker (M38-05), on-device battery and thermal measurement (M38-07), the punchCraft live session (tracked on #113).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M38-02, M38-03, M38-04, M38-05 (a stored choice to resolve), M32-08 (the live screen), M33-04 (round transition) and M37-05 (affirmation border) for the contrast sweep to cover real foreground elements.
- Unblocks: M38-07.

## Notes

- The punchCraft mode's live session (#113, M21-02) should adopt the same wrapper when it is built; a coordination comment has been left there so the shared component is used rather than a second one written.
- If any library entry fails the sweep, fix the entry in M38-03 rather than lowering the floor here.
- On completion, comment with files added, screenshots over the brightest and darkest entries, and any deviation from the Interfaces block.

issues.title: On-device backdrop performance, endurance, and degrade verification
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M38 (spec §31.4, §19.2). Proves on the real device that the shipped backdrop costs what M38-01 predicted: that the cue pipeline is untouched, that a 60-minute session does not cook or flatten the tablet, and that auto-degrade fires when it should. M38-01 measured prototypes; this measures the finished feature with the real library behind the real live screen. Marked `hardware-required`: the Lenovo TB125FU is the only environment where this means anything.

## Design references

- Spec §31.4 — the backdrop is the lowest-priority consumer; auto-degrade thresholds; reduced motion; the always-available off switch.
- Spec §19.2 — the p95 latency budget the backdrop must not disturb; §19.1 — reliability targets; §11.11 — foreground, keep-awake, screen on for the whole session.
- Puncheokie doc §9 — the longest supported schedule is 60 minutes, which is the endurance case; §25 — never let presentation cost the athlete the workout.
- M38-01's recorded thresholds and asset budget, which this issue either confirms or sends back.

## Method

### Files

- `docs/backdrop-tech-spike.md` — append a "Shipped feature measurements" section (modify).
- `src/presentation/backdrops/BackdropRenderer.tsx` — only if a threshold needs retuning (modify).

### Protocol

Run on the tablet, screen awake, mains disconnected, with the simulated punch source driving a realistic stream so latency is measured against a known input (M32-01).

1. **Latency.** A 10-minute Puncheokie session with (a) no backdrop, (b) the cheapest gradient, (c) the heaviest `active` entry in the library. Record p50, p95 and p99 cue-to-render latency for each. Three runs per configuration, median reported.
2. **Endurance.** One full 60-minute schedule on the heaviest entry. Record battery percentage every 10 minutes, peak device temperature, whether Android throttles, and whether auto-degrade fires and at what elapsed time.
3. **Degrade.** Force each trigger and confirm the ladder: enable OS reduced motion, enable battery saver, and induce frame drops. Confirm each steps exactly one notch (or straight to `still` for reduced motion and battery saver), that it is silent, and that it does not oscillate.
4. **Off.** Confirm the workout is fully completable with the backdrop off and that no residual cost remains — no animation loop running, no sensor listener, no wake source.
5. **Size.** Record the installed application size with and without the backdrop assets.

### Pass criteria

- p95 latency with the heaviest backdrop is within measurement noise of the no-backdrop baseline **and** still meets the §19.2 budget.
- The 60-minute session completes without thermal throttling that degrades the cue pipeline, and battery drain is recorded and judged acceptable for a workout of that length.
- Every degrade trigger behaves as specified, silently and without oscillation.

If any pass criterion fails, the outcome is to retune the thresholds or drop the offending motion level from the library — **not** to relax the §19.2 budget.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] p50/p95/p99 cue latency recorded for no backdrop, cheapest gradient and heaviest entry, three runs each, median reported (spec §19.2).
- [ ] p95 with the heaviest backdrop is within noise of baseline and inside the §19.2 budget; if not, the failing motion level is removed or retuned and re-measured.
- [ ] A full 60-minute session is completed on the heaviest entry with battery every 10 minutes, peak temperature, and any throttling recorded (doc §9, spec §11.11).
- [ ] Reduced motion and battery saver each force `still` immediately; induced frame drops step down exactly one notch; no trigger oscillates (spec §31.4).
- [ ] With the backdrop off, no animation loop, sensor listener or extra wake source remains active; verified, not assumed.
- [ ] Installed-size delta from the backdrop assets is recorded against the M38-01 budget (spec §31.6).
- [ ] Final thresholds are committed as constants with the measurements that justify them cited in a comment.
- [ ] Measurements are appended to `docs/backdrop-tech-spike.md` so the numbers live with the decision.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- The measurement protocol above is the deliverable. Every latency comparison uses the identical scripted punch stream so the configurations are like-for-like.
- Hardware: Lenovo TB125FU, both trackers connected for at least one run so the measurement includes real BLE traffic rather than only simulated events.

## Non-goals

- Choosing the technology (M38-01), authoring entries (M38-03), the renderer's implementation (M38-04), the picker (M38-05).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M38-04, M38-06 (the feature must be wired into the live screen to measure it), M32-01 (scripted stream), M33-01 (real tracker stream for the mixed run).
- Unblocks: nothing — this is the gate that says the backdrop is fit to ship.

## Notes

- Run the endurance case last: it is the slowest and the most likely to send a threshold back for retuning.
- If the heaviest entry fails only on battery rather than latency, prefer demoting that entry's `motion` label in the library over weakening the degrade thresholds — the ladder protects every future entry, one label protects one.
- On completion, comment with the full measurement table, the final thresholds, and whether any library entry was demoted or removed.

issues.title: Legibility fixture tests across the whole backdrop library
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 5 / M38 (spec §31.3). The regression net for the legibility guarantee. Because the scrim is a pure function of a theme's measured `peakLuminance` and the palette (M38-02), the entire library can be proven readable in CI without rendering a pixel — and, critically, so can every entry a future session adds. Without this, the guarantee is a paragraph in a document; with it, adding an unreadable backdrop fails the build.

## Design references

- Spec §31.3 — contrast floors of 4.5:1 for body text and metric values and 3:1 for large text, the round timer, cue tokens and the count badge; a theme that cannot reach the floor is rejected from the library rather than shipped dim.
- Spec §31.2 — `peakLuminance` is the measured input; §31.6 — every entry carries attribution.
- Spec §21.1 — pure domain functions get unit tests; §21.2 — fixtures are deterministic and run headless.
- D17 — no test may introduce an audio dependency.

## Method

### Files

- `src/presentation/backdrops/__tests__/legibility.test.ts` — the library sweep (new).
- `src/domain/presentation/__tests__/fixtures/scrim-cases.json` — hand-built boundary cases (new).
- `src/presentation/backdrops/__tests__/manifest.test.ts` — manifest integrity (new; extends M38-03's basic checks).

### Interfaces

```ts
interface ScrimCase {
  name: string
  peakLuminance: number
  palette: { scrim: string; text: string; large: string }
  expect: { opacity: number | null; bodyRatio: number; largeRatio: number }
}
```

### Coverage

**Library sweep** — for every entry in `BACKDROP_LIBRARY`, at its computed scrim opacity, assert the body and large floors both hold. The failure message names the entry and reports both achieved ratios, so a contributor who adds a too-bright loop sees exactly which floor it missed and by how much.

**Boundary fixtures** — hand-built cases the library may not currently contain, so the maths stays pinned independently of the shipped content:

1. `pure-black` — `peakLuminance: 0`, needs no scrim; asserts opacity 0 and a very high ratio.
2. `pure-white` — `peakLuminance: 1` against the dark palette; asserts a heavy but achievable opacity.
3. `unreachable` — a palette whose text colour cannot clear the floor at any opacity; asserts `null` rather than a bad value or a throw.
4. `exactly-at-floor` — tuned to land on 4.5:1; asserts the boundary is treated as passing, not failing.
5. `just-below-floor` — asserts it is treated as failing, so the comparison is not silently inclusive.
6. `large-passes-body-fails` — a case where the 3:1 element clears but the 4.5:1 element does not; asserts the stricter floor governs the returned opacity.

**Manifest integrity** — ids unique; every mood covered; at least one gradient per mood (the §31.4 floor); `DEFAULT_BACKDROP_ID` resolves to a gradient; every non-gradient entry has complete `attribution`; `peakLuminance` within 0..1; `loopDurationMs` positive and within a sane range.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every entry in `BACKDROP_LIBRARY` is asserted against both contrast floors at its computed scrim opacity (spec §31.3).
- [ ] A failing entry's message names the entry and reports the achieved body and large ratios against the required floors.
- [ ] All six boundary fixtures exist and pass, including `unreachable` returning `null` and the two floor-boundary cases behaving strictly.
- [ ] `large-passes-body-fails` proves the stricter floor governs the chosen opacity.
- [ ] Manifest integrity is asserted: unique ids, every mood covered, a gradient per mood, `DEFAULT_BACKDROP_ID` resolves to a gradient, complete attribution on non-gradient entries, `peakLuminance` in range.
- [ ] The suite runs headless in CI with no device, no Expo module and no network (spec §21.2).
- [ ] Adding a deliberately over-bright entry to the library makes the suite fail; demonstrated once and then reverted.
- [ ] No test imports audio, playback state or a rendering library (D17, spec §15.1).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `node tools/guards/velocity-terminology.mjs` pass.

## Test plan

- The suite is the deliverable and must be deterministic: fixtures carry explicit values, nothing samples a clock or a random source, and re-running produces identical output (spec §21.2).
- Pair with the end-to-end sweep in M38-06, which checks the real zone tree rather than the manifest. This issue proves the library is legible in principle; that one proves the screen is legible in practice. Both should fail if a bad entry lands.

## Non-goals

- Authoring library entries (M38-03), rendering behaviour (M38-04), on-device measurement (M38-07).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: M38-02 (`requiredScrimOpacity`, `isLegible`, `CONTRAST_FLOORS`), M38-03 (a library to sweep).
- Unblocks: nothing directly; it guards M38-03 and every future addition to the library.

## Notes

- Keep the boundary fixtures independent of the shipped library on purpose: the maths must stay pinned even if every current entry is replaced.
- When M38-07 demotes or removes an entry, this suite is the fastest confirmation that the manifest is still internally consistent.
- On completion, comment with files added, the fixtures authored, and the demonstration that an over-bright entry fails the build.

epic.title: [EPIC] Phase 6 — Spotify playlist connection
epic.body:
## Objectives

- Authorize one personal Spotify account via OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE.
- Retrieve and select playlists the user is permitted to access under Development Mode.
- Open selected content in the installed Spotify Android app via deep link.
- Keep workout timing fully independent of Spotify playback state.

## Milestones

- M27 — Spotify PKCE authorization & secure tokens
- M28 — Playlist selection, caching & deep link

## Definition of done

An allowlisted user can connect Spotify, choose an accessible playlist, open it in the Spotify app, return to Puncheokie, and run a program without Spotify controlling the workout clock. Tokens live only in `expo-secure-store` (§20.3); no client secret exists anywhere in the repo (§14.2); Puncheokie runs correctly with Spotify disconnected or failing (§14.3, §14.6); UI tolerates followed non-owned playlists whose metadata is visible but whose items are unavailable (§14.3); 401/403/429 handling matches §14.8; tokens are redacted from logs and diagnostic exports (§20.3, §20.4); the Spotify policy gate (§14.6) has been reviewed and documented prior to any public distribution.

## Non-goals

- Embedded audio streaming, Web Playback SDK, or App Remote SDK integration.
- Beat detection, audio-feature analysis, or song-synchronized cue choreography.
- Playback-control scopes (`user-modify-playback-state`, etc.) or Premium-gated player endpoints.
- Downloading, caching, or transforming Spotify audio content or artwork.
- Any workflow that couples the Puncheokie timer to Spotify player state.

## Sub-issues

GitHub auto-populates this list from issues linked to the epic — do not maintain by hand.

issues.title: Register Spotify developer app and configure Android redirect URI
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 6 (§14.2, §14.3, §22 Phase 6 tasks 1–2) requires a registered Spotify developer app owned by a Premium account, with the exact redirect URI and Android package information Expo AuthSession will use. Because Development Mode caps the app at five allowlisted users (§14.3), the allowlist and metadata must be recorded so future contributors can extend or migrate it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Spotify developer app is created under an owner-controlled Premium account.
- [ ] Redirect URI matches the Expo AuthSession scheme used by the app (documented in `docs/spotify-setup.md`).
- [ ] Android package name is registered in the Spotify dashboard.
- [ ] Allowlist (≤5 users) is recorded in `docs/spotify-setup.md` with instructions for adding/removing testers.
- [ ] Only `playlist-read-private` (plus `playlist-read-collaborative` if enabled) scopes are declared; no playback scopes.
- [ ] No client secret is committed to the repository; `.env.example` documents only the public client ID.

## Non-goals

- Applying for Extended Quota Mode.
- Requesting playback-control scopes.
- Publishing the app publicly.

## Notes

See §14.2, §14.3, references R13–R17. Client ID may be committed as a public identifier; secret must never be. This issue is `policy-review` because it is the first artifact where Spotify TOS acceptance and quota mode are chosen.

issues.title: Implement Authorization Code with PKCE via Expo AuthSession
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 6 §14.2 requires OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE using Expo AuthSession because mobile clients cannot safely hold a client secret. This task delivers the end-to-end sign-in plumbing: PKCE code verifier/challenge generation, browser handoff, redirect capture, and code-for-token exchange, with only the minimum scopes. The user-facing connect/disconnect narrative lives in M27-05.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/spotify/SpotifyAuth.ts` exposes `signIn()`, `signOut()`, and `getAccessToken()` and contains no client secret.
- [ ] PKCE code verifier is generated with a cryptographically secure RNG and the S256 challenge method is used.
- [ ] Only `playlist-read-private` (and optionally `playlist-read-collaborative`) are requested.
- [ ] Successful sign-in returns access token, refresh token, expiry, granted scopes, and Spotify account id.
- [ ] The domain layer (`src/domain/**`) does not import Expo, RN, or AuthSession (§15.1).
- [ ] User-visible errors distinguish user-cancelled, network, and Spotify-side failures.

## Non-goals

- Persisting tokens (covered in M27-03).
- Playlist fetching (M28-01).
- Playback control.

## Notes

See §14.2, §15.1, §16 (`src/spotify/`). References R13–R14. Follows the component boundaries in §11.4/§15.1 — Spotify code lives outside domain.

issues.title: Persist Spotify tokens in expo-secure-store with refresh and redaction
issues.body:
## Context

Per §14.2, §20.3, and §20.4, Spotify access token, refresh token, expiry, granted scopes, and Spotify account id must live in `expo-secure-store` — never SQLite, AsyncStorage, MMKV, log files, or diagnostic exports. This task adds the SecureStore-backed token repository, the single-shot refresh path used by higher-level clients, redaction hooks that scrub tokens from any log or export path, and a full erase on disconnect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/spotify/SpotifyTokenStore.ts` reads/writes tokens exclusively via `expo-secure-store`.
- [ ] Refresh-token exchange runs when the access token is expired or after a 401 (see M27-04).
- [ ] A grep of the repository confirms no Spotify token, refresh token, or client secret is written to SQLite, AsyncStorage, MMKV, or logs.
- [ ] All logger call sites route Spotify auth values through a redaction helper that replaces access/refresh tokens, PKCE verifiers, and `Authorization` headers with a fixed sentinel; diagnostic export bundles (§20.4) run the same scrubber before being written.
- [ ] `eraseAllTokens()` deletes access token, refresh token, expiry, granted scopes, and Spotify account id from SecureStore in a single call and is invoked by Disconnect (M27-05).
- [ ] Signing out clears all Spotify keys from SecureStore.
- [ ] Unit tests cover expiry math, refresh success, refresh failure (invalid_grant → forced re-auth), log-redaction of tokens, and erase-on-disconnect leaving no Spotify keys behind.

## Non-goals

- Encrypting SQLite (out of scope for MVP).
- Handling 403/429 (M27-04).

## Notes

See §14.2, §20.3, §20.4, reference R15. Depends on M27-02. Files per §16: `src/spotify/SpotifyTokenStore.ts`.

issues.title: Spotify HTTP client with 401/403/429 handling and backoff
issues.body:
## Context

§14.8 requires the Spotify client to refresh once on 401, treat 403 as missing allowlist/scope/access (not generic network failure), and honor `Retry-After` with exponential backoff on 429. This task centralizes that behavior in a single fetch wrapper used by all Spotify API calls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/spotify/SpotifyClient.ts` wraps `fetch` and injects the current access token.
- [ ] On 401, the client refreshes the token exactly once and retries the original request; a second 401 surfaces as an auth error requiring re-sign-in.
- [ ] On 403, the client raises a typed `SpotifyAccessError` distinct from network errors, carrying the response body for diagnosis.
- [ ] On 429, the client waits for `Retry-After` seconds (falling back to exponential backoff with jitter, capped) and retries up to a bounded number of attempts.
- [ ] Missing/optional response fields introduced by Development Mode restrictions do not throw (§14.8).
- [ ] Unit tests simulate 401→refresh→success, 401→refresh→401, 403, and 429 with `Retry-After`.

## Non-goals

- Full offline queueing of playlist requests.
- Metrics/telemetry export.

## Notes

See §14.8. Depends on M27-03. Files per §16: `src/spotify/SpotifyClient.ts`.

issues.title: Spotify connection settings screen: connect, status, and disconnect
issues.body:
## Context

Users must be able to see whether Spotify is connected, which account is connected, and disconnect at any time (§14.7, §14.8). Disconnect must erase tokens from SecureStore and cached Spotify data from SQLite. Puncheokie must continue to work when disconnected (§14.3, §14.6).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Settings screen shows connection status, connected Spotify account id/display name, and granted scopes.
- [ ] `Connect` triggers the PKCE flow from M27-02.
- [ ] `Disconnect` calls `eraseAllTokens()` from M27-03 (clearing access token, refresh token, expiry, granted scopes, and account id from SecureStore) and clears all rows from Spotify cache tables (see M28-03).
- [ ] After Disconnect, entering Puncheokie shows a clear message that Spotify is optional and allows a workout to run without it.
- [ ] All copy uses punchCraft terminology; no references to "impact speed", "force", "power", "energy", or "punch strength" (§4.3); tracker readings are described as "tracker-reported velocity".

## Non-goals

- Multi-account support.
- Re-authorizing scopes without full sign-out.

## Notes

See §14.3, §14.6, §14.7, §14.8. Files per §16: `src/features/settings/SpotifyConnectionScreen.tsx`.

issues.title: Fetch and paginate the current user's playlists
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 6 §22 task 7 and §14.8 require paginating the current-user playlists endpoint and tolerating fields that may be missing or restricted under Development Mode. This story delivers the playlist list used by the selection UI (M28-06).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/spotify/SpotifyPlaylistApi.ts` exposes `listCurrentUserPlaylists()` returning all pages.
- [ ] Pagination follows the `next` cursor and stops cleanly when `next` is null.
- [ ] Missing optional fields (owner display name, snapshot id, etc.) do not throw.
- [ ] Requests go through the M27-04 client so 401/403/429 handling is inherited.
- [ ] Unit tests cover a single-page response, a multi-page response, and a page with missing optional fields.

## Non-goals

- Search across all Spotify catalog playlists.
- Fetching playlist tracks (M28-02).

## Notes

See §14.8, §22 Phase 6. Depends on M27-04. Files per §16: `src/spotify/SpotifyPlaylistApi.ts`.

issues.title: Tolerate followed non-owned playlists with unavailable items
issues.body:
## Context

Spotify's February 2026 Development Mode change (§14.3) restricts playlist contents for playlists the user does not own or collaborate on: metadata remains visible but items are unavailable. The playlist selection UI must render these playlists as selectable-for-deep-link with a clear indicator that item enumeration is unavailable — not as a generic error. §14.3 makes this a mandatory UI behavior, so it is a P0 gate for M28.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When items endpoint returns empty/forbidden for a followed non-owned playlist, the playlist card renders with a `Items unavailable in Development Mode` note and still exposes deep-link (M28-04) as an action.
- [ ] Owned and collaborative playlists render full item counts.
- [ ] 403 on items is treated as a Development Mode restriction (`SpotifyAccessError`), not a crash.
- [ ] Unit tests cover owned, collaborative, and followed-non-owned playlist branches.

## Non-goals

- Attempting to enumerate items via unsupported endpoints.
- Requesting scopes beyond the current minimum set.

## Notes

See §14.3, §14.8, references R16–R17. Depends on M28-01. Raised to P0 because §14.3 makes tolerance of this restriction a mandatory MVP UI behavior.

issues.title: Cache selected playlist metadata in SQLite (tokens excluded)
issues.body:
## Context

Per §14.7, SQLite may cache Spotify account id, playlist id, URI, name, owner display name, snapshot id, item count, selected state, and last-sync time. Tokens stay in SecureStore. This task adds the schema and repository, with a data-erase path used by Disconnect (M27-05).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration creates `spotify_playlist_cache` with columns matching §14.7 (no token columns).
- [ ] Repository writes/reads playlist metadata and marks exactly one playlist as `selected`.
- [ ] `eraseSpotifyCache()` deletes all rows and is invoked by Disconnect.
- [ ] Artwork URLs are not stored in the MVP (§14.7).
- [ ] Domain layer imports no SQLite (§15.1); repository lives under `src/storage/`.
- [ ] Unit tests cover selection replacement and erase.

## Non-goals

- Storing playlist track lists.
- Storing artwork bytes.

## Notes

See §14.7, §15.1, §17. Files per §16: `src/storage/SpotifyPlaylistRepository.ts`, migration under `src/storage/migrations/`. Area is `spotify` because the cached data is Spotify-domain metadata, even though the storage medium is SQLite.

issues.title: Deep-link into the Spotify Android app for playback
issues.body:
## Context

Per §14.4 and §22 Phase 6 task 10, MVP playback is a content deep link into the installed Spotify Android app. The user starts playback in Spotify, returns to punchCraft, and Puncheokie runs on its own independent timer (§14.6). No embedded streaming, no player-state polling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `openPlaylistInSpotify(uri)` opens the installed Spotify app to the selected playlist URI.
- [ ] When Spotify is not installed, a clear fallback message is shown and Puncheokie can still start without Spotify.
- [ ] Returning to punchCraft does not reset or pause the Puncheokie session timer (§14.6).
- [ ] No code path polls Spotify player state.
- [ ] Manual test recorded in `docs/qa/spotify-deep-link.md` covers install-present and install-absent branches.

## Non-goals

- Spotify App Remote SDK or Web API playback control (§14.5).
- Beat/tempo synchronization.

## Notes

See §14.4, §14.6, reference R18. Depends on M28-03. Files per §16: `src/spotify/SpotifyDeepLink.ts`.

issues.title: Spotify policy review checklist for public distribution
issues.body:
## Context

§14.6 forbids public distribution until the Spotify Developer Policy has been reviewed against the intended Puncheokie behavior (synchronization risk, background listening framing, no audio overlay by default). §22 Phase 6 task 12 requires this review before enabling public distribution. This task delivers the written checklist and records the current decision, and is a go/no-go gate for any future public release.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/spotify-policy-review.md` enumerates each §14.6 constraint with a Pass/Fail/Deferred entry and a link to the code or design decision that supports it.
- [ ] Checklist explicitly confirms: workout timeline independent of track timing; no song-specific choreography; no audio analysis; no app-generated audio overlaid on Spotify by default; clear metadata/workout data separation.
- [ ] Reviewer and date recorded; a re-review is required before any public distribution.
- [ ] Any items marked Deferred link to a follow-up issue.

## Non-goals

- Obtaining formal Spotify approval.
- Legal opinion beyond a documented internal review.

## Notes

See §14.6, references R21–R22. Marked `policy-review` and `go-no-go` because a Fail on any §14.6 item blocks public distribution.

issues.title: Playlist picker screen for selecting the active workout playlist
issues.body:
## Context

The M28 roadmap DoD and §14.4 step 3 call for a user-facing playlist picker: the screen where a signed-in user browses their fetched playlists (M28-01), sees which are fully available vs. items-unavailable under Development Mode (M28-02), marks one as the active selection persisted in the SQLite cache (M28-03), and hands off to the Spotify deep link (M28-04). This story owns that screen as a distinct issue instead of folding the UI into the API/cache tasks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/features/settings/SpotifyPlaylistPickerScreen.tsx` lists all playlists returned by `listCurrentUserPlaylists()` with owner display name, item count when available, and an `Items unavailable in Development Mode` indicator per M28-02.
- [ ] Selecting a playlist writes it as the single `selected` row via the M28-03 repository and reflects the change on return to the screen.
- [ ] A `Play in Spotify` action on the selected row invokes `openPlaylistInSpotify(uri)` from M28-04.
- [ ] When Spotify is disconnected, the screen shows a Connect prompt (routing to M27-05) and does not attempt API calls.
- [ ] Pagination, empty-state (no playlists), and error-state (network / `SpotifyAccessError`) branches are all rendered without crashing and do not block Puncheokie from starting without Spotify (§14.6).
- [ ] Offline / API-unreachable path (§14.8): the picker falls back to cached rows from `spotify_playlist_cache` (M28-03) and still allows selecting and deep-linking the previously selected playlist, with a visible "cached" indicator on affected rows; automated test covers the offline-cache selection flow.
- [ ] Copy uses punchCraft terminology per §4.3 — no "impact speed / force / power / energy / punch strength" language.

## Non-goals

- Search across the full Spotify catalog.
- Multi-playlist selection or queueing.
- In-app playback controls (§14.5).

## Notes

See §14.3, §14.4 step 3, §14.6, §14.7. Depends on M28-01, M28-02, M28-03, M28-04. Files per §16: `src/features/settings/SpotifyPlaylistPickerScreen.tsx`.

epic.title: [EPIC] Phase 7 — Hardening and release preparation
epic.body:
## Objectives

- Prove reliability of a fully connected build under sustained load (§19.1, §21.6).
- Land the retention, privacy, safety, accessibility, and disclosure surface required before an external MVP build (§17.2, §19.4, §19.5, §20).
- Make the build reproducible and shippable: dependency lock, SBOM, release signing, backup APK, user documentation.
- Resolve open policy questions (Spotify §14.6, crash reporting) before the release gate.
- Pass the release gate defined in §21.6 as the single blocking checklist for M30.

## Milestones

- M29 — Endurance, reliability & storage retention
- M30 — Release readiness

## Definition of done

- One-hour field session completes without crash (§21.6).
- Counts match a manually reviewed reference within the agreed tolerance.
- Every displayed velocity has a clear unit/source label (tracker-reported velocity, calibrated, or normalized per §4.3).
- Data persists across app restart.
- Spotify failure does not block a non-Spotify workout.
- Raw-capture export/replay works on Windows.
- Retention defaults (30-day diagnostic + pin-capture + storage usage in Settings) are shipped per §17.2.
- Logging classification (safe / device-sensitive / secret) is enforced; secrets are never logged (§20.4).
- Accessibility, landscape/tablet, safety, and privacy disclosures are in place.
- Signed release build with reproducible dependency lock and SBOM exists.
- Spotify policy/legal decision (§14.6) is recorded before M30 closes.

## Non-goals

- No new metric surfaces, protocol fields, or Puncheokie programs.
- No backend, account system, or cloud sync.
- No Play Store submission automation; this phase produces the signed artifact and documentation, not a store listing.
- No paid Spotify SDK integration work beyond the policy/legal decision.

## Sub-issues

GitHub auto-populates the sub-issue list below from linked issues.

issues.title: Execute one-hour endurance session and record reliability metrics
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 7 / M29. The release gate in §21.6 requires a one-hour field session that completes without crash, with all reliability targets in §19.1 met on the physical Android tablet with both trackers. This task executes and evidences that run. Touches §19.1, §19.2, §19.3, §21.3, §21.6.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One continuous session of at least 60 minutes runs on the tablet with both trackers connected.
- [ ] Zero app crashes during the run.
- [ ] Zero database constraint failures logged.
- [ ] Zero knowingly duplicated accepted events (per §18.2).
- [ ] All incoming frames are stored, or an explicit storage-overrun error is recorded (§12.4).
- [ ] A simulated single-tracker disconnect during the run does not stop the other tracker.
- [ ] Session timer remains monotonic across the entire run (§18.3).
- [ ] Final metrics can be regenerated from stored events after app restart.
- [ ] p95 native-callback-to-UI latency is measured and recorded; target <=250 ms (§19.2).
- [ ] Reliability report attached to the issue with tablet model, Android version, dependency versions, and raw-capture export.

## Non-goals

- Not the controlled-punch acceptance test (M29-05).
- No new metrics or UI added during the run.

## Notes

Produces evidence for release-gate item in §21.6. Requires physical tablet and both trackers (§21.3). Store the raw capture per §12.4 and export via existing diagnostic export.

issues.title: Implement 30-day retention cleanup with pin-capture exemption
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 7 / M29. §17.2 sets the retention policy: session events and referenced calibration captures are kept indefinitely; general raw diagnostic captures are cleaned up after 30 days or a user-configured storage ceiling; users may 'pin' a capture to exempt it from cleanup. Implement the cleanup job and pin flag in the storage layer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Raw diagnostic captures older than 30 days are deleted on a scheduled sweep (default; user-configurable).
- [ ] A `pinned` flag on capture rows exempts a capture from cleanup regardless of age.
- [ ] Session punch events and captures referenced by a calibration profile are never cleaned up.
- [ ] User-configured storage ceiling triggers oldest-first cleanup of unpinned diagnostic captures when exceeded.
- [ ] Cleanup runs on app start and on a periodic timer while foregrounded; each run logs counts of items considered/deleted (safe log fields only).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: pinned excluded, referenced-by-calibration excluded, age boundary, ceiling boundary.
- [ ] Domain code performing the eligibility computation has no RN/Expo/SQLite imports (§15.1).

## Non-goals

- No cloud backup; storage stays local (§15.6).
- No UI beyond wiring a `pin` toggle already needed by M29-03.

## Notes

See §16 for storage module placement (`src/storage/*`). Retention rules live in a pure domain module callable from the storage repository.

issues.title: Add Settings storage-usage display and retention controls
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 7 / M29. §17.2 requires Settings to show estimated storage usage and let the user configure the retention ceiling; pin/unpin must be accessible from a capture. Ships the UI over the cleanup engine landed in M29-02.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Settings screen shows estimated storage used, broken down by: session events, calibration-referenced captures, diagnostic captures (pinned vs unpinned).
- [ ] User can set the retention age (default 30 days) and a storage ceiling; changes trigger a cleanup sweep.
- [ ] Capture detail view exposes a pin/unpin toggle that updates the `pinned` flag from M29-02.
- [ ] A 'Delete all unpinned diagnostic captures' action is present with a destructive-confirm dialog (§19.4).
- [ ] Storage figures refresh on returning to the Settings screen and after a cleanup sweep.
- [ ] Copy uses tracker-reported velocity vocabulary where relevant; no 'force/power/impact speed' terms (§4.3).

## Non-goals

- No export UI changes here.
- No cloud storage indicators.

## Notes

Related: M29-02 (cleanup engine), M30-06 (safety/privacy disclosures may cross-link to Settings). See §16 for Settings screen location.

issues.title: Enforce logging field classification (safe / device-sensitive / secret)
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 7 / M29. §20.4 requires structured logs to classify fields as safe, device-sensitive, or secret; secret fields are never logged and device-sensitive fields are redacted from normal support exports. This task lands the classification helper, redaction policy, and lint/tests that keep it honest across the logging pipeline.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A logging helper accepts field entries tagged `safe` | `device-sensitive` | `secret`; secret fields are dropped before serialization.
- [ ] Standard support export includes only `safe` fields; a user-enabled 'diagnostic detail' toggle additionally includes `device-sensitive` fields.
- [ ] Spotify access/refresh tokens, PKCE code verifiers, and any auth material are classified `secret` (§20.3).
- [ ] BLE MAC / device identifier / firmware values are classified `device-sensitive` (§20.2).
- [ ] Unit tests assert secret fields never appear in serialized log output regardless of caller mistake.
- [ ] A lint or grep-based CI check flags direct `console.log` / raw logger use in modules that handle tokens or device identifiers.
- [ ] Helper module lives under the app/infra layer per §16; domain code does not import it directly (§15.1).

## Non-goals

- No new log sinks or remote log shipping.
- No crash-reporter integration (M30-10).

## Notes

See §16 for a logging module location. Domain layer must not import RN/Expo (§15.1); the helper is a pure module used by adapters. Retagged from qa-docs to infra because this is code-level enforcement across the logging pipeline, not documentation.

issues.title: Execute controlled-punch protocol test suite on hardware
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 7 / M29. §21.4 lists the controlled-punch scenarios that qualify a build for the release gate. This task runs the full protocol on the tablet with both trackers and records evidence for each case.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No-motion false-positive test recorded; zero accepted events over the observation window.
- [ ] 1 left, 1 right; 5 left; 5 right; 10 alternating sequences each executed and counts match observation.
- [ ] Slow / normal / fast sets executed; tracker-reported velocity distributions recorded (§4.3 vocabulary).
- [ ] Rapid combination sequence recorded.
- [ ] Strike during rest and strike during pause both correctly excluded from work-interval metrics (§18.2).
- [ ] Disconnect / reconnect with a known punch count recovered per §19.3.
- [ ] Regular vs switch stance sequence recorded.
- [ ] Tracker placement variation recorded.
- [ ] Each case has a persisted raw capture and a reviewer sign-off note attached to the issue.

## Non-goals

- Not the one-hour endurance run (M29-01).
- No changes to the decoder in response to findings; file separate issues if defects surface.

## Notes

Requires physical trackers and tablet (§21.3, §21.4). Raw captures persisted per §12.4 into `src/storage/*`; export via existing diagnostic path.

issues.title: Complete release-gate checklist per §21.6
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 7 / M30. §21.6 defines the six gate criteria that any build must satisfy before being called an MVP. This is the single blocking checklist issue for M30; it must pass before M30 closes. It links out to the evidence issues rather than duplicating their work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One-hour field session completes without crash (evidence: M29-01).
- [ ] Counts match a manually reviewed reference within the agreed tolerance (evidence: M29-05).
- [ ] Every displayed velocity has a clear unit/source label — tracker-reported, calibrated, or normalized (§4.3).
- [ ] Data persists across app restart (evidence linked from M29-01 restart step).
- [ ] Spotify failure does not block a non-Spotify workout; verified with Spotify disconnected on the tablet.
- [ ] Raw-capture export/replay works on Windows using the current export format (§12.7) — evidence: M30-11.
- [ ] All six items above are ticked with links to the evidence issue / capture / commit before this issue is closed.

## Non-goals

- Not a re-run of every test issue; this issue aggregates evidence.
- Not the Play Store submission.

## Notes

Blocks M30 close. Related: M29-01, M29-05, M30-02, M30-06, M30-09, M30-11.

issues.title: Add in-app safety and privacy disclosures
issues.body:
## Context

Phase 7 / M30. §19.5 requires explicit safety language and §20 requires data-handling disclosures. Ship a Safety & Privacy screen (or grouped Settings sections) that presents the required statements before the release gate, and land the raw-capture export warning surface and the anonymized-export option that accompanies the new 30-day retention.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Safety copy states that tracker metrics are training estimates.
- [ ] Safety copy states that velocity is not equivalent to force or injury risk (§4.3, §19.5).
- [ ] Safety copy states that the app does not assess concussion or medical condition.

- [ ] Privacy section lists what data is stored locally and what is not requested (§20.1).

Use tracker-reported velocity vocabulary throughout (§4.3). Related: M30-09 Spotify decision may alter Spotify-related copy; M29-02/M29-03 retention surface links here. Area kept as qa-docs because the enum has no `ui`/`app` slug; the UI screens still live under the standard screen path in §16.

epic.title: [EPIC] Phase 8 — Puncheoke instrument (Note Cube + PunchBridge)
epic.body:
## Objectives

- Fork Puncheoke into a standalone punch-driven instrument under the PunchEoke tab: a two-handed sample-and-hold latched-voice instrument with elastic pitch bends (design authority: docs/puncheoke/instrument-design.md + docs/puncheoke/note-cube-design.md).
- Governing rule: pitch set chooses the notes; cube topology assigns them to hands and velocity zones; harmony policy resolves two-hand combinations; the four-route patch matrix changes the sound without redefining the notes; Z changes density, never latched pitches.
- Tablet compiles semantic gestures (single-mapping doctrine, patchHash-validated); PunchBridge renders MIDI for Studio One; instrument math is pure domain code.
- Milestone 1 = the decisive test: Two-Handed Pentatonic, each hand latching and bending only its own voice, no stuck notes ever.

## Status at filing

P1 (M40-01) and P2 (M40-02) shipped on branch puncheoke/instrument; P3 in progress this session.

issues.body:

Puncheoke P1 (instrument-design §24). The 9-byte punch record's peak-acceleration u16 (bytes 1-2 LE) was parsed and discarded by the decoder; the instrument needs it as its articulation axis.

- [x] `TrackerPunchEvent.accelerationRaw` populated by FightCampV1Decoder (golden pins 272/189/112/100)

issues.title: PunchBridge: WS gesture wire, MIDI backend abstraction, tablet client

issues.title: Note Cube domain model: pitch sets, topologies, harmony, cube compiler
issues.body:
## Context

Puncheoke P3 (note-cube-design §3-§10). Pure domain: PunchPatch (root x pitch set x topology x harmony x registers x transition x 4 mod routes) compiled once into a zoneCount² CompiledCubeMap consumed identically by MIDI, cube, and clouds. patchHash via mapHashOf.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pitchSets.ts` launch bank (min/maj pentatonic, minor blues, dorian-six, mixolydian-six, power lattice; cents internally)
- [ ] `punchPatch.ts` schema + 5 launch patches (Two-Handed Pentatonic default)

- [ ] `zoneQuantizer.ts` (4/5/6 zones, hysteresis), `latchedVoice.ts`, `activityEnvelope.ts` (Z never moves latched pitch), `transitions.ts`, `gestureCompiler.ts` (recovered refused; deterministic with injected now)
- [ ] Jest: compiler determinism + 36-cell snapshot, topology math, soft-guard tritone→fifth, hysteresis, latch no-stack

issues.title: Jam screen + bridge transition rendering — the decisive two-voice test
issues.body:
## Context

Puncheoke P4. The playable milestone: jam screen under the PunchEoke tab (six-row selector: KEY / PITCH SET / CUBE LAYOUT / HARMONY / REGISTERS / TRANSITION), keepalive punch feed, bridge with pitch-bend transition ramps + InstrumentProfile CC mapping. issues.title: Tracker sensitivity floor: probe config chars + modes for a lower transmit threshold
issues.body:
## Context

Soft punches produce NO frame at all: the firmware punch-detection threshold is set by init command 17 (vendor log “Set new Threshold to 30”) and the write carries no argument — the value is firmware-fixed. Kyle’s jam feedback (2026-09-05): low-velocity play needs feedback. High-sensitivity scaling now covers detected punches; this spike hunts a lever for the floor itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] READ ca281074/75/76 on both trackers (safe reads first) and document contents; correlate with threshold behavior
- [ ] Candidate writes tested on ONE tracker only (cradle-reset recovery plan; wrong-length-write clock-scramble precedent respected)
- [ ] Modes 2 (Gym), 4 (Test), 5 (Normal Kick) probed for different detection floors
- [ ] Verdict: achievable sensitivity range, or documented dead end

issues.title: Whammy + formant + Ampire wah — the deferred expression backends
issues.body:
## Context

transition-design.md ships the first implementation (legato glide + elastic ornament + synth-filter wah). Deferred expression work: Whammy Rise/Dive (full-octave bends on PEAK events only, 200-500ms), Punch Scoop (-1..-2 semitones into center), formant wah (Mai Tai Talky/Voxil, second CC to Character Sound), and the Ampire Pedalboard wah backend (requires Studio One >= 4.6 + Ampire license; Control Link mapping).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Whammy transition preset: scoop on hard punches, octave rise only on a new-peak event
- [ ] PitchTransitionProfile / WahTransitionProfile shapes from transition-design §4 in the profile schema
- [ ] Formant backend prototype (CC -> Character Sound) behind a profile flag
- [ ] Ampire backend documented/gated on the installed Studio One version
